chapters.title: Unit 1: Simplicity and Humility of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW)

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the mind-map and predict what the lesson is about. (Mind-map words: truthful, trustworthy, forgiving, tolerant, honest, courageous, loyal, patient, just)
    Ans: The mind-map shows the noble qualities of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) - truthful, trustworthy, forgiving, tolerant, honest, courageous, loyal, patient and just. The lesson is therefore about his character, especially his simplicity and humility, and how he lived a simple, humble life and treated everyone kindly and equally.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. What is meant by simplicity and humility?
    Ans: Simplicity means living a plain and unadorned life, without show, luxury or waste, and being content with simple food, dress and living. Humility means being humble and modest, not proud or arrogant, and never making others feel small, unwanted or embarrassed. The lesson says simplicity in life is part of faith.
  • Q: 2. Describe in a few sentences, the life style of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) in the light of the text that you have read.
    Ans: Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) lived a very simple and hard life in lifestyle, diet and manners. He never saw bread made from fine flour, his mattress was made of leather stuffed with the fibre of date tree, and when he died he left neither money nor anything else except his white riding mule, his arms and a piece of land left to charity. He milked his goat, mended his clothes, repaired his shoes and helped with household work, although the Muslim treasury was at his disposal.
  • Q: 3. How can simplicity and humility do away with the culture of extravagance and waste?
    Ans: If we adopt the sunnah of simplicity and humility, we stop squandering our hard-earned resources on unwanted luxurious items to satisfy pride and superiority. Simplicity teaches contentment with real needs, so extravagance and waste end. It also removes social evils like ostentation, haughtiness, arrogance and pride, and makes our social behaviour considerate and genuine.
  • Q: 4. Read the last paragraph of the lesson, "Simplicity and humility of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW)" with comprehension and write down the main idea and supporting details of the paragraph.
    Ans: Main idea: By adopting the sunnah of simplicity and humility we can improve our lifestyle and remove social evils, and live a genuinely happy life. Supporting details: Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) was endowed with impeccable qualities; simplicity and humility can eradicate ostentation, haughtiness, arrogance and pride; at present we squander resources on luxuries to gratify pride; if simplicity and humility become part of our personality, our behaviour will be considerate and genuine, our happiness unadulterated, and we will bow our heads in humility and affection instead of holding them high in pride.
  • Q: 5. How did Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) treat his foster sister?
    Ans: His foster sister was given similar treatment to his wet nurse. He stood up to receive the wet nurse who had reared him in infancy and would spread his own sheet for her, and his foster sister received the same respect and honour.

Comprehension B. Choose the correct option for the following statements

  • Q: 1. The mattress on which Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) slept was made of leather, stuffed with the fibre of date tree. This shows that he (SAW) __________.
    Options: was poor / led a simple life / could not purchase expensive mattress / was prominent
    Ans: led a simple life
  • Q: 2. The word that is opposite in meaning to affluent is __________.
    Options: rich / beautiful / well-mannered / poor
    Ans: poor
  • Q: 3. According to the text Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) and Hazrat Fatima (RA) greeted each other __________ way.
    Options: in the same / in the different / in a simple / in an affluent
    Ans: in the same
  • Q: 4. The word closest in meaning to impoverished is __________.
    Options: without money / without good manners / having money / having good health
    Ans: without money
  • Q: 5. According to the text of the lesson Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) used to milk his goat, this shows that __________.
    Options: the Rasool (SAW) liked the milk of goats / the Rasool (SAW) did not like milking of goat by other people / humility was essential part of the Rasool's (SAW) character / the Rasool (SAW) had no servants
    Ans: humility was essential part of the Rasool's (SAW) character

mcqs.q: 1. The mattress on which Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) slept was made of leather, stuffed with the fibre of date tree. This shows that he (SAW) __________.
mcqs.why: The lesson presents the rough leather mattress stuffed with date-tree fibre as proof of the Prophet's (SAW) simple living, not of poverty or inability to buy better.

mcqs.q: 2. The word that is opposite in meaning to affluent is __________.
mcqs.why: Affluent means rich and wealthy, so its opposite is poor. Beautiful and well-mannered describe appearance and behaviour, not wealth.

mcqs.q: 3. According to the text Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) and Hazrat Fatima (RA) greeted each other __________ way.
mcqs.why: The text says Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) and Hazrat Fatima (RA) greeted each other in the same way, showing equality and humility in their meeting.

mcqs.q: 4. The word closest in meaning to impoverished is __________.
mcqs.why: Impoverished means having no money or being very poor, so 'without money' is closest in meaning to it.

mcqs.q: 5. According to the text of the lesson Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) used to milk his goat, this shows that __________.
options: humility was essential part of the Rasool's (SAW) character
the Rasool (SAW) liked the milk of goats
the Rasool (SAW) did not like milking of goat by other people
mcqs.why: Milking his own goat, though he had help available, shows that humility was an essential part of the Rasool's (SAW) character, as the lesson stresses.

mcqs.q: What is meant by simplicity in the lesson?
options: Spending freely on luxuries to impress other people
Living a plain and unadorned life, without show, luxury or waste
Being proud and arrogant in front of other people
Making others feel small, unwanted or embarrassed
mcqs.why: The lesson defines simplicity as a plain, unadorned life with contentment in simple food, dress and living, free of show and waste.

mcqs.q: When Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) died, what did he leave behind besides his white riding mule and his arms?
options: A large sum of money kept in the treasury
A palace furnished with costly furniture
A piece of land left to charity
Stores of fine flour and rich food
mcqs.why: The text says he left neither money nor anything else except his white riding mule, his arms and a piece of land left to charity.

mcqs.q: How did Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) receive the wet nurse who had reared him in infancy?
options: He sent a servant to receive her at the door
He gave her money and sent her away quickly
He met her only on special public occasions
He stood up to receive her and spread his own sheet for her
mcqs.why: The lesson says he stood up to receive his wet nurse and spread his own sheet for her, and his foster sister received the same respect.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, simplicity in life is part of __________.
mcqs.why: The lesson states clearly that simplicity in life is part of faith, which is why the Prophet (SAW) lived simply despite his high status.

mcqs.q: Which quality is named in the pre-reading mind-map of the lesson?
mcqs.why: The mind-map lists truthful, trustworthy, forgiving, tolerant, honest, courageous, loyal, patient and just as his noble qualities.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: Use dictionaries to locate guide words, locate entry word, choose appropriate word definition and identify pronunciation through pronunciation key, for the word: prominent
    Ans: Entry word: prominent. Part of speech: adjective. Pronunciation: /'prominant/ (PROM-i-nuhnt). Definition (as used in the lesson, e.g. a prominent place): important, famous, or easily seen / standing out. In a dictionary it is found on the page whose guide words cover words alphabetically around 'prominent'; the entry word is the bold word 'prominent' itself.
  • Q: Use dictionaries to locate guide words, locate entry word, choose appropriate word definition and identify pronunciation through pronunciation key, for the word: slaughter
    Ans: Entry word: slaughter. Part of speech: verb / noun. Pronunciation: /'slo:ta(r)/ (SLAW-ter). Definition (as used in the lesson, to slaughter a sheep): to kill an animal for food. The entry word 'slaughter' is located with the help of the guide words at the top of its dictionary page.
  • Q: Use dictionaries to locate guide words, locate entry word, choose appropriate word definition and identify pronunciation through pronunciation key, for the word: humility
    Ans: Entry word: humility. Part of speech: noun (uncountable). Pronunciation: /hju:'milati/ (hyoo-MIL-i-tee). Definition: the quality of being humble; modesty and a lack of pride. It is the key quality described throughout the lesson.
  • Q: Use dictionaries to locate guide words, locate entry word, choose appropriate word definition and identify pronunciation through pronunciation key, for the word: humbleness
    Ans: Entry word: humbleness. Part of speech: noun (uncountable). Pronunciation: /'hamblnas/ (HUM-bul-ness). Definition: the quality of being humble; humility, modesty. It is a synonym of humility.
  • Q: Use dictionaries to locate guide words, locate entry word, choose appropriate word definition and identify pronunciation through pronunciation key, for the word: dignitary
    Ans: Entry word: dignitary. Part of speech: noun (plural: dignitaries). Pronunciation: /'dignitari/ (DIG-ni-tree). Definition (as used in the lesson): a person who has an important official position; an important person. The lesson says Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) would himself stand up when any dignitary came to him.
  • Q: Use dictionaries to locate guide words, locate entry word, choose appropriate word definition and identify pronunciation through pronunciation key, for the word: foster
    Ans: Entry word: foster. Part of speech: adjective / verb. Pronunciation: /'fosta(r)/ (FOS-ter). Definition (as used in the lesson, foster sister / foster mother): used for a child, sister or parent related by fostering, that is, looked after by someone who is not the natural parent. His foster sister was the daughter of the wet nurse who reared him.

Grammar A. Choose the correct option for each sentence

  • Q: 1. "Success" is an example of __________.
    Options: countable noun / uncountable noun / abstract noun / material noun
    Ans: abstract noun
  • Q: 2. "Sugar" is an example of __________.
    Options: countable noun / uncountable noun / abstract noun / collective noun
    Ans: uncountable noun
  • Q: 3. "Honey" is an example of __________.
    Options: countable noun / uncountable noun / abstract noun / collective noun
    Ans: uncountable noun
  • Q: 4. "Bravery" is an example of __________.
    Options: countable noun / uncountable noun / abstract noun / material noun
    Ans: abstract noun
  • Q: 5. "Tables" is an example of __________.
    Options: countable noun / uncountable noun / abstract noun / collective noun
    Ans: countable noun

Grammar B. Write the correct plural of the nouns in parenthesis

  • Q: These ____ (person) are protesting against the president.
    Ans: persons (also accepted: people)
  • Q: The ____ (woman) over there want to meet the manager.
    Ans: women
  • Q: My ____ (child) hate eating pasta.
    Ans: children
  • Q: The ____ (student) are doing the exercise right now.
    Ans: students
  • Q: The ____ (fish) I bought is in the fridge.
    Ans: fish
  • Q: Where did you put the ____ (knife) which were on the shelf?
    Ans: knives
  • Q: Where did you put the knives which were on the ____ (shelf)?
    Ans: shelves
  • Q: ____ (Piano) are expensive.
    Ans: Pianos
  • Q: These ____ (phenomenon) are not fully understood.
    Ans: phenomena

Grammar C. Some nouns change meaning in the plural form. Use both the singular and plural nouns below in sentences to show difference in meaning

  • Q: good - goods
    Ans: Good (singular, noun/adjective sense of benefit/virtue): We should always do good to others. Goods (plural, merchandise): The shopkeeper displayed his goods in the window.
  • Q: wood - woods
    Ans: Wood (singular, timber/material): This table is made of wood. Woods (plural, forest): We went for a walk in the woods.
  • Q: spectacle - spectacles
    Ans: Spectacle (singular, a grand sight): The fireworks were a wonderful spectacle. Spectacles (plural, glasses): My grandfather wears spectacles for reading.
  • Q: character - characters
    Ans: Character (singular, moral quality/personality): He is a man of strong character. Characters (plural, persons in a story/play): Ali and Gul are the main characters of 'The Champions'.
  • Q: manner - manners
    Ans: Manner (singular, way of doing something): He solved the problem in a clever manner. Manners (plural, polite behaviour): Good manners make a person loved by all.
  • Q: force - forces
    Ans: Force (singular, strength/power): The force of the wind broke the tree. Forces (plural, army/troops): The armed forces defend the country.

Grammar D. Identify the noun phrases in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. He wished to talk to his manager.
    Ans: Noun phrases: 'his manager' (object of the preposition 'to'). 'He' is a pronoun, not a noun phrase.
  • Q: 2. The wicked man loves getting poor people into trouble.
    Ans: Noun phrases: 'The wicked man' (subject) and 'poor people' (object of 'getting').
  • Q: 3. The poor man wanted to pay back every penny he owed.
    Ans: Noun phrases: 'The poor man' (subject) and 'every penny he owed' (object).
  • Q: 4. All the kids were sleeping.
    Ans: Noun phrase: 'All the kids' (subject).
  • Q: 5. Horses prefer living in dark stables.
    Ans: Noun phrases: 'Horses' (subject, a single-word noun phrase) and 'dark stables' (object of the preposition 'in').

Grammar E. Complete each sentence with a properly formed noun clause

  • Q: 1. Jamal asked me __________?
    Options: where was his wallet / where his wallet was
    Ans: where his wallet was
  • Q: 2. I couldn't tell him __________.
    Options: where was I / where I was
    Ans: where I was
  • Q: 3. I don't know __________.
    Options: how many children he has / how many children does he have
    Ans: how many children he has
  • Q: 4. __________ is not important.
    Options: How close we are / How close are we
    Ans: How close we are
  • Q: 5. __________ was sad.
    Options: What did she say / What she said
    Ans: What she said

mcqs.q: 1. "Success" is an example of __________.
mcqs.why: Success names an abstract idea that cannot be touched or counted, so it is an abstract noun, not a countable, material or ordinary uncountable noun.

mcqs.q: 2. "Sugar" is an example of __________.
mcqs.why: Sugar cannot be counted as separate units in its normal use, so it is an uncountable noun in the book's classification exercise.

mcqs.q: 3. "Honey" is an example of __________.
mcqs.why: Honey, like sugar, is used as an uncountable mass noun, so the book classifies it as an uncountable noun.

mcqs.q: 4. "Bravery" is an example of __________.
mcqs.why: Bravery names a quality that exists in the mind, so it is an abstract noun rather than a countable or material noun.

mcqs.q: 5. "Tables" is an example of __________.
mcqs.why: Tables can be counted one by one — one table, two tables — so 'Tables' is an example of a countable noun.

mcqs.q: 1. Jamal asked me __________?
mcqs.why: A noun clause after 'asked me' uses statement word order, subject before verb: 'where his wallet was', not question order 'where was his wallet'.

mcqs.q: 2. I couldn't tell him __________.
mcqs.why: In the noun clause the subject 'I' must come before the verb 'was', giving 'where I was'; 'where was I' keeps direct-question order, which is wrong here.

options: how many children does he have
mcqs.why: The noun clause needs statement order without the auxiliary 'does': 'how many children he has' is correct, while 'does he have' is question order.

mcqs.q: 4. __________ is not important.
mcqs.why: As the subject of the sentence the noun clause must use statement order, 'How close we are'; 'How close are we' is a direct question form.
The noun clause acting as subject uses statement order, 'What she said'; 'What did she say' is the direct-question form and cannot fill this slot.

mcqs.q: What is the correct plural of 'woman' in the sentence 'The ____ over there want to meet the manager'?
mcqs.why: Woman is an irregular noun whose plural is 'women', as given in the solved plural exercise in this lesson.

mcqs.q: What is the correct plural of 'knife' in 'Where did you put the ____ which were on the shelf?'
mcqs.why: Nouns ending in -fe change the f to v and add -es in the plural, so knife becomes knives, as the solved exercise shows.

mcqs.q: In the plural, 'goods' means __________.
options: acts of virtue and benefit done for others
merchandise displayed or kept for sale
a grand and wonderful public sight
mcqs.why: Grammar C shows that 'goods' in the plural means merchandise — the shopkeeper displayed his goods — while singular 'good' means benefit or virtue.

mcqs.q: In 'The wicked man loves getting poor people into trouble', the noun phrase that is the subject is __________.
mcqs.why: The solved exercise identifies 'The wicked man' as the subject noun phrase and 'poor people' as the object of 'getting'.

mcqs.q: As used in the lesson, a 'dignitary' is __________.
options: a person who has an important official position
a child looked after by someone who is not the natural parent
the quality of being humble and modest
a person who kills an animal for food
mcqs.why: The vocabulary section defines a dignitary as a person with an important official position; the lesson says the Prophet (SAW) stood up when any dignitary came.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Write a unified paragraph

  • Q: A. Write a unified paragraph on topic sentence, 'pride makes us artificial and humility makes us real' by using specific words, vivid verbs, modifier and adequate supporting details to develop the main idea.
    Ans: Pride makes us artificial and humility makes us real. A proud person dresses, speaks and spends only to impress others, squandering hard-earned money on unwanted luxuries and wearing a false smile that hides an empty heart. He brags, looks down upon the poor and feels embarrassed to do his own work. In contrast, a humble person lives simply, speaks gently and helps others without show, just as Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) milked his goat, mended his clothes and sat wherever a place was available. Such a person is loved by everyone because his behaviour is considerate and genuine. Truly, pride builds a shining mask, while humility reveals the real, happy human being.

Writing B. Write a brief summary

  • Q: B. Write a brief summary of the lesson, "Simplicity and humility of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW)".
    Ans: The lesson describes the simplicity and humility that were ingrained traits of Hazrat Muhammad (SAW). He never made anyone feel small, sat wherever a place was available, wore nothing that could distinguish him from his companions and met the affluent and the impoverished alike. He ate simple food, slept on a leather mattress stuffed with date-tree fibre, milked his goat, mended his clothes and shoes, visited the sick and helped his companions dig a trench. He greeted others first, stood up for his wet nurse and foster sister and for Hazrat Fatima (RA), and refused to be privileged even in collecting firewood. The lesson ends by urging us to adopt his sunnah of simplicity and humility to remove ostentation, arrogance and waste from our lives.

mcqs.q: What is the topic sentence of the model unified paragraph in Writing A?
options: Pride makes us artificial and humility makes us real
Simplicity in life is part of faith
The Prophet (SAW) lived a very simple life
We should greet others before they greet us
mcqs.why: Writing A asks for a unified paragraph built on exactly this topic sentence, and every supporting detail in the model develops this contrast.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph, a proud person squanders his hard-earned money on __________.
options: books and education for his children
unwanted luxuries bought only to impress others
charity for the poor of his town
mcqs.why: The paragraph says a proud person dresses, speaks and spends only to impress others, squandering hard-earned money on unwanted luxuries.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph, what does pride build, while humility reveals the real human being?
mcqs.why: The paragraph ends: pride builds a shining mask, while humility reveals the real, happy human being — the false smile is only one detail of the mask.

mcqs.q: According to the brief summary in Writing B, Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) sat __________.
options: only on a raised seat of honour
on a leather mattress at all gatherings
mcqs.why: The summary says he never made anyone feel small and sat wherever a place was available, wearing nothing that distinguished him from his companions.

mcqs.q: According to the summary, Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) met __________ alike.
options: only the affluent and the dignitaries
only the poor and the sick
mcqs.why: The summary states that he met the affluent and the impoverished alike, without distinction, which is a key sign of his humility.

mcqs.q: In the summary, which task did Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) refuse to be privileged in?
mcqs.why: The summary lists many humble acts, but the refusal to be privileged is specifically tied to collecting firewood with his companions.

mcqs.q: According to the summary, the lesson ends by urging us to adopt his sunnah in order to remove __________ from our lives.
mcqs.why: The summary closes by urging adoption of his sunnah of simplicity and humility to remove ostentation, arrogance and waste from our lives.

mcqs.q: Which humble act is NOT mentioned in the Writing B summary?
options: He milked his goat and mended his clothes
He helped his companions dig a trench
He built a large house for his family
mcqs.why: The summary mentions milking his goat, mending clothes and shoes, visiting the sick and digging a trench — it never mentions building a large house.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph, the humble person is loved by everyone because his behaviour is __________.
mcqs.why: The paragraph says such a person is loved by everyone because his behaviour is considerate and genuine, unlike the proud person's show.

mcqs.q: The Writing A paragraph develops its main idea with supporting details about the humble person. Which detail belongs to the humble person?
options: He brags and looks down upon the poor
He feels embarrassed to do his own work
He helps others without show, as the Prophet (SAW) milked his goat and mended his clothes
He wears a false smile that hides an empty heart
mcqs.why: The other three details describe the proud person; helping without show, like milking his goat and mending his clothes, describes the humble person.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking A. Group presentation

  • Q: A. Create a group presentation on how we can adopt the sunnah of simplicity and humility. Present your point clearly and support your opinion with reasons.
    Ans: Model presentation: Assalam-o-Alaikum. Our group believes we can adopt the sunnah of simplicity and humility in daily life. First, we should be content with simple food, dress and living and avoid wasting money on showy luxuries, because simplicity is part of faith. Second, we should do our own work - clean our rooms, polish our shoes and help at home - as the Rasool (SAW) did. Third, we should greet others first, listen to them fully, visit the sick and treat rich and poor alike, without distinction of caste, creed or colour. If we practise these habits, pride and arrogance will leave us, our behaviour will become considerate and genuine, and our society will become happier. Thank you.

chapters.title: Unit 2: The Champions (Adapted from Amigo Brothers by Piri Thomas)

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the picture and guess what the story is about.
    Ans: The picture shows two young boxers wearing gloves and head-guards facing each other, ready to fight. The story is therefore about boxing - two young friends who are boxers and who have to fight each other in a championship, and how their friendship survives the fight.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. What is the significance of the title "The Champions"?
    Ans: The title is significant because both Ahmad Ali and Gul Sher are champions, not only in boxing but also in friendship and sportsmanship. At the end they leave the ring arm in arm before the winner is announced, because they knew they would always be champions to each other. The title therefore celebrates both of them, not a single winner.
  • Q: 2. What was the dream of Ahmad Ali and Gul Sher?
    Ans: Each youngster had a dream of someday becoming a lightweight boxing champion of the world. To achieve this cherished dream they strove hard day and night, running along the River Lyari at sunrise and attending the boxing club daily without any break.
  • Q: 3. Why was the fight so important for both Ali and Gul Sher?
    Ans: The fight was the final of the National Boxing Championship, and the winner was to represent the country (Pakistan) in the World Lightweight Boxing Championship. It was the gateway to their life-long dream of becoming world champion, there could be no draw, and only one of them could win, so it was the most important fight of their lives.
  • Q: 4. How did the two friends fight? Describe in your own words in five sentences.
    Ans: The two friends fought bravely, honestly and without holding back for three rounds. In Round One, Gul's piston-like left jabs snapped Ali's head back, while Ali trapped Gul against the ropes and poured punishing rights and lefts into his midsection. In Round Two, Ali rushed like a bull, but Gul's crushing blow unbalanced him, and then Ali's short right turned Gul's legs to jelly. In Round Three, both pounded away toe-to-toe, neither giving an inch and neither falling, until Ali's left eye was tightly closed and blood poured from Gul's nose. Even after the final bell they kept fighting until the referee and trainers pried them apart, after which they embraced each other.
  • Q: 5. Compare and contrast the characters of Ali and Gul.
    Ans: Both Ali and Gul are Grade Ten classmates from Lyari, equally good boxers, best friends like brothers, and both dream of becoming world lightweight champion. In contrast, Gul Sher was fair, lean and lanky, with hair always falling over his eyes, and his family had moved from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Karachi before his birth; his lean form and long reach made him the better boxer. Ahmad Ali was Sheedi, dark, short and husky, with black hair in a natural Afro style; his short, muscular frame made him the better slugger.
  • Q: 6. Is there any conflict in the story? If yes, describe it in detail.
    Ans: Yes, the central conflict is between friendship and ambition. Ali and Gul, bosom friends who felt themselves to be brothers, are selected to fight each other in the final, where only one can win and there is no draw. Each wants to win fair and square, yet each lies awake at night pulling punches and trying not to hurt the other, and a wall seems to rise between them. This inner conflict - duty to their dream versus love for their friend - is resolved when they fight fully and honestly, yet leave the ring together as friends.
  • Q: 7. What was the effect of the fight on the relationship of the two friends?
    Ans: The fight did not harm their relationship; it strengthened it. After the savage three rounds they rushed toward each other and embraced, and then left the ring arm in arm before the decision was announced. They proved that their friendship was greater than winning or losing.
  • Q: 8. Keeping in view the relationship of the two friends, is it easier or harder for them to fight each other? Support your answer by giving references from the text.
    Ans: It was harder for them to fight each other because they were like brothers. The text says they sensed that a wall was rising between them, Ali had a restless and fitful sleep thinking about the fight, and Gul passed heavy time on his rooftop wondering how the fight would affect his relationship with Ali. Gul confessed, 'I've been awake at nights, pulling punches on you, trying not to hurt you,' and Ali replied, 'Same here.' Yet once in the ring, Gul's hard punches dispelled Ali's doubt that friendship would affect their fight.
  • Q: 9. Are you satisfied with the ending? Support your response with cogent arguments.
    Ans: Yes, I am fully satisfied with the ending. The announcer is left alone because the champions have already left the ring arm in arm, which shows that friendship is more valuable than a title or trophy. Both fought honestly and neither was disgraced, so declaring one winner would have spoiled the moral of the story. The ending teaches true sportsmanship: compete with full strength, but never let competition destroy love and brotherhood.

Comprehension B. Choose the correct option for the following statements

  • Q: 1. Gul's lean form and long reach made him better boxer. This statement means that Gul was a better boxer because __________.
    Options: he was short, big with long arms / he was tall, skinny with long arms / he was short, skinny with long arms / he was high, well-built with short arms
    Ans: he was tall, skinny with long arms
  • Q: 2. "Ali was dark, short and husky". In this sentence the phrase "short and husky" means:
    Options: huge and muscular / thick and strong / small and well-built / a powerful and huge
    Ans: thick and strong
  • Q: 3. They both sensed that a wall was rising between them. This statement means:
    Options: they were climbing higher on the wall of fame. / communication gap was increasing between them. / they were getting closer to each other. / they were not happy about their fight.
    Ans: communication gap was increasing between them.
  • Q: 4. They could not win the contest because __________.
    Options: they were not good boxers. / they were afraid of each other. / they realised that boxing is not a good sport. / friendship was greater than winning fight.
    Ans: friendship was greater than winning fight.
  • Q: 5. Ali had restless and fitful sleep on the night before the fight because __________.
    Options: he had quarrelled with Gul Sher / he was challenged by Gul Sher / he had fallen ill on that particular night / he was disturbed about the effects of the forthcoming fight on their friendship
    Ans: he was disturbed about the effects of the forthcoming fight on their friendship

mcqs.q: 1. Gul's lean form and long reach made him better boxer. This statement means that Gul was a better boxer because __________.
options: he was tall, skinny with long arms
he was short, big with long arms
he was short, skinny with long arms
he was high, well-built with short arms
mcqs.why: Lean means tall and skinny, and a long reach comes from long arms, so Gul was a better boxer because he was tall and skinny with long arms.

mcqs.q: 2. "Ali was dark, short and husky". In this sentence the phrase "short and husky" means:
mcqs.why: Husky describes a thick, strong build, so 'short and husky' means thick and strong rather than huge or merely small and well-built.

mcqs.q: 3. They both sensed that a wall was rising between them. This statement means:
options: they were climbing higher on the wall of fame.
they were getting closer to each other.
communication gap was increasing between them.
they were not happy about their fight.
mcqs.why: A wall rising between close friends is an idiom for a growing communication gap and distance, not a real wall or growing fame.

mcqs.q: 4. They could not win the contest because __________.
options: they were afraid of each other.
they realised that boxing is not a good sport.
friendship was greater than winning fight.
mcqs.why: The book's key gives friendship as the reason: for both boys, friendship was greater than winning the fight, so the contest itself could not truly be won.

mcqs.q: 5. Ali had restless and fitful sleep on the night before the fight because __________.
options: he was disturbed about the effects of the forthcoming fight on their friendship
he had quarrelled with Gul Sher
he was challenged by Gul Sher
he had fallen ill on that particular night
mcqs.why: Ali's restless, fitful sleep came from worry about how the forthcoming fight would affect his friendship with Gul, as the text describes in detail.

mcqs.q: What was the shared dream of Ahmad Ali and Gul Sher?
options: To become heavyweight champion of their city
To become lightweight boxing champion of the world
To open a boxing club in Lyari together
To represent their school in a local contest
mcqs.why: The text says each youngster dreamed of someday becoming lightweight boxing champion of the world and strove day and night for it.

mcqs.q: The winner of the National Boxing Championship final was to represent Pakistan in __________.
mcqs.why: Comprehension A explains the fight was so important because the winner would represent the country in the World Lightweight Boxing Championship.

mcqs.q: To train for their dream, Ali and Gul ran at sunrise along __________.
options: the rooftop of the boxing club
mcqs.why: The story says they ran along the River Lyari at sunrise and attended the boxing club daily without any break.

mcqs.q: For how many rounds did the two friends fight in the final?
mcqs.why: The description of the fight covers three rounds, ending with Ali's eye closed and blood pouring from Gul's nose before they were separated.

mcqs.q: How did Ali and Gul leave the ring at the end of the story?
options: Separately, after the winner was announced
Carried out by their trainers on stretchers
Arm in arm, before the winner was announced
After refusing to speak to each other
mcqs.why: They embraced and left the ring arm in arm before the decision was announced, leaving the announcer alone — proof their friendship survived.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: Find out the common meaning of the word 'haymaker' in dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviations used. (Boxing meaning given in the book: the word usually used in boxing, when the person swings with full force, twists his waist and shoulders round before turning back unleashing a mighty blow!)
    Ans: Common meaning: a powerful, swinging punch. Part of speech: noun (n.). In the story Ali 'lashed back with a haymaker'.
  • Q: Find out the common meaning of the phrase 'bobbed and weaved' in dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviations used. (Boxing meaning given in the book: in boxing, a series of movements executed in which one participant dodges and defend himself/herself against his opponent's punches by moving quickly back and forth, and up and down, so as not to present a stable target)
    Ans: Common meaning: moved quickly up, down and from side to side to avoid blows. Part of speech: verb phrase; 'bob' and 'weave' are verbs (v.). In the story Ali bobbed and weaved and threw occasional punches with his right.
  • Q: Find out the common meaning of the word 'jab' in dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviations used. (Boxing meaning given in the book: jab is a type of punch used in boxing, several variations of the jab exist, but every jab shares these characteristics: while in a fighting stance, the lead fist is thrown straight ahead and the arm is fully extended.)
    Ans: Common meaning: a quick, straight punch with the front hand; also, to poke or thrust quickly. Part of speech: noun (n.) and verb (v.). In the story Gul's left hand pumped jabs one right after another.
  • Q: Find out the common meaning of the phrase 'pulling punches' in dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviations used. (Boxing meaning given in the book: it's a boxing term, when you pull a punch you don't hit the other fighter as hard as you can)
    Ans: Common meaning: holding back and not hitting with full force; also, not expressing one's opinion fully for fear of offending. Part of speech: verb phrase (idiom). Gul confessed he had been awake at nights 'pulling punches' on Ali, trying not to hurt him.
  • Q: Find out the common meaning of the word 'bout' in dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviations used. (Boxing meaning given in the book: a wrestling or boxing match)
    Ans: Common meaning: a contest or match in boxing or wrestling; also a short period of an activity or illness. Part of speech: noun (n.). The text says 'less than a week before their bout, they met as usual for their daily workout'.
  • Q: Find out the common meaning of the word 'slugger' in dictionary and identify the part of speech of the word through abbreviations used. (Boxing meaning given in the book: a person who strikes hard, especially a boxer noted for the ability to deliver hard punches)
    Ans: Common meaning: a boxer or batter who hits very hard. Part of speech: noun (n.). In the story Ali's short and muscular frame made him the better slugger.

Grammar - Articles A. Complete the following sentences using appropriate articles

  • Q: 1. My mother is ______ doctor and my father is ______ author.
    Options: a / a / a / an / the / an / a / no article
    Ans: a / an
  • Q: 2. Amjad recommended ______ good dentist, but ______ dentist doesn't have any openings for two months.
    Options: a / no article / the / an / a / the / the / the
    Ans: a / the
  • Q: 3. Do you have ______ broom? I dropped ______ piece of cake, and I need to clean it up.
    Options: a / a / no article / a / the / the / an / a
    Ans: a / a
  • Q: 4. Do you have ______ dictionary? I don't have one, and I need to look up ______ word.
    Options: a / the / an / a / the / a / a / a
    Ans: a / a
  • Q: 5. Do you have ______ passport? You need ______ passport to travel outside of ______ country.
    Options: a / a / the / an / a / the / the / the / a / a / the / a
    Ans: a / a / the

Grammar - Articles B. Complete the following exercise with a / an or the articles. Put "x" where no article is needed

  • Q: Boxing was originated in ____ Ancient Greece and has been a popular sport ever since.
    Ans: x (no article)
  • Q: Boxing was originated in Ancient Greece and has been ____ popular sport ever since, especially for men.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Boxing has been a popular sport ever since, especially for ____ men. (general reference)
    Ans: x (no article)
  • Q: Lately, however, it has been ____ major health fitness trend for women.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Lately, however, it has been a major health fitness trend for ____ women. (general reference)
    Ans: x (no article)
  • Q: Boxing was included during ____ first Olympic games.
    Ans: the
  • Q: In ____ Ancient Greece boxing was not a safe sport, they never used gloves.
    Ans: x (no article)
  • Q: In Ancient Greece boxing was not ____ safe sport, they never used gloves.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Professional boxing is ____ excellent career.
    Ans: an
  • Q: ____ boxer's aim is to land as many punches on an opponent as possible.
    Ans: A
  • Q: A boxer's aim is to land as many punches on ____ opponent as possible.
    Ans: the
  • Q: For most of ____ 20th century, boxing attracted huge fan and media attention.
    Ans: the

Pronouns A. Choose the correct pronoun to correctly finish this sentence

  • Q: 1. My name is Sonia. ____ love my family.
    Options: He / I / She / We
    Ans: I
  • Q: 2. I met Sonia yesterday. ____ made me laugh.
    Options: It / Her / She / They
    Ans: She
  • Q: 3. At the left, you can see Saad. ____ is my brother.
    Options: That / He / It / Him
    Ans: He
  • Q: 4. Birds flap ____ wings.
    Options: it / his / their / those
    Ans: their
  • Q: 5. My grandparents live in Karachi. ____ visit us.
    Options: Them / They / Their / He
    Ans: They
  • Q: 6. Lubna, Laila and Tahira were cross because __________ had waited ages for the bus.
    Options: them / he / they / it
    Ans: they
  • Q: 7. Palwasha watched the children carefully as __________ crossed the road.
    Options: them / he / they / it
    Ans: they
  • Q: 8. Hold the bag please while I put the shopping in __________.
    Options: him / it / she / i
    Ans: it

Pronouns B. Choose one of the following relative pronouns who, which or whose to complete each sentence

  • Q: I talked to the girl ____ car had broken down in front of the shop.
    Ans: whose
  • Q: Mr. Razaq, ____ is a taxi driver, lives on the corner.
    Ans: who
  • Q: I live in a house in Naran ____ is in Northern Pakistan.
    Ans: which
  • Q: This is the girl ____ comes from Swat.
    Ans: who
  • Q: That's Naeem, the boy ____ has just arrived at the airport.
    Ans: who
  • Q: Those ____ haven't paid their fee should do so at once.
    Ans: who
  • Q: This is a detective novel ____ you might like.
    Ans: which
  • Q: Here are the keys ____ you were searching for.
    Ans: which

Pronouns C. Underline the indefinite pronouns in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. Everybody enjoys a good movie.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: Everybody.
  • Q: 2. Does anybody have the time?
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: anybody.
  • Q: 3. Nobody knows the trouble I've seen.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: Nobody.
  • Q: 4. The secret was known by few.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: few.
  • Q: 5. No, the secret was known by many.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: many.
  • Q: 6. Calculus is too hard for some.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: some.
  • Q: 7. Surely you recognize somebody.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: somebody.
  • Q: 8. He's not a liar. I'm sure everything he said was true.
    Ans: Indefinite pronoun: everything.

Pronouns D. Identifying Pronouns and their antecedents. In each sentence underline once the personal pronoun and underline twice its antecedent

  • Q: 1. As a child, Asma often played with her dollhouse.
    Ans: Personal pronoun: her. Antecedent: Asma.
  • Q: 2. Neither Danish nor Waseem will have trouble finding information for their report.
    Ans: Personal pronoun: their. Antecedents: Danish and Waseem.
  • Q: 3. Each of the boys refused help saying that they would proofread the report on their own.
    Ans: Personal pronouns: they, their. Antecedent: the boys (Each of the boys).
  • Q: 4. Nobody likes to discover that they have just read a dull report about an interesting subject.
    Ans: Personal pronoun: they. Antecedent: Nobody.
  • Q: 5. Tania needs a result card of her grades.
    Ans: Personal pronoun: her. Antecedent: Tania.
  • Q: 6. Asif said that they made their own clothes.
    Ans: Personal pronouns: they, their. Antecedent: they refers to the people Asif spoke about; within this sentence no noun antecedent is named - Asif is the speaker, not the antecedent of 'they/their'.
  • Q: 7. One of the girls left her sweater in the bus.
    Ans: Personal pronoun: her. Antecedent: One (of the girls).
  • Q: 8. Several other classmates also chose their topic.
    Ans: Personal pronoun: their. Antecedent: classmates (Several other classmates).

Pronouns E. Underline the pronoun and circle its antecedent in parenthesis in sentences below (choose the correct pronoun)

  • Q: 1. Someone has removed the grammar book, and I want (him, them) to return it.
    Ans: Correct pronoun: him. Antecedent: Someone. Full sentence: Someone has removed the grammar book, and I want him to return it.
  • Q: 2. Although I knew somebody called me, I did not answer (her, them).
    Ans: Correct pronoun: them (in modern standard use for an indefinite singular antecedent; traditional singular agreement would be him/her, which is not offered as a single choice - between the two printed options, 'them' is used for 'somebody'). Antecedent: somebody.
  • Q: 3. Each man must do what (he, they) feel(s) is right.
    Ans: Correct pronoun: he (with 'feels'). Antecedent: Each man. Full sentence: Each man must do what he feels is right.
  • Q: 4. Everybody in the lab was ready to complete (her, their) assignment.
    Ans: Correct pronoun: their (everybody is treated as plural in sense; 'her' would exclude others). Antecedent: Everybody. Note: in strict traditional grammar 'his or her' is also used, but between the printed options 'their' is the inclusive choice.
  • Q: 5. No one wants to admit (his, their) weaknesses.
    Ans: Correct pronoun: his (traditional singular agreement with 'No one'; 'their' is also widely accepted today). Antecedent: No one.

mcqs.q: 1. My mother is ______ doctor and my father is ______ author.
mcqs.why: Doctor takes 'a' before a consonant sound and author takes 'an' before a vowel sound, so the correct pair is 'a / an'.

mcqs.q: 2. Amjad recommended ______ good dentist, but ______ dentist doesn't have any openings for two months.
mcqs.why: The dentist is mentioned for the first time, so 'a good dentist'; the same dentist is then specific and known, so 'the dentist'.

mcqs.q: 3. Do you have ______ broom? I dropped ______ piece of cake, and I need to clean it up.
mcqs.why: Both broom and piece of cake are mentioned for the first time and are countable singular nouns, so each takes 'a': 'a / a'.

mcqs.q: 4. Do you have ______ dictionary? I don't have one, and I need to look up ______ word.
mcqs.why: Dictionary and word are both first mentions of countable singular nouns, so the correct pair is 'a / a' in the book's key.

mcqs.q: 5. Do you have ______ passport? You need ______ passport to travel outside of ______ country.
mcqs.why: Passport is a first-mention countable noun taking 'a' twice, while 'the country' is specific and definite, giving 'a / a / the'.

mcqs.q: 1. My name is Sonia. ____ love my family.
mcqs.why: Sonia is speaking about herself, so the first-person subject pronoun 'I' is correct: 'My name is Sonia. I love my family.'

mcqs.q: 2. I met Sonia yesterday. ____ made me laugh.
mcqs.why: The pronoun refers back to Sonia as the subject of the new sentence, so the subject form 'She' is correct, not the object form 'Her'.

mcqs.q: 3. At the left, you can see Saad. ____ is my brother.
mcqs.why: Saad is male and the subject of the sentence, so 'He is my brother' is correct; 'Him' is an object form and cannot be the subject.

mcqs.q: 4. Birds flap ____ wings.
mcqs.why: Birds is plural, so the possessive pronoun must be the plural 'their': birds flap their wings.

mcqs.q: 5. My grandparents live in Karachi. ____ visit us.
mcqs.why: Grandparents is plural and the pronoun is the subject of 'visit', so the subject form 'They' is correct, not 'Them' or 'Their'.

mcqs.q: 6. Lubna, Laila and Tahira were cross because __________ had waited ages for the bus.
mcqs.why: Lubna, Laila and Tahira are three girls acting as the subject, so the plural subject pronoun 'they' is correct.

mcqs.q: 7. Palwasha watched the children carefully as __________ crossed the road.
mcqs.why: The children are the subject of 'crossed the road', so the plural subject pronoun 'they' must be used, not the object form 'them'.

mcqs.q: 8. Hold the bag please while I put the shopping in __________.
mcqs.why: The bag is a thing and the object of 'in', so the pronoun 'it' is correct: put the shopping in it.

mcqs.q: In the vocabulary section, a 'haymaker' is __________.
options: a quick, straight punch with the front hand
mcqs.why: The book defines a haymaker as the mighty swinging blow thrown with full force; the quick straight punch is a jab, and a match is a bout.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun: 'I talked to the girl ____ car had broken down in front of the shop.'
mcqs.why: The solved relative-pronoun exercise uses 'whose' because the car belongs to the girl; 'who' and 'which' cannot show possession here.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Paragraph on boxing as a sport

  • Q: A. Having read the story, one feels that boxing is too brutal to be a sport for young people. Do you agree? Which side of this debate is presented in "The Champions"? Using details and examples from the story, write a paragraph with a clear opening statement, specific details and examples to explain your response.
    Ans: Boxing is a demanding and risky sport, but 'The Champions' presents it mainly as a test of courage, discipline and friendship rather than mere brutality. Ali and Gul train day and night, running at sunrise and attending the club daily, which shows the discipline the sport builds. In the ring they fight fiercely - Ali's left eye closes and blood pours from Gul's nose - which does show the physical danger and supports those who call boxing brutal. However, the story ends with the two friends embracing and leaving the ring arm in arm, presenting boxing as a sport that can teach sportsmanship and strengthen character. I therefore partly agree that boxing is hard and risky for young people, but with proper training, rules and medical care, as the story suggests, it remains a noble sport.

Writing B. Dialogue

  • Q: B. Imagine Ali and Gul Sher as they walk away from the boxing ring after the fight. Now, keeping in mind their friendship, write their conversation as a one-page dialogue.
    Ans: Ali: Bro, your left hand is still like a piston. My eye is completely shut! Gul: And your rights, Ali! My nose is still bleeding. You fought like a real champion. Ali: So did you. For a moment in the third round I thought one of us would fall. Gul: I thought so too, but how could I enjoy winning by seeing you on the canvas? Ali: Same here. Last night I could not sleep, thinking this fight would finish our friendship. Gul: And look at us now - walking out together before they even announce the result. Ali: Let them announce whatever they like. Whoever represents Pakistan, the other will be in his corner, training with him. Gul: Agreed. We entered the ring as brothers, we fought as champions, and we leave as brothers. Ali: Arm in arm, bro. Always.

mcqs.q: The Writing A paragraph presents 'The Champions' as showing boxing mainly as __________.
options: a test of courage, discipline and friendship
a brutal street fight without any rules
an easy game that needs no training
a contest that always destroys friendship
mcqs.why: The model paragraph says the story presents boxing mainly as a test of courage, discipline and friendship rather than mere brutality.

mcqs.q: Which detail in the Writing A paragraph shows the discipline that boxing builds?
options: Ali's left eye closes during the fight
Ali and Gul run at sunrise and attend the club daily
Blood pours from Gul's nose in round three
The announcer is left alone in the ring
mcqs.why: Running at sunrise and daily club attendance show discipline; the injuries show physical danger, and the ending shows sportsmanship.

mcqs.q: Which detail in the Writing A paragraph supports those who call boxing brutal?
options: The two friends embrace after the final bell
Ali's left eye closes and blood pours from Gul's nose
They leave the ring arm in arm
mcqs.why: The paragraph admits the physical danger — a closed eye and a bleeding nose — as the evidence for the 'too brutal' side of the debate.

mcqs.q: The writer of the Writing A paragraph concludes that boxing can remain a noble sport with __________.
options: proper training, rules and medical care
mcqs.why: The paragraph concludes that with proper training, rules and medical care, boxing remains a noble sport despite its risks.

mcqs.q: The debate question set in Writing A asks whether boxing is __________.
options: too brutal to be a sport for young people
too easy to be a sport for young people
too expensive to be a sport for young people
too slow to be a sport for young people
mcqs.why: The task itself frames the debate: one feels boxing is too brutal to be a sport for young people, and the paragraph responds to that claim.

mcqs.q: In the Writing B dialogue, Gul says Ali's left hand is still like __________.
mcqs.why: Gul opens the dialogue: 'Bro, your left hand is still like a piston. My eye is completely shut!' — echoing the story's piston-like jabs.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, why does Gul say he could not enjoy winning?
options: He was too tired to enjoy anything
He did not want to represent Pakistan
He could not enjoy winning by seeing Ali on the canvas
He thought the referee was unfair
mcqs.why: Gul says: 'how could I enjoy winning by seeing you on the canvas?' — his friendship makes a victory over Ali joyless.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, what do the friends agree about representing Pakistan?
options: Neither of them will ever represent Pakistan
Only the loser will train for the world championship
They will ask for the final to be held again
Whoever represents Pakistan, the other will be in his corner, training with him
mcqs.why: Ali says whoever represents Pakistan, the other will be in his corner, training with him — the dialogue turns rivalry into partnership.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, Ali says he could not sleep the night before because he was thinking __________.
options: about the prize money of the championship
that the fight would finish their friendship
that Gul had quarrelled with him
mcqs.why: Ali confesses in the dialogue: 'Last night I could not sleep, thinking this fight would finish our friendship.'

mcqs.q: How does the Writing B dialogue end?
options: They decide never to meet again
They demand to know the winner's name
They agree they entered as brothers, fought as champions, and leave as brothers
They challenge each other to a second fight
mcqs.why: Gul's closing words sum up the dialogue: 'We entered the ring as brothers, we fought as champions, and we leave as brothers.'

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking

  • Q: Present and explain your point of view and feeling about the story 'The Champions' to the class.
    Ans: Model presentation: In my view, 'The Champions' is not only a story about boxing; it is a story about true friendship. I felt tense when Ali and Gul, who were like brothers, had to fight each other for a place in the World Championship, and I admired their honesty in agreeing to fight fair and square. During the three rounds I felt excited and also sad, because every punch hurt a friend. The ending made me happy and satisfied: they embraced and left the ring arm in arm, proving that friendship is greater than any trophy. The story teaches us to compete honestly but never to sacrifice our relationships for victory.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: What are dreams?
    Ans: Here 'dreams' does not mean only the pictures we see in sleep. It means our hopes, aims and ambitions for the future - the goals that give direction and purpose to our life, such as becoming a teacher, a doctor or a champion.
  • Q: What would your life be like if you had no dreams for your future?
    Ans: Life without dreams would be empty, dull and without direction. There would be nothing to strive for, no hope to work hard, and life would become like a broken-winged bird that cannot fly, or a barren field frozen with snow, as the poem says.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. What is the theme of the poem?
    Ans: The theme of the poem is the importance of holding fast to our dreams and ambitions. The poet warns that if dreams die, life loses its purpose, hope and fruitfulness, so we must never let our dreams go.
  • Q: 2. How important do you think dreams are? Explain.
    Ans: Dreams are extremely important because they give life direction, hope and energy to work hard. A person with a dream strives day and night to achieve it, while a person without dreams drifts aimlessly. As the poem shows, without dreams life becomes hopeless and unproductive.
  • Q: 3. Identify an example of a word or phrase that is repeated in the poem and explain why the poet makes this repetition.
    Ans: The phrase 'Hold fast to dreams' is repeated at the start of both stanzas, and the word 'Life is a...' structure is also repeated. The poet repeats it to emphasise his central advice and to fix it in the reader's mind: in both cases - if dreams die and when dreams go - the result is a ruined life, so the command must be obeyed.
  • Q: 4. Identify an example of personification. Explain what is being personified and how?
    Ans: Personification is found in 'For if dreams die' and 'For when dreams go'. Dreams, which are abstract ideas, are personified - they are given the human qualities of being able to die and to go away, as if they were living persons. This makes the loss of dreams feel real and painful.
  • Q: 5. Identify lines containing metaphors. What ideas are being conveyed by these metaphors?
    Ans: The metaphors are: 'Life is a broken-winged bird / That cannot fly' and 'Life is a barren field / Frozen with snow'. The first conveys that life without dreams is crippled and helpless, unable to rise or progress. The second conveys that life without dreams is unproductive, cold and lifeless, producing nothing of value.
  • Q: 6. List the alliterative words from the poem "Dream".
    Ans: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound. Clear examples in the poem are: 'dreams die' (d-d), 'broken-winged bird' (b-b), and the repeated 'f' sound in 'fast', 'For', 'field' and 'Frozen'.
  • Q: 7. How is imagery used in this poem?
    Ans: The poet uses strong visual imagery. The image of a broken-winged bird that cannot fly lets us picture a helpless, grounded life, and the image of a barren field frozen with snow lets us see and feel a cold, empty, unproductive life. These pictures appeal to our senses and make the abstract idea of a dreamless life concrete and moving.
  • Q: 8. What is the mood of this poem? How does it make you feel?
    Ans: The mood is serious, urgent and warning, yet also encouraging. The poet earnestly urges us to hold fast to dreams before it is too late. It makes me feel thoughtful and determined: sad at the picture of a broken, frozen life, but hopeful and motivated to protect my own dreams.

Comprehension B. Write the correct option in following statement

  • Q: 1. The phrase "hold fast to dreams" means:
    Options: don't do anything just dream day and night / day dreaming is good for health / dreaming will make your holding power strong / stick fast to your ambition in life
    Ans: stick fast to your ambition in life
  • Q: 2. In the line "life is a broken-winged bird", the poet uses the technique of __________.
    Options: metaphor / personification / simile / repetition
    Ans: metaphor
  • Q: 3. "life is a barren field", in this line the phrase "a barren field" is ______.
    Options: simile. / metaphor / personification / alliteration
    Ans: metaphor
  • Q: 4. According to the poet life without dream is __________.
    Options: hollow and bleak. / lush and hopeful / dynamic and productive / passionate and optimistic
    Ans: hollow and bleak.
  • Q: 5. According to "Dreams", what will happen if our dreams die?
    Options: Life will be easier to handle. / Life will appear as it is. / Life will continue as normal. / Life will be hopeless.
    Ans: Life will be hopeless.

mcqs.q: 1. The phrase "hold fast to dreams" means:
options: stick fast to your ambition in life
don't do anything just dream day and night
day dreaming is good for health
dreaming will make your holding power strong
mcqs.why: Hold fast means to grip tightly and not let go, so the phrase urges us to stick fast to our ambition in life, not to daydream idly.

mcqs.q: 2. In the line "life is a broken-winged bird", the poet uses the technique of __________.
mcqs.why: Life is directly compared to a broken-winged bird without 'like' or 'as', which is a metaphor, not a simile or personification.

mcqs.q: 3. "life is a barren field", in this line the phrase "a barren field" is ______.
mcqs.why: Calling life 'a barren field' directly, without a comparison word, is a metaphor; it is not a simile, personification or alliteration.

mcqs.q: 4. According to the poet life without dream is __________.
mcqs.why: The book's key describes life without dreams as hollow and bleak — empty and hopeless — the opposite of lush, dynamic or passionate.

mcqs.q: 5. According to "Dreams", what will happen if our dreams die?
options: Life will be easier to handle.
Life will appear as it is.
mcqs.why: The poem warns that if dreams die, life becomes like a broken-winged bird that cannot fly, so life will be hopeless.

mcqs.q: What is the theme of the poem 'Dreams'?
options: The pleasures of sleeping and dreaming at night
The importance of holding fast to our dreams and ambitions
The beauty of birds and snow-covered fields
The life story of the poet Langston Hughes
mcqs.why: Comprehension A states the theme: we must hold fast to dreams, because if dreams die, life loses its purpose, hope and fruitfulness.

mcqs.q: How are dreams personified in the poem?
options: They are compared to a bird with a broken wing
They are described as a field covered with snow
They are given human qualities — they can die and can go away
They are repeated at the start of both stanzas
mcqs.why: Personification appears in 'if dreams die' and 'when dreams go': abstract dreams are treated as living persons who can die or leave.

mcqs.q: The metaphor 'Life is a barren field / Frozen with snow' conveys that life without dreams is __________.
options: busy, warm and full of harvest
crippled and unable to rise or fly
unproductive, cold and lifeless, producing nothing of value
mcqs.why: The solved answer explains the barren field shows an unproductive, cold, lifeless existence; the crippled, flightless idea belongs to the bird metaphor.

mcqs.q: Which words from the poem show alliteration with the initial 'b' sound?
mcqs.why: Alliteration repeats the same initial sound: 'broken-winged bird' repeats b-b, just as 'dreams die' repeats the d sound.

mcqs.q: What is the mood of the poem 'Dreams'?
options: Angry, bitter and full of despair only
Serious, urgent and warning, yet also encouraging
Calm, sleepy and without any advice
mcqs.why: The solved answer describes a serious, urgent, warning mood that is also encouraging, making the reader determined to protect his dreams.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: Word / phrase: broken-winged - Explain if you were correct, close, or totally off and why you think that happened by using evidence from the text. Give inferred meaning and dictionary definition.
    Ans: Inferred meaning: having a damaged wing, unable to fly. Dictionary definition: with a wing that is broken. Evaluation: Correct, because the text itself gives the evidence in the next line, 'That cannot fly' - if dreams die, life is like such a bird.
  • Q: Word / phrase: barren field - Explain if you were correct, close, or totally off and why you think that happened by using evidence from the text. Give inferred meaning and dictionary definition.
    Ans: Inferred meaning: a field that produces nothing; a hopeless, unproductive life. Dictionary definition: (of land) too poor to produce much or any vegetation; an area of open land planted with crops or pasture. Evaluation: Correct / close, because the text links it with dreams going away and with being 'Frozen with snow', which shows lifelessness and no growth.
  • Q: Word / phrase: frozen with snow - Explain if you were correct, close, or totally off and why you think that happened by using evidence from the text. Give inferred meaning and dictionary definition.
    Ans: Inferred meaning: covered and hardened with snow; cold, still and lifeless. Dictionary definition: having turned into ice as a result of extreme cold (frozen). Evaluation: Correct, because in the poem the barren field is 'Frozen with snow', picturing a life with no warmth, movement or production once dreams go.
  • Q: Word / phrase: hold fast - Explain if you were correct, close, or totally off and why you think that happened by using evidence from the text. Give inferred meaning and dictionary definition.
    Ans: Inferred meaning: hold tightly and do not let go; stick firmly to your ambition. Dictionary definition (Glossary): hold something tightly and firmly. Evaluation: Correct, because the poet repeats 'Hold fast to dreams' as a command in both stanzas and warns of the loss that follows if dreams die or go.

Grammar - Transitive and intransitive verbs A. Do as directed

  • Q: 1. Choose the sentence that does not have an intransitive verb.
    Options: I jog. / The child gurgles. / I watched a movie. / She sobs.
    Ans: I watched a movie.
  • Q: 2. Choose the sentence that does not have a transitive verb.
    Options: He presented a bouquet. / He waved his arm. / She understood my question. / She laughed heartily.
    Ans: She laughed heartily.
  • Q: 3. Choose the sentence that does not have a transitive verb.
    Options: We showed her the flower vase. / The grocer is selling vegetables. / The birds are flying. / The coach advised me to practice daily.
    Ans: The birds are flying.
  • Q: 4. Choose the sentence that does not have an intransitive verb.
    Options: The customer is buying this afternoon. / The customer is buying pancakes. / They were crying all day long. / She helped me.
    Ans: The customer is buying pancakes.
  • Q: 5. Choose the sentence that does not have a transitive verb.
    Options: She cut the cake. / They climbed the hill. / Arman telephoned Tariq. / Asma shouted in the class.
    Ans: Asma shouted in the class.
  • Q: 6. Choose the sentence that does not have an intransitive verb.
    Options: The student is answering questions. / Akbar is jogging at this moment. / She sleeps too much. / He complains frequently.
    Ans: The student is answering questions.

Grammar B. Pick out five transitive and five intransitive verbs from the story "The Champions"

  • Q: Pick out five transitive and five intransitive verbs from the story "The Champions".
    Ans: Five transitive verbs (with their objects): 1) represent (the country) - the winner was to represent the country; 2) throw (fists) - to throw fists at an imaginary jaw; 3) trapped (him) - Ali trapped him against the ropes; 4) pour (rights and lefts) - to pour some punishing rights and lefts; 5) raised (their arms) - they raised their arms in acknowledgment. Five intransitive verbs: 1) running - they would be found running along the River Lyari; 2) bowed - Gul and Ali both bowed gracefully; 3) rushed - Ali rushed at Gul like a bull; 4) blinked - the lights of the city blinked; 5) falling - falling into a restless and fitful sleep.

Present Participle or Past Participle A. Write the verb in parenthesis in the correct form (present participle or past participle)

  • Q: ____ (prepare) by the best cook in town, the meal was sheer poetry.
    Ans: Prepared
  • Q: After ____ (study) all day, her head was aching in the evening.
    Ans: studying
  • Q: ____ (lie) on the sofa, they were watching TV.
    Ans: Lying
  • Q: Everybody was ____ (shock) to hear the news.
    Ans: shocked
  • Q: Before ____ (leave) the house, I always check if all lights are switched-off.
    Ans: leaving

Present Participle or Past Participle B. Combine the following pairs of sentences by using participles (present / past). The first one has been done: We met a boy. He was carrying a heavy bag. - We met a boy carrying a heavy bag

  • Q: 2. The house was decorated with lights. It looked beautiful.
    Ans: Decorated with lights, the house looked beautiful. (Also: The house, decorated with lights, looked beautiful.)
  • Q: 3. The robbers saw the policeman. They ran away.
    Ans: Seeing the policeman, the robbers ran away.
  • Q: 4. I found the door open. I went inside.
    Ans: Finding the door open, I went inside.
  • Q: 5. The police saw the body. It was floating down the river.
    Ans: The police saw the body floating down the river.

Grammar - The Clause: Read the sentences and decide if the bold words form a dependent, independent or relative clause

  • Q: 1. Tahir did his homework before he went to bed. (Bold: 'Tahir did his homework')
    Ans: Independent clause (main clause) - it has a subject and verb and expresses a complete thought.
  • Q: 2. Isn't that the woman who lives across the road from you? (Bold: 'the woman who lives' / 'who lives across the road from you')
    Ans: Relative clause - 'who lives across the road from you' begins with the relative pronoun 'who' and describes 'the woman'.
  • Q: 3. Because the test was so difficult, none of the students got a very good grade. (Bold: 'none of the students got a very good grade')
    Ans: Independent clause (main clause) - it can stand alone as a complete sentence.
  • Q: 4. She is very fit because she goes running every day. (Bold: 'because she goes running every day')
    Ans: Dependent (subordinate) clause - it begins with the subordinate conjunction 'because' and cannot stand alone.
  • Q: 5. The police said the accident that happened last night was unavoidable. (Bold: 'the accident that happened')
    Ans: Relative clause - 'that happened last night' begins with the relative pronoun 'that' and describes 'the accident'.
  • Q: 6. I don't like Mondays.
    Ans: Independent clause - the whole sentence is a single main clause with subject 'I' and verb 'don't like'.
  • Q: 7. Have you seen those people who we met on holiday? (Bold: 'those people who we met')
    Ans: Relative clause - 'who we met on holiday' begins with the relative pronoun 'who' and describes 'those people'.
  • Q: 8. Can you tell me why you said that? (Bold: 'Can you tell me')
    Ans: Independent clause (main clause) - 'Can you tell me' is the main clause of the question.
  • Q: 9. You shouldn't believe everything that you read in the newspaper. (Bold: 'everything that you read')
    Ans: Relative clause - 'that you read in the newspaper' begins with the relative pronoun 'that' and describes 'everything'.
  • Q: 10. If you help me, I will help you! (Bold: 'If you help me')
    Ans: Dependent (subordinate) clause - it begins with the subordinate conjunction 'If' and needs the main clause to complete its thought.

mcqs.q: 1. Choose the sentence that does not have an intransitive verb.
mcqs.why: 'I watched a movie' has the transitive verb 'watched' with the object 'a movie'; jog, gurgles and sobs in the other sentences have no object.

mcqs.q: 2. Choose the sentence that does not have a transitive verb.
mcqs.why: 'She laughed heartily' has no object after 'laughed', so it has no transitive verb; the other sentences all have verbs with objects.

mcqs.q: 3. Choose the sentence that does not have a transitive verb.
options: We showed her the flower vase.
The coach advised me to practice daily.
mcqs.why: 'The birds are flying' has no object, so it has no transitive verb; showed, selling and advised in the others all take objects.

mcqs.q: 4. Choose the sentence that does not have an intransitive verb.
options: The customer is buying this afternoon.
They were crying all day long.
mcqs.why: 'The customer is buying pancakes' has the transitive verb 'buying' with the object 'pancakes'; note the book also lists 'She helped me' here, but 'buying pancakes' is the book's keyed answer.

mcqs.q: 5. Choose the sentence that does not have a transitive verb.
mcqs.why: 'Asma shouted in the class' has no object, so it has no transitive verb; cut, climbed and telephoned in the others all take objects.

mcqs.q: 6. Choose the sentence that does not have an intransitive verb.
options: Akbar is jogging at this moment.
mcqs.why: 'The student is answering questions' has the transitive verb 'answering' with the object 'questions'; jogging, sleeps and complains take no object.

mcqs.q: Which verb from 'The Champions' is listed in Grammar B as transitive, with the object 'the country'?
mcqs.why: Grammar B lists 'represent (the country)' among the transitive verbs, while running, bowed and blinked are listed as intransitive.

mcqs.q: Which verb from 'The Champions' is listed in Grammar B as intransitive?
mcqs.why: Grammar B lists 'bowed — Gul and Ali both bowed gracefully' as intransitive; represent, trapped and raised all take objects and are transitive.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct participle form: '____ (prepare) by the best cook in town, the meal was sheer poetry.'
mcqs.why: The meal was prepared by someone else, so the past participle 'Prepared' is correct, as given in the solved participle exercise.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank with the correct participle form: 'Everybody was ____ (shock) to hear the news.'
mcqs.why: Everybody received the shock, so the past participle adjective 'shocked' is correct; 'shocking' would describe what causes the shock.

mcqs.q: Combine the sentences using a participle: 'The robbers saw the policeman. They ran away.'
options: Seen the policeman, the robbers ran away.
Saw the policeman, the robbers ran away.
Seeing the policeman, the robbers ran away.
See the policeman, the robbers ran away.
mcqs.why: The solved combination uses the present participle 'Seeing' because the robbers were the ones who saw the policeman.

mcqs.q: In 'She is very fit because she goes running every day', the clause 'because she goes running every day' is __________.
mcqs.why: The clause begins with the subordinate conjunction 'because' and cannot stand alone, so the solved exercise calls it a dependent clause.

mcqs.q: In 'Isn't that the woman who lives across the road from you?', the clause 'who lives across the road from you' is __________.
mcqs.why: It begins with the relative pronoun 'who' and describes 'the woman', so the solved exercise identifies it as a relative clause.

mcqs.q: According to the glossary work in Vocabulary, 'hold fast' means __________.
options: let go of something slowly and gently
mcqs.why: The vocabulary section gives the dictionary definition of 'hold fast' as holding something tightly and firmly — the poem's central command.

mcqs.q: In the combined sentence 'The police saw the body floating down the river', the word 'floating' is __________.
mcqs.why: The solved combination uses the present participle 'floating' to join 'The police saw the body' with 'It was floating down the river'.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Persuasive essay

  • Q: A. Keeping in view the main points of persuasive essay, write an essay having a thesis sentence: "A dream doesn't become reality through magic; it takes sweat, determination and hard work."
    Ans: A dream doesn't become reality through magic; it takes sweat, determination and hard work. Every successful person first dreams, but only those who work for the dream succeed. Langston Hughes urges us to hold fast to dreams, yet holding fast means daily effort, not day-dreaming. A student who dreams of becoming a doctor must study for years, face failures and still continue; a boxer like Ali and Gul in 'The Champions' ran every morning and trained daily to chase his dream. Some people argue that luck decides success, but luck helps only those who are prepared through hard work. Therefore, we should protect our dreams and then pay their price in sweat and determination, because a dream without work remains only a wish.

Writing B. Research task

  • Q: B. Research the life of a famous person who faced obstacles during his / her life. Describe the obstacles and how the person overcame them.
    Ans: Model answer (on the poet, Langston Hughes, and a life of obstacles): Langston Hughes was born on February 1, 1902, in Joplin, Missouri, in a time when Black Americans faced poverty and racial discrimination, and his family life was unsettled. He faced the obstacles of poverty, prejudice and lack of recognition for Black writers. He overcame them by holding fast to his dream of writing: he worked at ordinary jobs, kept writing poetry, prose and plays, published his first book in 1926, and went on to write countless works and a popular column for the Chicago Defender. His life proves the message of 'Dreams' - obstacles cannot kill a person who refuses to let his dream die.

mcqs.q: What is the thesis sentence of the persuasive essay in Writing A?
options: A dream doesn't become reality through magic; it takes sweat, determination and hard work.
Dreams are the pictures we see in our sleep at night.
Luck alone decides who succeeds in life.
Hold fast to dreams, for if dreams die, life is a broken-winged bird.
mcqs.why: Writing A sets this exact thesis sentence, and the whole model essay is built to persuade the reader of it.

mcqs.q: In the essay, a student who dreams of becoming a doctor must __________.
options: wait for magic to make the dream real
study for years, face failures and still continue
stop studying after the first failure
depend only on luck to succeed
mcqs.why: The essay argues that holding fast means daily effort: the future doctor must study for years, face failures and still continue.

mcqs.q: Which example does the essay use from 'The Champions' to support hard work?
options: Ali and Gul won their fight without any training
Ali and Gul gave up boxing after one defeat
Ali and Gul ran every morning and trained daily to chase their dream
Ali and Gul depended on the referee to win
mcqs.why: The essay cites the boxers of 'The Champions', who ran every morning and trained daily, as proof that dreams demand sweat and effort.

mcqs.q: How does the essay answer the argument that luck decides success?
options: Luck is the only thing that decides success
Hard work has no connection with success
Dreams become real through magic and luck
Luck helps only those who are prepared through hard work
mcqs.why: The essay concedes the luck argument only to refute it: luck helps only those who are prepared through hard work.

mcqs.q: The essay concludes that a dream without work remains only __________.
mcqs.why: The final line of the essay warns: a dream without work remains only a wish — so we must pay the price in sweat and determination.

mcqs.q: The model answer for the Writing B research task describes the obstacles in the life of __________.
options: Piri Thomas, the author of a boxing story
Ahmad Ali and Gul Sher, the two boxers
mcqs.why: The research model answer takes the poet Langston Hughes himself and describes the obstacles he faced and overcame.

mcqs.q: According to the research model answer, Langston Hughes was born __________.
options: in Lyari, Karachi, before his family moved
in a wealthy family in New York
mcqs.why: The model answer gives his birth as February 1, 1902, in Joplin, Missouri, in a time of poverty and racial discrimination.

mcqs.q: Which obstacles did Hughes face, according to the research model answer?
options: A broken wing and a frozen, barren field
Defeat in a national boxing final
Poverty, prejudice and lack of recognition for Black writers
mcqs.why: The answer lists poverty, racial prejudice and lack of recognition for Black writers as the obstacles of his unsettled early life.

mcqs.q: How did Hughes overcome his obstacles, according to the model answer?
options: He gave up writing and chose another profession
