He worked at ordinary jobs and kept writing poetry, prose and plays
He waited for recognition without publishing anything
He left his country and stopped writing poetry
mcqs.why: He held fast to his writing dream: he worked ordinary jobs, kept writing, published his first book in 1926 and wrote a column for the Chicago Defender.

mcqs.q: According to the model answer, Hughes published his first book in __________.
mcqs.why: The research answer states that he published his first book in 1926 and went on to write countless works — 1902 is his birth year.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking

  • Q: Each student should share his / her future dreams and aspirations with the class and get opinion and feedback of the class on them.
    Ans: Model sharing: My dream is to become a good teacher in my own area. I want this because education can change the life of poor children, just as dreams changed the lives of Ali and Gul in 'The Champions'. To achieve it, I will hold fast to my dream, study hard, improve my English and never give up when I face difficulties. I welcome the opinion and feedback of my class on how I can prepare better for this goal.

chapters.title: Unit 4: Population Growth and its Impact on Environment

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the mind-map to predict the theme of the lesson. (Mind-map: Population Growth - Increased Needs - Increased Consumption - Environmental Destruction - Declining Resources - Scarcity and Proverty [Poverty] - Discrimination, Migration, Conflict)
    Ans: The mind-map predicts that the lesson is about how population growth increases human needs and consumption, which destroys the environment and declines resources. This leads to scarcity and poverty, and finally to discrimination, migration and conflict. The theme is therefore the direct and harmful impact of population growth on the environment.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. Why is there no single and easy solution to the problem of population growth and its impact on environment?
    Ans: There is no single easy solution because the problem has many linked causes and effects - consumption of land, food, water and fossil fuel, production of waste, deforestation, urbanization and industrialization. The text says all options must be part of the solution: educating people about their actions and effects, reassessing consumption patterns, reducing resource use, saying no to plastics, buying less and recycling waste, along with managing population growth.
  • Q: 2. How is the carrying capacity of earth affected?
    Ans: The carrying capacity of earth means the number of people the earth can support with its limited resources; scientists estimate it ranges from 500 million to more than one trillion. As population continues to grow, more people use more resources and create more waste, so the pressure on this limited capacity increases. Whether the figure is 500 million or one trillion, we still have only one planet with limited resources, so unchecked growth strains and threatens that capacity.
  • Q: 3. Why does population growth directly affect the environment?
    Ans: Population growth directly affects the environment because an increase in population means an increase in consuming more resources and producing vast quantities of waste materials. More people need more land, food, water and fossil fuel, and produce more garbage, greenhouse gases and water and air pollutants. It also causes deforestation, urbanization and industrialization, which deteriorate the health of the environment.
  • Q: 4. Analyse any passage of the text 'Population Growth and its Impact on Environment' and identify key idea and its supporting details.
    Ans: Passage analysed: the paragraph beginning 'The conversion of forested areas to non-forest land... is called deforestation.' Key idea: Deforestation is a major result of population pressure and it creates several imbalances in the environment, decreasing habitat and biodiversity. Supporting details: urbanization, mining, fires, logging and agricultural activities are causes of deforestation; forests cover 30% of the earth's land; according to the FAO, an estimated 18 million acres (7.3 million hectares) of forest are lost each year; agriculture, urbanization, poverty, over-population and unequal land access are the main causes of man-made deforestation; if the current rate continues, all forests will be destroyed in less than 100 years.
  • Q: 5. Locate examples from the text 'Population Growth and its Impact on Environment' that support an opinion.
    Ans: An opinion in the text is: 'Experts in the field of population and environment worry that this unchecked population growth may result in environmental catastrophe.' Examples from the text that support an opinion (rather than a plain fact) include: 'A quick look at the realities on ground show that the health of our environment has deteriorated because of overpopulation' - this is presented as the writer's judgement supported by facts such as forests being cleared, more factories being built, and more unwanted materials being thrown away every day adding to the garbage-mound.
  • Q: 6. Keeping in view the population and the environment of your area, do you agree or not with the content of the lesson? Support your view with solid arguments.
    Ans: Yes, I agree with the content of the lesson, because the same effects can be seen in my area. Population has increased, so more houses are built on agricultural land, trees are cut, and garbage is thrown in streets and open places. More vehicles and small factories pollute the air and water, and clean water and open green places are becoming scarce. These local facts prove the lesson's point that increased needs and consumption lead to environmental destruction and declining resources, so we must reduce waste, recycle and protect trees.

Comprehension B. Choose the correct option

  • Q: 1. Experts in the field of population and environment worry that this unchecked population growth may result in environmental catastrophe. In this sentence the word "unchecked" means ______.
    Options: enormous / unnatural / free / limited
    Ans: free
  • Q: 2. Presently seven billion and six million people live in the world. The idea expressed in this sentence is based on __________.
    Options: fact / opinion / inference / comparison and contrast
    Ans: fact
  • Q: 3. A huge quantity of pollutants are being let out in the air. In this sentence the phrase "let out" means __________________.
    Options: released / produced / absorbed / bold
    Ans: released
  • Q: 4. According to the text, the term "the carrying capacity of earth" means ____________.
    Options: the huge quantities of pollutants that are being let out on earth / the maximum population size of the species that the environment can sustain / the dominant influence of humans and their activities on the environment / the difference between the birth rate and the death rate
    Ans: the maximum population size of the species that the environment can sustain
  • Q: 5. The issue of population growth and environment is the issue of __________.
    Options: poor and developing nations only. / wealthy and advanced nations only. / poor, developing and advanced nations / niether poor nor advanced nations
    Ans: poor, developing and advanced nations

mcqs.q: Experts in the field of population and environment worry that this unchecked population growth may result in environmental catastrophe. In this sentence the word "unchecked" means ______.
mcqs.why: The solved key gives 'free' for 'unchecked', meaning not controlled or not checked, so the other choices do not fit the sentence.

mcqs.q: Presently seven billion and six million people live in the world. The idea expressed in this sentence is based on __________.
mcqs.why: The sentence states a countable population figure, so the lesson treats it as a statement of fact rather than an opinion or inference.

mcqs.q: A huge quantity of pollutants are being let out in the air. In this sentence the phrase "let out" means __________________.
mcqs.why: In the lesson 'let out' is used for pollutants entering the air, which means they are released, not produced or absorbed there.

mcqs.q: According to the text, the term "the carrying capacity of earth" means ____________.
options: the maximum population size of the species that the environment can sustain
the dominant influence of humans and their activities on the environment
the huge quantities of pollutants that are being let out on earth
the difference between the birth rate and the death rate
mcqs.why: The lesson defines carrying capacity as the maximum population size that the environment can sustain with its limited resources.

mcqs.q: The issue of population growth and environment is the issue of __________.
mcqs.why: The lesson stresses that population and environment concern poor, developing and advanced nations together, not only one group.

mcqs.q: Why is there no single and easy solution to the problem of population growth and its impact on environment, according to the lesson?
options: Because scientists have not studied the problem at all
Because population growth has no effect on resources
Because it has many linked causes and effects, so all options must be part of the solution
Because only deforestation causes the whole problem
mcqs.why: The answer explains that land, food, water and fuel use, waste, deforestation, urbanization and industrialization are all linked, so no single step can solve it.

mcqs.q: According to scientists in the lesson, the carrying capacity of earth is estimated to range from what to what?
options: From 500 million to more than one trillion
From seven billion to eight billion
From one billion to two billion
mcqs.why: The comprehension answer states that scientists estimate the carrying capacity ranges from 500 million to more than one trillion people.

mcqs.q: According to the FAO figure quoted in the lesson, how much forest is lost each year?
options: An estimated 1.8 million acres (0.73 million hectares)
An estimated 100 million acres (40 million hectares)
An estimated 18 million acres (7.3 million hectares)
An estimated 30 million acres (12 million hectares)
mcqs.why: The passage analysis quotes the FAO estimate of 18 million acres, that is 7.3 million hectares, of forest lost each year.

mcqs.q: What share of the earth's land do forests cover, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The supporting details in the lesson state clearly that forests cover 30% of the earth's land surface.

mcqs.q: Which action is listed in the lesson as part of the solution to population and environment problems?
options: Saying no to plastics, buying less and recycling waste
Using more plastics and buying more goods
mcqs.why: The lesson lists educating people, reassessing consumption, reducing resource use, saying no to plastics, buying less and recycling waste as parts of the solution.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: Find out the meaning of the word 'vivid', identify its part of speech and use it in your own sentence to make its sense clear.
    Ans: Meaning: very clear, bright and detailed, producing a strong picture in the mind. Part of speech: adjective. Sentence: The picture of growing population and environmental limitations will become more vivid if we dwell on this problem in some detail. (Own sentence: She gave a vivid description of the flooded street.)
  • Q: Find out the meaning of the word 'dwell', identify its part of speech and use it in your own sentence to make its sense clear.
    Ans: Meaning: to live in a place (formal); 'dwell on' means to think or speak about something for a long time. Part of speech: verb. Sentence: The lesson asks us to dwell on the problem of population growth in some detail.
  • Q: Find out the meaning of the word 'deteriorated', identify its part of speech and use it in your own sentence to make its sense clear.
    Ans: Meaning: became worse in quality or condition. Part of speech: verb (past tense / past participle of 'deteriorate'). Sentence: The health of our environment has deteriorated because of overpopulation.
  • Q: Find out the meaning of the word 'pasture', identify its part of speech and use it in your own sentence to make its sense clear.
    Ans: Meaning (Glossary): land covered with grass that is suitable for feeding animals on. Part of speech: noun. Sentence: Forests are cleared and turned into pasture for cattle.
  • Q: Find out the meaning of the word 'logging', identify its part of speech and use it in your own sentence to make its sense clear.
    Ans: Meaning: the work or business of cutting down trees for wood. Part of speech: noun (also verb form of 'log'). Sentence: Logging is one of the causes of deforestation.
  • Q: Find out the meaning of the word 'migration', identify its part of speech and use it in your own sentence to make its sense clear.
    Ans: Meaning: the movement of people (or animals) from one place to another to live or work there. Part of speech: noun. Sentence: Much of urban migration is driven by rural populations' desire for the advantages that urban areas offer.

Grammar - Tenses A. Rewrite the following sentences using the tense indicated in the brackets

  • Q: 1. He will do his work with diligence. (Simple present)
    Ans: He does his work with diligence.
  • Q: 2. I followed his instructions. (Simple future)
    Ans: I will follow his instructions.
  • Q: 3. That will be interesting. (Present continuous)
    Ans: That is being interesting. (Note: 'be' is a stative verb and is not normally used in the continuous form; this is the mechanical conversion asked for in the exercise. In natural English we say: That is interesting.)
  • Q: 4. I will not allow this to happen. (Simple past)
    Ans: I did not allow this to happen.
  • Q: 5. He worked very hard. (Future continuous)
    Ans: He will be working very hard.
  • Q: 6. I will never raise any demand. (Present perfect)
    Ans: I have never raised any demand.
  • Q: 7. He is crying at the top of his voice. (Past perfect)
    Ans: He had cried at the top of his voice.
  • Q: 8. We buy vegetables from the market. (Present perfect)
    Ans: We have bought vegetables from the market.

Grammar - Tenses B. Fill in the correct form of the verb (Hashim passage)

  • Q: My friend, Hashim, has always been fat, but things ____ (get) so bad recently that he decided to go on a diet.
    Ans: got
  • Q: He ____ (begin) his diet a week ago.
    Ans: began
  • Q: First of all, he ____ (write) out a long list of all the foods which were forbidden.
    Ans: wrote
  • Q: The list included most of the food he ____ (love): butter, potatoes, rice, cold drink, chocolate, sweets and so on.
    Ans: loved
  • Q: Yesterday, I ____ (pay) him a visit.
    Ans: paid
  • Q: I ____ (ring) the bell and was not surprised to see Hashim as fat as ever.
    Ans: rang
  • Q: He ____ (lead) me to his room and hurriedly hid a large parcel under his desk.
    Ans: led
  • Q: He hurriedly ____ (hide) a large parcel under his desk.
    Ans: hid
  • Q: When I ____ (ask) him what he was doing, he smiled guiltily.
    Ans: asked
  • Q: When I asked him what he ____ (do), he smiled guiltily and then put the parcel on the desk.
    Ans: was doing (also accepted: did)
  • Q: He ____ (smile) guiltily and then put the parcel on the desk.
    Ans: smiled
  • Q: He smiled guiltily and then ____ (put) the parcel on the desk.
    Ans: put
  • Q: He ____ (show) me the contents of the parcel. It contained five large bars of chocolate and three bags of sweets!
    Ans: showed

Present Perfect Continuous / Past Perfect Continuous A. Choose the correct answer

  • Q: 1. I love this writer's books. I have been reading / had been reading them for years.
    Ans: have been reading - the reading started in the past and continues up to the present, with a present result (I love his books now).
  • Q: 2. His clothes were dirty because he has been working / had been working in the garden.
    Ans: had been working - the working happened before another past action/state (his clothes were dirty).
  • Q: 3. Where have you been? We had been waiting / have been waiting for you for ages.
    Ans: have been waiting - the waiting continued up to the present moment of speaking.
  • Q: 4. He hasn't decided on a career yet, but he has been thinking / had been thinking about it lately.
    Ans: has been thinking - 'hasn't decided yet' and 'lately' show the action continues to the present.
  • Q: 5. After she has been playing / had been playing the tennis for ten years, she joined a squash team.
    Ans: had been playing - the playing happened before the past action 'she joined a squash team'.

Present Perfect Continuous / Past Perfect Continuous B. Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets. Use the Present Perfect Continuous or the Past Perfect Continuous

  • Q: Nabeel has never had an accident and he ____ (drive) for years.
    Ans: has been driving
  • Q: She had no idea it was so late because she ____ (not / watch) the time.
    Ans: had not been watching
  • Q: "____ (you / take) your medicine regularly, Mrs. Sami?" "Yes, doctor."
    Ans: Have you been taking
  • Q: They eventually found the dog after they ____ (look) for it all night.
    Ans: had been looking
  • Q: How long ____ your father ____ (work) for the company when he retired?
    Ans: had ... been working (How long had your father been working for the company when he retired?)

Present Perfect Continuous / Past Perfect Continuous C. Complete the sentences with a suitable word or expression (for, by tomorrow, so far, the week before, since)

  • Q: Our TV hasn't been working ____ last week.
    Ans: since
  • Q: The Khans invited us to dinner although we had only met ____.
    Ans: the week before
  • Q: They will have finished painting the house ____.
    Ans: by tomorrow
  • Q: We had been writing ____ nearly an hour when the bell rang.
    Ans: for
  • Q: They have interviewed three suspects ____.
    Ans: so far

Present Perfect Continuous / Past Perfect Continuous D. Correct the errors in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. Jameela has lost weight. She had been dieting for months now.
    Ans: Corrected: Jameela has lost weight. She has been dieting for months now. ('now' requires the Present Perfect Continuous, not 'had been'.)
  • Q: 2. Everything was white when we woke up because it has been snowing all night.
    Ans: Corrected: Everything was white when we woke up because it had been snowing all night. (The snowing happened before the past action 'we woke up', so Past Perfect Continuous is needed.)
  • Q: 3. I was so happy when I received the gold medal. I has been working hard for years.
    Ans: Corrected: I was so happy when I received the gold medal. I had been working hard for years. ('I has' is wrong, and the working was before the past receiving, so 'had been working'.)
  • Q: 4. The upcoming test is making me nervous. I had been preparing all evening.
    Ans: Corrected: The upcoming test is making me nervous. I have been preparing all evening. (The preparation continues to the present, so Present Perfect Continuous is needed.)
  • Q: 5. We have been writing since nearly an hour when the bell rang.
    Ans: Corrected: We had been writing for nearly an hour when the bell rang. (Use 'for' with a period of time, and Past Perfect Continuous because the bell rang in the past.)

mcqs.q: Choose the correct form: 'His clothes were dirty because he ____ in the garden.'

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Essay

  • Q: A. Write an essay of about 500 words on 'Causes and effects of the wild growth of urban population' by keeping in mind the following steps: introductory paragraph with central thought; provide key ideas that support central thought, use separate paragraph for each key idea; give evidence, examples or different point of view; use transitional device to connect ideas within and between paragraphs; add closing paragraph with closing statement.
    Ans: Causes and Effects of the Wild Growth of Urban Population. Central thought: The wild growth of urban population, called urbanization, is reshaping our environment and our lives, and unless it is managed wisely it will create scarcity, pollution and conflict. Urbanization is a process whereby populations move from rural to urban areas, enabling cities and towns to grow. First, the main cause of this growth is the search for a better life. Rural people migrate to cities for greater opportunities in education, health care, jobs and entertainment. Urbanization began during the Industrial Revolution in the 18th century, when workers moved towards manufacturing hubs in cities to obtain jobs in factories as agricultural jobs became less common, and the same attraction continues today. Secondly, the natural increase of city population itself adds to the growth, and experts think that future world population growth will be in towns and cities. As a result, the effects are severe. Urban people change their environment through their consumption of food, energy, water and land, and in turn the polluted urban environment affects their health and quality of life. Moreover, industrialisation and urbanization are the major cause of waste production: every year we dump a massive 2.12 billion tons of waste, plastic clogs the world's oceans and rivers, and huge quantities of pollutants are let out in the air, water and land. Consequently, pressure on housing, water, energy and land increases, forests are cleared for urban use, and scarcity and poverty grow. Some people argue that city growth brings development, services and progress, and this is true to an extent; however, development that destroys forests, pollutes rivers and fills streets with garbage cannot last. In conclusion, the wild growth of urban population is caused mainly by migration for jobs, education and services, and its effects - pollution, waste, deforestation and scarcity - harm both people and the planet. We must therefore plan our cities, reduce and recycle waste, save resources and educate people, so that our cities remain places worth living in for future generations.

mcqs.q: What is the topic of the model essay in Writing A?
options: The history of the Industrial Revolution only
Causes and effects of deforestation only
Causes and effects of the wild growth of urban population
How to recycle plastic waste at home
mcqs.why: Writing A asks for an essay of about 500 words on the causes and effects of the wild growth of urban population, which is urbanization.

mcqs.q: How does the model essay define urbanization?
options: A process whereby city people move back to villages
A process of reducing the size of cities and towns
A process of building factories in forests
A process whereby populations move from rural to urban areas, enabling cities and towns to grow
mcqs.why: The model essay defines urbanization as the movement of populations from rural to urban areas, enabling cities and towns to grow.

mcqs.q: According to the model essay, what is the main cause of the wild growth of urban population?
options: City people want to live in villages for farming
Rural people migrate to cities in search of a better life, including jobs, education and health care
Forests are cleared to make new villages
Factories force all workers to leave cities
mcqs.why: The essay says the main cause is the search for a better life, as rural people migrate for education, health care, jobs and entertainment.

mcqs.q: When did urbanization begin, according to the model essay?
options: During the Industrial Revolution in the 20th century
During the Industrial Revolution in the 18th century
Before farming began in ancient times
After the invention of plastic in recent years
mcqs.why: The essay states that urbanization began during the Industrial Revolution in the 18th century, when workers moved towards manufacturing hubs.

mcqs.q: How much waste do we dump every year, according to the model essay?
options: A massive 2.12 million tons of waste
A massive 21.2 thousand tons of waste
A massive 212 billion tons of waste
A massive 2.12 billion tons of waste
mcqs.why: The model essay gives the figure of 2.12 billion tons of waste dumped every year, with plastic clogging oceans and rivers.

mcqs.q: How should the model essay be structured, according to the Writing A instructions?
options: A closing paragraph first, then the introduction at the end
An introductory paragraph with the central thought, a separate paragraph for each key idea, and a closing paragraph
One single paragraph with no introduction or conclusion
Only a list of points with no paragraphs at all
mcqs.why: The instructions require an introductory paragraph with the central thought, a separate paragraph for each key idea, and a closing paragraph with a closing statement.

mcqs.q: What should be used to connect ideas within and between paragraphs in the essay?
mcqs.why: Writing A explicitly requires transitional devices to connect ideas within paragraphs and between paragraphs in the essay.

mcqs.q: According to the model essay, how does the polluted urban environment affect urban people?
options: It only affects people living in villages
It improves their health and quality of life
It affects their health and quality of life
It has no effect on people at all
mcqs.why: The essay says urban people change their environment through consumption, and in turn the polluted urban environment affects their health and quality of life.

mcqs.q: What different point of view does the model essay include about city growth?
options: Some people argue that city growth brings development, services and progress
Some people argue that cities should have no schools
Some people argue that migration should be stopped by force
Some people argue that waste protects the environment
mcqs.why: The essay includes the other viewpoint that city growth brings development, services and progress, while noting that destructive development cannot last.

mcqs.q: What does the closing paragraph of the model essay recommend?
options: Plan our cities, reduce and recycle waste, save resources and educate people
Build more factories and dump more waste
Cut all forests and fill streets with garbage
Stop education and ignore resource use
mcqs.why: The conclusion recommends planning cities, reducing and recycling waste, saving resources and educating people so cities remain worth living in.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking

  • Q: Keeping in view the conventions and dynamics of group discussion and interaction, share your information and ideas about the effects of population growth on Environment with the class.
    Ans: Model discussion contribution: I would like to share that population growth has a direct impact on our environment. More people consume more land, food, water and fossil fuel, and produce more garbage, greenhouse gases and pollutants. In our own area we can see forests and fields turning into housing, and garbage-mounds growing every day. In my opinion, there is no single easy solution; we all must take shorter showers, say no to plastics, buy less and recycle our waste. I invite my classmates to add their observations and suggestions so that we can agree on practical steps for our school and homes.

chapters.title: Unit 5: The Great Masjid of Cordoba and Iqbal

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the picture and guess what the lesson is about.
    Ans: The pictures show a grand old masjid with minarets, arches, columns, a Mehrab and a dome. The lesson is about the Great Masjid of Cordoba in Spain, a masterpiece of Islamic architecture, and about Allama Iqbal, who visited it in 1933 and wrote his famous poem Masjid-e-Qurtuba about it.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. Where did Abdur Rehman 1 import fruit trees and other plants from? Why?
    Ans: Abdur Rehman 1 imported fruit trees and olive plants from his former home, Damascus, the capital of the Islamic state. He did this because he wanted to recreate in Cordoba the glory and grandeur of Damascus, which he had left after the fall of the Umayyad Dynasty.
  • Q: 2. What can we achieve again if we enkindle in ourselves the master passion (Ishq)?
    Ans: If we enkindle in ourselves the master passion, Ishq, we can again achieve the exalted state of moral and spiritual character and produce the finest works of art like the Masjid of Cordoba. The lesson says such a masterpiece can be accomplished only when a person (mard-e-Khuda) is at that exalted state, and we can achieve this again by reviving Ishq, the perpetual and sincere struggle to achieve one's ideals.
  • Q: 3. What is the view of Iqbal about the Masjid of Cordoba? Explain his view in your own words.
    Ans: Iqbal viewed the Masjid not as an ordinary ancient monument but as a living symbol of faith and of the Ishq of those who built it. He believed its beauty and grandeur came from the intense Ishq of the Mard-e-Khuda, which still emanates from its premises. For Iqbal, Ishq is the burning desire to achieve one's ideal of perfection and self-realisation through the moral teachings of Islam, and it is the essence of life on which death has no power.
  • Q: 4. What, in your opinion, is the significance of the Masjid of Cordoba to present day Muslims? Explain
    Ans: For present-day Muslims the Masjid is a reminder of their glorious past, when Cordoba was the intellectual and cultural centre of Europe and Muslim civilisation led the world in learning, art and architecture. It teaches them that such greatness was achieved through Ishq, faith and sincere struggle. It also warns them, through its conversion into a cathedral, that nations lose their heritage when they lose that passion, so it inspires them to revive it.
  • Q: 5. Why did Iqbal greatly appreciate a faraway Masjid in Spain, when there were superb buildings of the Muslim era in Sub-Continent?
    Ans: Iqbal appreciated the Masjid of Cordoba because it was not merely a fine building but a symbol of the past glory of Islam and of the Ishq of the Mard-e-Khuda who built it. Its sight transported him into the golden age of Islam which gave roots to the enlightenment of Europe. In it he saw the traces of the Ishq of its builders, and those strong feelings resulted in one of his superb poems, the Masjid-e-Qurtuba, which carries his message for Muslims everywhere.

Comprehension B. Choose the correct option

  • Q: 1. After the fall of Muslims in Spain, the Masjid was converted into a cathedral. It shows that Muslims were overthrown by ________________.
    Options: Hindus / Jews / Christians / Sikhs
    Ans: Christians
  • Q: 2. We can achieve ________________ again if we enkindle in ourselves the master passion (Ishq).
    Options: the great Masjid of Cordoba / finest work of art / exalted state of moral and spiritual character / Spain
    Ans: finest work of art
  • Q: 3. It was an era when the Iberian Peninsula was glittering with progress and advancement of the Muslim civilization. In this sentence the word “glittering” is used as ________________.
    Options: simile / metaphor / personification / alliteration
    Ans: metaphor
  • Q: 4. The most consummate and accomplished structure of the Masjid is its prayer hall. By using contextual clues, the word that is closest in meaning to consummate is ________________.
    Options: faultless / complete / imperfect / skillful
    Ans: complete
  • Q: 5. After careful reading of the text “The Great Masjid of Cordoba and Iqbal” it can be concluded that the theme of the lesson is________________
    Options: the artistic beauty of the Masjid / the glory of Muslims rule in Spain / contributions of Muslims to art and architecture / Islam, present, past and future
    Ans: Islam, present, past and future

mcqs.q: After the fall of Muslims in Spain, the Masjid was converted into a cathedral. It shows that Muslims were overthrown by ________________.
mcqs.why: After the fall of Muslim rule in Spain the Masjid was converted into a cathedral in 1246, which shows that Muslims were overthrown by Christians.

mcqs.q: We can achieve ________________ again if we enkindle in ourselves the master passion (Ishq).
options: exalted state of moral and spiritual character
mcqs.why: The book key gives 'finest work of art'; the fuller answer also links Ishq to an exalted moral and spiritual character that produces such finest works of art.

mcqs.q: It was an era when the Iberian Peninsula was glittering with progress and advancement of the Muslim civilization. In this sentence the word “glittering” is used as ________________.
mcqs.why: The word 'glittering' describes progress in figurative language without 'like' or 'as', so the lesson keys it as a metaphor in this sentence.

mcqs.q: The most consummate and accomplished structure of the Masjid is its prayer hall. By using contextual clues, the word that is closest in meaning to consummate is ________________.
mcqs.why: Using the context of the most accomplished prayer hall, the book key gives 'complete' as the closest meaning of 'consummate' here.

mcqs.q: After careful reading of the text “The Great Masjid of Cordoba and Iqbal” it can be concluded that the theme of the lesson is________________
options: contributions of Muslims to art and architecture
the glory of Muslims rule in Spain
the artistic beauty of the Masjid
mcqs.why: The lesson conclusion goes beyond beauty or past glory alone and presents the theme as Islam in its present, past and future.

mcqs.q: Where did Abdur Rehman 1 import fruit trees and olive plants from?
mcqs.why: The answer states that Abdur Rehman 1 imported fruit trees and olive plants from Damascus, his former home and the capital of the Islamic state.

mcqs.q: Why did Abdur Rehman 1 import fruit trees and other plants to Cordoba?
options: To recreate in Cordoba the glory and grandeur of Damascus
To grow food only for his own palace
To replace the columns of the prayer hall
To sell fruit in the markets of Cordoba
mcqs.why: He wanted to recreate in Cordoba the glory and grandeur of Damascus, which he had left after the fall of the Umayyad Dynasty.

mcqs.q: In which year did Allama Iqbal visit the Masjid of Cordoba, according to the lesson introduction?
mcqs.why: The pre-reading answer says Iqbal visited the Masjid in 1933 and wrote his famous poem Masjid-e-Qurtuba about it.

mcqs.q: What is Ishq for Iqbal, according to the lesson?
options: The burning desire to achieve one's ideal of perfection and self-realisation through the moral teachings of Islam
The wish to travel to faraway countries
The love of luxury and an easy life
The desire to build the largest building in Spain
mcqs.why: The lesson explains Iqbal's Ishq as the burning desire to achieve perfection and self-realisation through the moral teachings of Islam, the essence of life.

mcqs.q: What was Cordoba in the age of Muslim civilisation, according to the lesson?
options: A port used only for trade in fruit
A city famous only for its farms
A small village with no learning
The intellectual and cultural centre of Europe
mcqs.why: The significance answer describes Cordoba as the intellectual and cultural centre of Europe when Muslim civilisation led the world in learning and art.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A. Use the pronunciation key in a dictionary to pronounce the following words. Also use a thesaurus to locate synonyms of the following words that are closest to the meaning of the given word in the context

  • Q: eternal
    Ans: Pronunciation: /ɪˈtɜːn(ə)l/. Closest synonym in the context (Ishq, that is eternal): everlasting, never-ending.
  • Q: perfection
    Ans: Pronunciation: /pəˈfekʃ(ə)n/. Closest synonym in the context (one's ideal of perfection): flawlessness, completeness.
  • Q: columns
    Ans: Pronunciation: /ˈkɒləmz/. Closest synonym in the context (857 columns of the prayer hall): pillars.
  • Q: profusion
    Ans: Pronunciation: /prəˈfjuːʒ(ə)n/. Closest synonym in the context (the profusion of palms): abundance, great plenty.
  • Q: exquisitely
    Ans: Pronunciation: /ɪkˈskwɪzɪtli/. Closest synonym: beautifully, delicately, in a very fine and skilful way.

Grammar A. For each of the following sentences, choose the correct type of adjectives to fill in the blank

  • Q: 1. “Can you see that plane?” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (that)?
    Options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun / indefinite adjective / demonstrative adjective / possessive adjective
    Ans: demonstrative adjective
  • Q: 2. “Did you see any person come on this road?” “No, I saw no one come here.” Which type of adjectives are the words in bold (any, no)?
    Options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun / indefinite adjective / demonstrative adjective / possessive adjective
    Ans: indefinite adjective
  • Q: 3. “Dog collars will be given to those dogs that are trained.” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (those)?
    Options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun / indefinite adjective / demonstrative adjective / possessive adjective
    Ans: demonstrative adjective
  • Q: 4. “He was asked to spot the car that crashed and he identified the red one.” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (red)?
    Options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun / indefinite adjective / demonstrative adjective / possessive adjective
    Ans: an adjective that modifies the pronoun
  • Q: 5. “The brave few fought the war.” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (brave)?
    Options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun / indefinite adjective / demonstrative adjective / possessive adjective
    Ans: an adjective that modifies the pronoun

Grammar B. Fill in the correct degree of adjective

  • Q: 1. My house is (big) ____ than yours.
    Ans: bigger
  • Q: 2. This flower is (beautiful) ____ than that one.
    Ans: more beautiful
  • Q: 3. This is the (interesting) ____ book I have ever read.
    Ans: most interesting
  • Q: 4. Non-smokers usually live (long) ____ than smokers.
    Ans: longer
  • Q: 5. Which is the (dangerous) ____ animal in the world?
    Ans: most dangerous
  • Q: 6. A holiday by the sea is (good) ____ than a holiday in the mountains.
    Ans: better
  • Q: 7. It is strange but often a cola is (expensive) ____ than a juice.
    Ans: more expensive
  • Q: 8. Who is the (rich) ____ woman on earth?
    Ans: richest
  • Q: 9. The weather this summer is even (bad) ____ than last summer.
    Ans: worse
  • Q: 10. He was the (clever) ____ thief of all.
    Ans: cleverest

Grammar C. For each of the following sentences, choose the correct order of adjectives to fill in the blank

  • Q: 1. My grandmother lives in the ________________ house on the corner.
    Options: modern, huge, beautiful and white / white, huge, beautiful and modern / huge, beautiful, modern and white / white, huge, beautiful and modern
    Ans: huge, beautiful, modern and white
  • Q: 2. The store carries an assortment of ________________ objects.
    Options: interesting new, old and antique / new, old, interesting and antique / interesting, old and new and antique / antique, interesting, old and new
    Ans: interesting new, old and antique
  • Q: 3. We went for a two-week cruise on an ________________ ocean liner.
    Options: incredible, brand-new, huge, Italian / incredible, huge, brand-new Italian / Italian incredible, brand-new, huge / huge, brand-new, Italian, incredible
    Ans: incredible, huge, brand-new Italian
  • Q: 4. I bought a pair of ________________ rain boots.
    Options: new, nice, red / nice, new, red / red, nice, new / new, red, nice
    Ans: nice, new, red
  • Q: 5. Please put the marbles into that ________________ box.
    Options: round, huge, old, red / huge, old, round, red / huge, old, red, round / red, huge, round, old
    Ans: huge, old, round, red

Grammar D. Use the nouns given in parenthesis to form adjectives

  • Q: 1. I wish I had (magic) ____ powers.
    Ans: magical
  • Q: 2. My sister is (allergy) ____ to cats.
    Ans: allergic
  • Q: 3. That bird has a (love) ____ voice.
    Ans: lovely
  • Q: 4. Akram has a (friend) ____ relationship with his customers.
    Ans: friendly
  • Q: 5. The project has been brought to a (success) ____ conclusion.
    Ans: successful

mcqs.q: “Can you see that plane?” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (that)?
options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun
mcqs.why: The word 'that' points out a particular plane, so the exercise keys it as a demonstrative adjective in this sentence.

mcqs.q: “Did you see any person come on this road?” “No, I saw no one come here.” Which type of adjectives are the words in bold (any, no)?
options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun
mcqs.why: The words 'any' and 'no' do not point to a definite person, so the exercise keys them as indefinite adjectives.

mcqs.q: “Dog collars will be given to those dogs that are trained.” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (those)?
options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun
mcqs.why: The word 'those' points out particular dogs, so the exercise keys it as a demonstrative adjective, like 'that' for a singular noun.

mcqs.q: “He was asked to spot the car that crashed and he identified the red one.” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (red)?
options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun
mcqs.why: In this exercise 'red' stands with the pronoun 'one' for the car, so the book keys it under an adjective that modifies the pronoun.

mcqs.q: “The brave few fought the war.” - Which type of adjective is the word in bold (brave)?
options: an adjective that modifies the pronoun
mcqs.why: In 'the brave few' the adjective 'brave' is grouped with 'few' in this exercise, so the book keys it as an adjective that modifies the pronoun.

mcqs.q: My grandmother lives in the ________________ house on the corner.
mcqs.why: The correct adjective order puts size and quality before age and colour: huge, beautiful, modern and white. The dump repeats one wrong order twice, so a distinct wrong order is used here to keep four different options.

mcqs.q: The store carries an assortment of ________________ objects.
options: interesting, old and new and antique
mcqs.why: The book key orders the adjectives as interesting new, old and antique for the assortment of objects in the store.

mcqs.q: We went for a two-week cruise on an ________________ ocean liner.
mcqs.why: The book key orders the adjectives as incredible, huge, brand-new Italian for the ocean liner in this sentence.

mcqs.q: I bought a pair of ________________ rain boots.
mcqs.why: The correct order is opinion, age and colour: nice, new, red rain boots, as keyed in the adjective-order exercise.

mcqs.q: Please put the marbles into that ________________ box.
mcqs.why: The correct order is size, age, shape and colour: huge, old, round, red box, as keyed in the adjective-order exercise.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct degree of adjective: 'My house is (big) ____ than yours.'
mcqs.why: The sentence compares two houses with 'than', so the comparative form 'bigger' is used, as given in the degree-of-adjective exercise.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct degree of adjective: 'This is the (interesting) ____ book I have ever read.'
mcqs.why: The sentence uses 'the' and 'I have ever read', so the superlative form 'most interesting' is correct in this exercise.

mcqs.q: Fill in the correct degree of adjective: 'A holiday by the sea is (good) ____ than a holiday in the mountains.'
mcqs.why: The comparative of 'good' is the irregular form 'better', which the exercise uses before 'than a holiday in the mountains'.

mcqs.q: Use the word in parenthesis to form an adjective: 'I wish I had (magic) ____ powers.'
mcqs.why: The noun-to-adjective exercise forms 'magical' from 'magic' to describe the noun 'powers' in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Which word is the closest synonym of 'columns' in the context of the 857 columns of the prayer hall?
mcqs.why: The vocabulary answer gives 'pillars' as the closest synonym of 'columns' in the context of the 857 columns of the prayer hall.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Paragraph in spatial order

  • Q: A. Imagine yourself to be standing in the middle of the prayer hall of the Masjid of Cordoba; now develop a paragraph in spatial order on what you see around you.
    Ans: Standing in the middle of the prayer hall, I see around me a forest of 857 columns rising on every side. From each column sprout amazing two-tiered symmetrical arches of stone and red bricks, which give a strong colour effect to the whole interior. In front of me, at the focal point of the hall, is the famous horseshoe-arched Mehrab, decorated with Kufic calligraphy in gold on blue and blue on gold. Above the Mehrab hovers a dazzling dome built of crisscrossing ribs covered with gold mosaic in a radial pattern. To my left and right the rows of columns stretch away like the palms of Syria, countless and lasting, filling me with awe at the Ishq of those who built this hall.

Writing B. Expository essay

  • Q: B. Write an expository essay showing comparison and contrast between the Masjid of Cordoba and the Badshahi Masjid.
    Ans: The Masjid of Cordoba and the Badshahi Masjid are both jewels of Islamic architecture, but they belong to different lands and ages. The Masjid of Cordoba in Spain was founded by Abdur Rehman 1 in 784 AD and completed in 976, while the Badshahi Masjid in Lahore was built by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the 1670s. Both are vast prayer spaces built to show the glory of Islam, and both use arches, domes and fine calligraphy. In contrast, Cordoba is famous for its hypostyle prayer hall of 857 columns with two-tiered arches of stone and red brick and its horseshoe-arched Mehrab, whereas Badshahi Masjid is famous for its huge open courtyard, its three marble domes and its red sandstone building decorated with white marble. Another contrast is their fate: after the fall of Muslim Spain, Cordoba was converted into a cathedral in 1246, while Badshahi Masjid is still a living masjid where thousands pray. In short, Cordoba shows the art of early Muslim Spain and inspired Iqbal's Masjid-e-Qurtuba, while Badshahi Masjid shows the grandeur of Mughal India; both remind Muslims of a glorious past.

mcqs.q: How many columns does the spatial-order paragraph describe in the prayer hall of the Masjid of Cordoba?
mcqs.why: The model paragraph describes a forest of 857 columns rising on every side of the prayer hall of the Masjid of Cordoba.

mcqs.q: What sprout from each column in the prayer hall, according to the model paragraph?
options: Two-tiered symmetrical arches of stone and red bricks
Three marble domes with white decoration
Rows of palms growing inside the hall
Single wooden arches painted blue and gold
mcqs.why: The paragraph says that from each column sprout amazing two-tiered symmetrical arches of stone and red bricks.

mcqs.q: What stands at the focal point of the prayer hall in the model paragraph?
mcqs.why: Standing in the middle of the hall, the writer sees the famous horseshoe-arched Mehrab at the focal point in front of him.

mcqs.q: How is the Mehrab decorated, according to the model paragraph?
options: With Kufic calligraphy in gold on blue and blue on gold
With gold mosaic in a radial pattern only
With red sandstone and white marble
With pictures of fruit trees and olives
mcqs.why: The paragraph describes the Mehrab as decorated with Kufic calligraphy in gold on blue and blue on gold.

mcqs.q: What hovers above the Mehrab, according to the model paragraph?
options: A two-tiered arch of stone and red brick
A row of 857 columns stretching away
A huge open courtyard with three domes
A dazzling dome built of crisscrossing ribs covered with gold mosaic in a radial pattern
mcqs.why: Above the Mehrab hovers a dazzling dome built of crisscrossing ribs covered with gold mosaic in a radial pattern.

mcqs.q: When was the Masjid of Cordoba founded and completed, according to the expository essay?
options: Founded in 1246 and converted the same year
Visited by Iqbal in 1933 and rebuilt then
Built by Aurangzeb in the 1670s in Lahore
Founded by Abdur Rehman 1 in 784 AD and completed in 976
mcqs.why: The comparison essay states that the Masjid of Cordoba was founded by Abdur Rehman 1 in 784 AD and completed in 976.

mcqs.q: Who built the Badshahi Masjid and when, according to the expository essay?
options: The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the 1670s
mcqs.why: The essay contrasts Cordoba with the Badshahi Masjid in Lahore, built by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the 1670s.

mcqs.q: What is the Badshahi Masjid famous for, according to the expository essay?
options: Its huge open courtyard, its three marble domes and its red sandstone decorated with white marble
Its conversion into a cathedral in 1246
Its two-tiered arches of stone and red brick
mcqs.why: The essay says Badshahi Masjid is famous for its huge open courtyard, three marble domes and red sandstone building with white marble.

mcqs.q: What contrast in fate does the expository essay make between the two masjids?
options: Cordoba is still a living masjid, while Badshahi was converted into a cathedral
Cordoba was converted into a cathedral in 1246, while Badshahi Masjid is still a living masjid
Both were converted into cathedrals in 1246
Both were built by the same emperor in Spain
mcqs.why: The essay contrasts their fate: Cordoba became a cathedral in 1246 after the fall of Muslim Spain, while Badshahi Masjid is still a living masjid.

mcqs.q: What kind of essay is Writing B?
options: A paragraph in spatial order describing the prayer hall
A poem about the Masjid written by Iqbal
An expository essay showing comparison and contrast between the Masjid of Cordoba and the Badshahi Masjid
A group discussion on the downfall of Muslim Spain
mcqs.why: Writing B explicitly asks for an expository essay showing comparison and contrast between the Masjid of Cordoba and the Badshahi Masjid.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking

  • Q: Arrange a group discussion on the causes of the downfall of Muslim rule in Spain.
    Ans: Model discussion points: Muslim rule in Spain fell mainly because the rulers lost the Ishq, unity and sincere struggle that had built their civilisation. After the early glory of Cordoba, the state broke into small rival kingdoms that fought one another instead of uniting against their enemies. Luxury, ease and neglect of learning weakened them, while Christian kingdoms grew united and strong. The lesson itself shows the result: after the fall of the Muslims in Spain, the great Masjid was converted into a cathedral in 1246 A.D. So the main causes were disunity, internal quarrels, love of luxury, and loss of faith, knowledge and the master passion.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
A. Choose the correct kind of noun for the underlined words in each sentence

  • Q: 1. The cat drank the milk from the saucer. (Underlined: cat, milk, saucer)
    Options: abstract, common, common / proper, common, common / common, uncountable, common / common, compound, common
    Ans: common, uncountable, common
  • Q: 2. Lubna loves to climb a mountain every Sunday. (Underlined: Lubna, mountain, Sunday)
    Options: proper, common, collective / collective, common, proper / abstract, common, proper / proper, common, proper
    Ans: proper, common, proper
  • Q: 3. The history of the city is recorded in a book. (Underlined: history, city, book)
    Options: abstract, abstract, abstract / abstract, proper, abstract / common, collective, abstract / abstract, common, common
    Ans: abstract, common, common
  • Q: 4. His wealth is the envy of his friends. (Underlined: wealth, envy, friends)
    Options: collective, abstract, collective / abstract, abstract, plural / abstract, concrete, collective / proper, abstract, countable
    Ans: abstract, abstract, plural
  • Q: 5. My family is going to Lahore by train next month. (Underlined: family, Lahore, train)
    Options: collective, proper, common / collective, common, abstract / common, collective, abstract / common, proper, abstract
    Ans: collective, proper, common

B. Circle the noun phrase in each sentence given below

  • Q: 1. Has anyone seen the little green parrot?
    Ans: Noun phrase: the little green parrot.
  • Q: 2. The football coach got very upset with his team.
    Ans: Noun phrase: The football coach (the subject noun phrase; 'his team' is also a noun phrase).
  • Q: 3. She is my favorite English teacher.
    Ans: Noun phrase: my favorite English teacher.
  • Q: 4. The kids were surprised by the summer rain.
    Ans: Noun phrase: the summer rain (the subject noun phrase is 'The kids').
  • Q: 5. I live in a good, family home.
    Ans: Noun phrase: a good, family home.

C. Complete the following exercise with the articles a / an or the. Put “x” where no article is needed

  • Q: My mother is ____ English teacher.
    Ans: an
  • Q: I am ____ student.
    Ans: a
  • Q: When I get home from school, I watch ____ programs on TV.
    Ans: x
  • Q: That's ____ best part of my day.
    Ans: the
  • Q: ____ programs I watch are for ____ children. (first blank)
    Ans: The
  • Q: The programs I watch are for ____ children. (second blank)
    Ans: x
  • Q: I am ____ child, so I think they are funny.
    Ans: a
  • Q: I'm ____ little excited because it's ____ Friday. (first blank)
    Ans: a
  • Q: I'm a little excited because it's ____ Friday. (second blank)
    Ans: x
  • Q: There are ____ lot of good shows on TV today.
    Ans: a
  • Q: ____ one I usually watch is at 3:30.
    Ans: The
  • Q: It's about ____ animals.
    Ans: x
  • Q: Also, I'm excited today because my mother is making ____ rice for dinner.
    Ans: x
  • Q: Later, after eating dinner and doing my homework, I go to my room and read ____ book for 30 minutes.
    Ans: a
  • Q: Then I turn off ____ light and go to ____ bed. (first blank)
    Ans: the
  • Q: Then I turn off the light and go to ____ bed. (second blank)
    Ans: x

D. Read the following letter from Beenish to her friend Sameena. For each space, put a relative pronoun: whose, where, when, who, which, that. Write 0 (Zero) in the blank space where no relative pronoun is used. Write 'that' where both 'which' and 'that' can be used

  • Q: Dear Sameena, In your last letter, you asked me to tell you about all the things I did during my summer vacation. We went to Narran ____ I have some old friends.
    Ans: where
  • Q: We went to Narran where I have some old friends ____ I haven't seen for about three years.
    Ans: 0
  • Q: My friend Tina, ____ mother I wrote about in my last letter to you, came with me and we had a great time.
    Ans: whose
  • Q: We drove to Narran on Monday 24th, ____ was also my birthday.
    Ans: which
  • Q: The first thing we did was to visit the wonderful Lake Saif-ul-Malook ____, on the jeep that we hired.
    Ans: 0
  • Q: The first thing we did was to visit the wonderful Lake Saif-ul-Malook, on the jeep ____ we hired.
    Ans: that
  • Q: We arrived in the late afternoon ____.
    Ans: 0
  • Q: The following day, ____ was cloudy and rainy unfortunately, we went to Babusar top.
    Ans: which
  • Q: The following day, which was cloudy and rainy unfortunately, we went to Babusar top ____.
    Ans: 0
  • Q: The next time ____ you write to me, you must tell me about your last vacation.
    Ans: when

E. Insert the pronoun that agrees in number with its antecedents

  • Q: 1. Of all the subjects Asif liked, English was ____ favorite.
    Ans: his
  • Q: 2. Haneef bought me a story book for my birthday. I can't wait to open ____ and start reading!
    Ans: it
  • Q: 3. Kangaroos, koalas, and possums all have something in common, ____ are marsupials.
    Ans: they
  • Q: 4. The flight attendant instructed all passengers to keep the seatbelts fastened across ____ laps while seated.
    Ans: their
  • Q: 5. Both Ryan and Sabrina love watching a good car race; ____ find it thrilling.
    Ans: they

F. Insert indefinite pronouns: some-, any-, no-, every- in the sentences below

  • Q: 1. Would you like ____ to eat?
    Ans: something
  • Q: 2. It was really dark and I couldn't see ____.
    Ans: anything
  • Q: 3. Does ____ live in that house?
    Ans: anyone
  • Q: 4. It doesn't matter where we go. We can go ____ we want to.
    Ans: anywhere
  • Q: 5. This is boring. There's ____ to do.
    Ans: nothing

G. State whether the verbs in the following sentences are transitive or intransitive. Name the object of each transitive verb, and the complement of each verb of incomplete predication

  • Q: 1. The sun rises in the east.
    Ans: Intransitive. The verb 'rises' has no object; 'in the east' only tells where.
  • Q: 2. The dog barks.
    Ans: Intransitive. The verb 'barks' has no object.
  • Q: 3. He raised his hands.
    Ans: Transitive. The verb 'raised' has the object 'his hands'.
  • Q: 4. The information proved false.
    Ans: Verb of incomplete predication (linking verb). Its complement is 'false', which completes the sense and describes 'the information'.
  • Q: 5. The child has fallen asleep.
    Ans: Intransitive. The verb 'has fallen' has no object; 'asleep' states the condition of the child.

H. Choose the correct participle (present / past) from the parenthesis

  • Q: 1. I am so ____ (relaxed / relaxing) that I don't want to move.
    Ans: relaxed
  • Q: 2. I find horror films really ____ (frightened / frightening) and not at all fun to watch.
    Ans: frightening
  • Q: 3. Sometimes I get really ____ (frustrated / frustrating) when I can't express myself well in English.
    Ans: frustrated
  • Q: 4. We were stopped by a man with a knife who took our money. It was ____ (terrified / terrifying).
    Ans: terrifying
  • Q: 5. The programme was really ____ (interested / interesting).
    Ans: interesting

I. Underline the main clause and encircle the subordinate clause or clauses in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. Jameel spoke as though he were a born orator.
    Ans: Main clause: Jameel spoke. Subordinate clause: as though he were a born orator.
  • Q: 2. When at last he returned to the village, the people told him that his mother had died.
    Ans: Main clause: the people told him. Subordinate clauses: When at last he returned to the village; that his mother had died.
  • Q: 3. The newspaper will tell us tomorrow what the world does today.
    Ans: Main clause: The newspaper will tell us tomorrow. Subordinate clause: what the world does today.
  • Q: 4. The few books that were produced in the Middle Ages were written by hand.
    Ans: Main clause: The few books were written by hand. Subordinate clause: that were produced in the Middle Ages.
  • Q: 5. When the world was young, artists drew their pictures on stone.
    Ans: Main clause: artists drew their pictures on stone. Subordinate clause: When the world was young.

J. Choose the correct tense for each sentence

  • Q: 1. After Javeria ____ her degree, she intends to work in an office.
    Options: will finish / will have finished / finished / is finishing
    Ans: will have finished
  • Q: 2. Laila looked down to discover a snake. When she saw it she ____.
    Options: screamed / was screaming / had screamed / screams
    Ans: screamed
  • Q: 3. I borrowed four books on gardening the last time I ____ to the library.
    Options: go / went / had gone / have gone
    Ans: went
  • Q: 4. By the time I go to bed tonight I ____ my work for the day.
    Options: will finish / have finished / will have finished / finish
    Ans: will have finished
  • Q: 5. Until you learn how to take a break, you ____ your ability to speak English.
    Options: haven't improved / aren't improving / don't improve / won't improve
    Ans: won't improve

K. Make the past perfect continuous tense

  • Q: 1. I ____ (work) all day, so I didn't want to go out.
    Ans: had been working
  • Q: 2. She ____ (sleep) for ten hours when I woke her.
    Ans: had been sleeping
  • Q: 3. They ____ (live) in Beijing for three years when he lost his job.
    Ans: had been living
  • Q: 4. When we met, you ____ (work) at that company for six months.
    Ans: had been working
  • Q: 5. We ____ (eat) all day, so we felt a bit ill.
    Ans: had been eating

mcqs.q: The cat drank the milk from the saucer. (Underlined: cat, milk, saucer)
mcqs.why: In this sentence 'cat' and 'saucer' are common nouns while 'milk' is an uncountable noun, as keyed in the noun exercise.

mcqs.q: Lubna loves to climb a mountain every Sunday. (Underlined: Lubna, mountain, Sunday)
mcqs.why: Lubna and Sunday are names, so they are proper nouns, while mountain is a common noun, as keyed in the exercise.

mcqs.q: The history of the city is recorded in a book. (Underlined: history, city, book)
mcqs.why: History cannot be touched, so it is abstract, while city and book are common nouns in this sentence, as keyed in the exercise.

mcqs.q: His wealth is the envy of his friends. (Underlined: wealth, envy, friends)
mcqs.why: Wealth and envy are abstract nouns, while friends is a plural noun in this sentence, as keyed in the noun exercise.

mcqs.q: My family is going to Lahore by train next month. (Underlined: family, Lahore, train)
mcqs.why: Family names a group, so it is collective, Lahore is a proper noun, and train is a common noun, as keyed in the exercise.

mcqs.q: After Javeria ____ her degree, she intends to work in an office.
mcqs.why: The degree will be completed before the future intention, so the future perfect 'will have finished' is keyed for this sentence.

mcqs.q: Laila looked down to discover a snake. When she saw it she ____.
mcqs.why: Seeing the snake and screaming are both completed past actions in sequence, so the simple past 'screamed' is keyed here.

mcqs.q: I borrowed four books on gardening the last time I ____ to the library.
mcqs.why: The borrowing happened at a finished past time, 'the last time', so the simple past 'went' is keyed for this sentence.

mcqs.q: By the time I go to bed tonight I ____ my work for the day.
mcqs.why: The work will be completed by a future time, bedtime tonight, so the future perfect 'will have finished' is keyed here.

mcqs.q: Until you learn how to take a break, you ____ your ability to speak English.
mcqs.why: The improvement depends on a future condition introduced by 'until', so the keyed answer is the future negative 'won't improve'.

mcqs.q: Complete with the correct article: 'My mother is ____ English teacher.'
mcqs.why: The article exercise uses 'an' before 'English teacher' because 'English' begins with a vowel sound in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Complete with the correct relative pronoun: 'We went to Narran ____ I have some old friends.'
mcqs.why: The letter exercise uses 'where' for the place Narran, where Beenish has some old friends from her vacation.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct participle: 'I find horror films really ____ (frightened / frightening) and not at all fun to watch.'
mcqs.why: The films cause the feeling, so the present participle 'frightening' is correct, while 'frightened' describes the person who feels it.

mcqs.q: Make the past perfect continuous tense: 'I ____ (work) all day, so I didn't want to go out.'
mcqs.why: The past perfect continuous exercise forms 'had been working' for an action continuing up to a past result, not wanting to go out.

mcqs.q: In 'He raised his hands,' what kind of verb is 'raised'?
options: A linking verb with the complement 'false'
mcqs.why: The verb exercise states that 'raised' is transitive because it has the object 'his hands', unlike 'rises' or 'barks' which have no object.

chapters.title: Unit 6: In Spite of War (By Angela Morgan)

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the pictures and predict the theme of the poem.
    Ans: The pictures show a green tree and the earth held in hands, signs of living nature. The poem's theme is that life, hope and the beauty of nature go on in spite of war, death and suffering: flowers bloom, birds and waves sing, and the human spirit still laughs and praises life.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. What are the things that thrive despite the ravages of war?
    Ans: Despite war, death and hate, nature and life thrive: lilacs bloom at the gate, tulips trip down the path, the morning-glory and daisy speak, pansies lift their eyes, clouds romp with the sea, and roses are born and gardens bloom though guns roar and cannons boom. The poet's own spirit also thrives, laughing, singing and praising with all her breath.
  • Q: 2. What are some of the different words and images used in the poem that convey the emotion of loss?
    Ans: Loss is conveyed by the dark war words repeated in the refrains: 'war', 'death', 'all man's sufferings', 'hate', 'wrath', 'despair', 'shame' and 'nightmare'. The sounds of war, 'guns may roar and cannon boom', also create an image of destruction and loss against which the flowers and songs stand out.
  • Q: 3. In the poem “In Spite of War”, there are several examples of personification. Identify two examples of personification: explain what is being personified and how in each example.
    Ans: First, the morning-glory is personified: the flower is made to speak like a human being and say 'Courage!' Second, the daisy is personified: it 'murmureth' the human message 'Rejoice!' like a person whispering. In the same way the pansies 'lift their eyes' to the poet, as if they were people looking up at her.
  • Q: 4. Make a list of the words that tell you about the tone of the poem 'In spite of War' and explain how those words tell us what the tone is. Use examples from the poem to back up your reasoning.
    Ans: Words such as 'laughs and sings', 'praise', 'Courage!', 'Rejoice!', 'divine', 'glory', 'ecstasy', 'blooming' and 'roses are born' tell us the tone is joyful, hopeful and optimistic. Although the poem names war, death and despair, these bright words dominate, for example 'Something within me laughs and sings' and 'life is naught but ecstasy', so the poet sounds triumphant rather than sad.
  • Q: 5. What is the theme of the poem 'In spite of War'?
    Ans: The theme is that life, hope and natural beauty are stronger than war and death. In spite of war, hate, wrath and man's sufferings, flowers bloom, gardens grow and the human spirit keeps its flame alight. The poem teaches us to wake from the nightmare of despair and see that, everywhere, a glory lives through despair.

Comprehension B. Choose the correct option

  • Q: 1. According to Angela Morgan, despite death and destruction of war life springs in the form of ___________
    Options: natural beauty / social beauty / cultural beauty / artistic beauty
    Ans: natural beauty
  • Q: 2. “When pansies lift their eyes to mine”: in this line the poet has used the poetic device of ___________
    Options: simile. / metaphor / personification / alliteration
    Ans: personification
  • Q: 3. The words boom, roar, murmurth and whispering breath is the example of ___________
    Options: simile / metaphor / rhymes / onomatopoeia
    Ans: onomatopoeia
  • Q: 4. According to the poet Angela Morgan, life is the name of ___________
    Options: sufferings and despair / hate and wrath / nightmare and shame / ecstasy and elation
    Ans: ecstasy and elation
  • Q: 5. The tone of the poem is ___________
    Options: optimistic / pessimistic / ecstatic / gloomy
    Ans: optimistic

mcqs.q: According to Angela Morgan, despite death and destruction of war life springs in the form of ___________
mcqs.why: The poem shows life springing again through flowers, gardens and other forms of natural beauty despite war.

mcqs.q: “When pansies lift their eyes to mine”: in this line the poet has used the poetic device of ___________
mcqs.why: The pansies are given the human action of lifting their eyes to look at the poet, which is personification.

mcqs.q: The words boom, roar, murmurth and whispering breath is the example of ___________
mcqs.why: Words such as boom, roar and murmur imitate the sounds they describe, so they are examples of onomatopoeia.

mcqs.q: According to the poet Angela Morgan, life is the name of ___________
mcqs.why: The poet declares that life is nothing but ecstasy, so she presents life as ecstasy and joyful elation.

mcqs.q: The tone of the poem is ___________
mcqs.why: Bright words such as laughs, sings, praise and Rejoice dominate the poem, making its tone optimistic and hopeful.

mcqs.q: What thrives in the poem despite the ravages of war?
options: Only the poet's sorrow and despair
Lilacs, tulips, roses and gardens in bloom
Cities destroyed by hate and wrath
mcqs.why: The solved answers list lilacs, tulips, roses and gardens blooming even though guns roar and cannons boom.

mcqs.q: What does the morning-glory say in the poem?
mcqs.why: The morning-glory is personified as speaking to the poet and giving her the human message 'Courage!'.

mcqs.q: What does the daisy murmur in the poem?
mcqs.why: The daisy is personified as murmuring 'Rejoice!', urging the poet to be joyful rather than despairing.

mcqs.q: Which set of words conveys loss and destruction in the poem?
options: war, death, hate, wrath and despair
mcqs.why: Loss is conveyed by the dark repeated words war, death, sufferings, hate, wrath, despair, shame and nightmare.

mcqs.q: What is the theme of 'In Spite of War'?
options: Life, hope and natural beauty are stronger than war and death
War is stronger than every form of life
Nature should be feared and avoided
Despair is the only response to suffering
mcqs.why: The theme is that life, hope and natural beauty are stronger than war, because flowers bloom and the spirit keeps its flame alight.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • Q: Read the poem “In Spite of War” and make a list of words that evoke positive emotions and the others that evoke negative emotions.
    Ans: Words that evoke positive emotions: laughs, sings, praise, blooming, tripping, Courage, Rejoice, divine, glory, fair, roses, gardens bloom, flame, ecstasy, lilies, silver, morning. Words that evoke negative emotions: war, death, sufferings, hate, wrath, despair, shame, nightmare, guns roar, cannon boom.

Grammar A. Underline the adjective phrases in the following sentences

  • Q: 1. Have you ever seen an elephant with a white skin?
    Ans: Adjective phrase: with a white skin. It modifies the noun 'elephant'.
  • Q: 2. He was wearing a crown made of gold.
    Ans: Adjective phrase: made of gold. It modifies the noun 'crown'.
  • Q: 3. There I met a girl with blue eyes.
    Ans: Adjective phrase: with blue eyes. It modifies the noun 'girl'.
  • Q: 4. Wild beasts in small cages are a sorry sight.
    Ans: Adjective phrase: in small cages. It modifies the noun 'beasts'.
  • Q: 5. A man with a long beard came to see me.
    Ans: Adjective phrase: with a long beard. It modifies the noun 'man'.

Grammar B. In each of the following sentences replace the adjective in bold letters by an adjective phrase of the same meaning. The first one has been done

  • Q: 1. The King wore a golden crown.
    Ans: The King wore a crown made of gold. (given in the book)
  • Q: 2. It is a white elephant.
    Ans: It is an elephant of white colour.
  • Q: 3. He lived in a stone house.
    Ans: He lived in a house made of stone.
  • Q: 4. There was an earthen pot on the table.
    Ans: There was a pot made of earth on the table.
  • Q: 5. She wore a diamond necklace.
    Ans: She wore a necklace made of diamond.
  • Q: 6. That was a brave act.
    Ans: That was an act of bravery.

Grammar C. Underline the adjective clause in the following sentences and circle the word it modifies

  • Q: 1. I like a leader who listens to his people.
    Ans: Adjective clause: who listens to his people. It modifies the word 'leader'.
  • Q: 2. The dog which I loved dearly was hit by a truck last night.
    Ans: Adjective clause: which I loved dearly. It modifies the word 'dog'.
  • Q: 3. Rasheed is a person who takes responsibility well.
    Ans: Adjective clause: who takes responsibility well. It modifies the word 'person'.
  • Q: 4. Ghazala is the one for whom you are looking.
    Ans: Adjective clause: for whom you are looking. It modifies the word 'one'.
  • Q: 5. The shirt that you bought me doesn't fit well.
    Ans: Adjective clause: that you bought me. It modifies the word 'shirt'.

Grammar D. Combine each of the following pairs of simple sentences into one complex sentence containing an adjective clause. The first one has been done

  • Q: 1. The theft was committed last night. The police has caught the man.
    Ans: The police has caught the man who committed the theft last night. (given in the book)
  • Q: 2. You are looking upset. Can you tell me the reason?
    Ans: Can you tell me the reason why you are looking upset?
  • Q: 3. He had several plans for making money quickly. All of them have failed.
    Ans: He had several plans for making money quickly, all of which have failed.
  • Q: 4. This is the village. I was born here.
    Ans: This is the village where I was born.
  • Q: 5. You put the keys somewhere. Show me the place.
    Ans: Show me the place where you put the keys.

mcqs.q: In 'an elephant with a white skin', the adjective phrase 'with a white skin' modifies which noun?
mcqs.why: An adjective phrase qualifies the noun it follows, and here 'with a white skin' describes the elephant.

mcqs.q: In 'a crown made of gold', what does the adjective phrase 'made of gold' modify?
mcqs.why: The phrase 'made of gold' tells us what kind of crown it is, so it modifies the noun 'crown'.

mcqs.q: In 'a girl with blue eyes', the adjective phrase is:
mcqs.why: The group of words 'with blue eyes' describes the girl and works as an adjective phrase in the sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'Wild beasts in small cages are a sorry sight', the adjective phrase 'in small cages' modifies:
mcqs.why: The phrase 'in small cages' tells us where the beasts are and qualifies the noun 'beasts'.

mcqs.q: Which adjective phrase replaces the adjective in 'The King wore a golden crown' with the same meaning?
options: a crown of gold colour only
mcqs.why: The book's solved answer rewrites 'golden crown' as 'a crown made of gold', an adjective phrase of the same meaning.

mcqs.q: 'He lived in a stone house' becomes, with an adjective phrase:
options: He lived in a house of stones only
He lived in a house made of stone
He lived in a stony house
He lived in a house with stone colour
mcqs.why: The adjective 'stone' is replaced by the adjective phrase 'made of stone' after the noun 'house'.

mcqs.q: 'There was an earthen pot on the table' becomes, with an adjective phrase:
options: There was an earth pot on the table
There was a pot of earthen colour on the table
There was a pot made of earth on the table
There was a pot made on earth on the table
mcqs.why: The solved answer replaces 'earthen' with the adjective phrase 'made of earth' qualifying the pot.

mcqs.q: 'She wore a diamond necklace' becomes, with an adjective phrase:
options: She wore a necklace of diamonds colour
She wore a diamond-like necklace only
She wore a necklace wearing diamond
She wore a necklace made of diamond
mcqs.why: The adjective 'diamond' is expanded into the adjective phrase 'made of diamond' after 'necklace'.

mcqs.q: 'That was a brave act' becomes, with an adjective phrase:
options: That was an act with bravery colour
That was an act of bravery
That was an act made brave
mcqs.why: The solved answer replaces the adjective 'brave' with the adjective phrase 'of bravery' qualifying 'act'.

mcqs.q: In 'I like a leader who listens to his people', the adjective clause is:
mcqs.why: The clause 'who listens to his people' has its own subject and verb and qualifies the noun 'leader'.

mcqs.q: In 'The dog which I loved dearly was hit by a truck', which word does the adjective clause modify?
mcqs.why: The adjective clause 'which I loved dearly' gives more information about the noun 'dog'.

mcqs.q: In 'The shirt that you bought me doesn't fit well', the adjective clause is:
mcqs.why: The clause 'that you bought me' qualifies the noun 'shirt' and therefore works as an adjective clause.

mcqs.q: Combine: 'This is the village. I was born here.' Using an adjective clause:
options: This is the village which I was born
This is the village when I was born
This is the village where I was born
This is the village why I was born
mcqs.why: The two sentences combine with 'where', because the adjective clause refers to the place of birth.

mcqs.q: Combine: 'You put the keys somewhere. Show me the place.' Using an adjective clause:
options: Show me the place which you put the keys
Show me the place where you put the keys
Show me the place when you put the keys
Show me the place why you put the keys
mcqs.why: The solved combination uses 'where', since the clause tells us the place where the keys were put.

mcqs.q: In 'Ghazala is the one for whom you are looking', the adjective clause 'for whom you are looking' modifies:
mcqs.why: The clause 'for whom you are looking' qualifies the word 'one', so 'one' is the word it modifies.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Write the summary of the poem

  • Q: A. Write the summary of the poem, “In Spite of War” in your own words.
    Ans: Angela Morgan says that in spite of war, death and all man's sufferings, something within her laughs and sings and she must praise life with all her breath. In spite of hate and wrath, lilacs bloom at her gate and tulips trip down the path; the morning-glory calls 'Courage!' and the daisy murmurs 'Rejoice!' Clouds romp with the sea and flashing waves tell her that everywhere a glory lives through despair. Though guns roar and cannons boom, roses are born and gardens bloom, lilies lift their silver urns, and a whispering voice tells her to wake from the nightmare, for life is nothing but ecstasy, in spite of war and death.

Writing B. Paraphrase the following stanza

  • Q: B. Paraphrase the following stanza. “Courage!” the morning-glory saith; / “Rejoice!” the daisy murmureth, / And just to live is so divine / When pansies lift their eyes to mine.
    Ans: The morning-glory flower seems to say, 'Be brave!' and the daisy softly whispers, 'Be happy!' Life itself feels holy and wonderful when the pansies look up at me as if they were meeting my eyes. In simple words, nature encourages the poet to be courageous and joyful, and merely being alive is a divine blessing.

mcqs.q: What does the poet say she must do in spite of war, death and man's sufferings?
options: Praise life with all her breath
mcqs.why: In the summary the poet says something within her laughs and sings and she must praise life with all her breath.

mcqs.q: In the summary, what blooms at the poet's gate in spite of hate and wrath?
mcqs.why: The summary states that in spite of hate and wrath, lilacs bloom at the poet's gate and tulips trip down the path.

mcqs.q: In the summary, what do the clouds do with the sea?
mcqs.why: The summary says clouds romp with the sea and flashing waves tell her that a glory lives through despair.

mcqs.q: What are born and bloom though guns roar and cannons boom, according to the summary?
options: Roses are born and gardens bloom
mcqs.why: The summary says that though guns roar and cannons boom, roses are born and gardens bloom.
