mcqs.q: What does the whispering voice in the summary tell the poet to wake from?
mcqs.why: A whispering voice tells her to wake from the nightmare, for life is nothing but ecstasy in spite of war.

mcqs.q: In the paraphrase, what does the morning-glory seem to say?
mcqs.why: The paraphrase explains 'Courage!' as the morning-glory seeming to say 'Be brave!' to the poet.

mcqs.q: In the paraphrase, what does the daisy softly whisper?
mcqs.why: The paraphrase explains 'Rejoice!' as the daisy softly whispering 'Be happy!' to the poet.

mcqs.q: In the paraphrase, how does merely being alive feel to the poet?
mcqs.why: The paraphrase says merely being alive is a divine blessing, because life itself feels holy and wonderful.

mcqs.q: In the paraphrased stanza, why do the pansies seem human to the poet?
options: They close their eyes at night
They lift their eyes to hers as if meeting her eyes
mcqs.why: The paraphrase says the pansies look up at the poet as if they were meeting her eyes, like human beings.

mcqs.q: What is the main message of the summary of 'In Spite of War'?
options: War ends all beauty and hope
Nature encourages courage and joy despite war
Death is stronger than life itself
mcqs.why: The summary shows nature encouraging the poet to be courageous and joyful, with life continuing in spite of war and death.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking

  • Q: Create a class presentation on the topic 'Importance of Peace', and deliver in front of class.
    Ans: Model presentation: Peace is important because war brings only death, suffering, hate and despair, as the poem 'In Spite of War' shows. In peace, children study, farmers grow gardens, cities progress and families live without fear, just as flowers bloom freely in the poem. Peace lets nations spend on schools, hospitals and welfare instead of guns and cannons. Above all, peace keeps hope, love and humanity alive, so every one of us should work for peace at home, in school and in society.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the mind map and guess what the story is about. (Mind-map: Mother - patient, humble, forgiving, sacrificing, loving, supportive, empathic, considerate)
    Ans: The mind map describes a mother as patient, humble, forgiving, sacrificing, loving, supportive, empathic and considerate. The story is therefore about a mother and her selfless love and sacrifice for her child, and about how a son should love, respect and obey his aged mother.

Comprehension A. Answer the following questions

  • Q: 1. Why did the farmer decide to take her mother on the summit?
    Ans: The despotic governor of Shinano had issued a cruel proclamation ordering that all the aged people be put to death at once. No one could refuse to obey the mandate of the governor, so the poor farmer, with deep and hopeless sighs, decided to carry his aged mother to the summit of Obatsuyama, the mountain of the 'abandoning of the aged', as the kindest mode of obeying the order.
  • Q: 2. Why did the son hide her mother in the closet?
    Ans: On the mountain the mother had dropped piles of twigs to guide her son safely back home, and her unselfish love broke his heart, so he brought her back down. He hid her in the walled closet for food beneath the kitchen floor, which was covered and hidden from view, to keep her safe from the governor's cruel order and supplied her with everything she needed.
  • Q: 3. What does the phrase “with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom!” mean?
    Ans: The 'crown of snow' means the white hair of old age, and the phrase means that wisdom comes with old age and experience. The governor himself says it when he realises that the young farmer's wisdom in making a rope of ashes had really come from his aged mother.
  • Q: 4. What is the theme of “The Aged Mother”?
    Ans: The theme is the value of aged parents: a mother's unselfish love and sacrifice for her children, a child's love and reverence for his mother, and the wisdom that comes with old age. The story teaches that the aged are not a burden but a blessing, summed up in the saying, 'with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom!'
  • Q: 5. What is the climax of the story “The Aged Mother”?
    Ans: The climax comes on the summit when the son is about to leave his mother and she gives her last injunction: 'Let not thine eyes be blind, my son. Follow the path which holds the piles of twigs.' Seeing her shriveled, scratched and soiled hands, his heart breaks and he cries that he will not leave her and that together they will follow the path of twigs and together die. From this point the story turns towards the happy ending.
  • Q: 6. Why did the farmer disclose his secret?
    Ans: The governor was pleased at the youth's wit in presenting a rope of ashes but insisted on knowing where he had got his wisdom. The honest farmer felt that the truth must be told, so with deep bows he related his whole story of hiding his mother and of her solution. His honesty moved the governor to abolish the cruel law.
  • Q: 7. What are the elements of the story “The Aged Mother”?
    Ans: The elements of the story are: characters - the poor farmer, his aged widowed mother and the despotic governor of Shinano; setting - the province of Shinano in Japan, the farmer's hut at the foot of a mountain and Mount Obatsuyama; plot - the cruel proclamation, the journey up the mountain, the piles of twigs, the hiding in the closet and the rope of ashes; climax - the mother's last injunction on the summit; and theme - a mother's unselfish love and the wisdom of old age.
  • Q: 8. What is the setting of the story?
    Ans: The story is set in Shinano, a town (province) in Japan, in old, barbarous days. The farmer and his mother live in a little hut at the foot of a mountain, and the main action takes place on the long, steep and narrow road up to the high bare summit of Obatsuyama, the mountain of the 'abandoning of the aged'.
  • Q: 9. Why did the leader issue the proclamation?
    Ans: The leader of Shinano, though a warrior, had a great and cowardly shrinking from anything suggestive of failing health and strength. Because of this fear of weakness and old age, he sent out the cruel proclamation that all the aged people of the province be put to death immediately.
  • Q: 10. How does the poor youth feel about the proclamation?
    Ans: The proclamation filled the youth's heart with sorrow, because he had immense love and reverence for his aged mother. With many a deep and hopeless sighs he prepared for the kindest mode he could kill his mother with, since no one could even think of refusing to obey the governor's mandate.
  • Q: 11. How did the youth carry out the order?
    Ans: At twilight he cooked and dried a quantity of unwhitened rice, tied it in a square cloth, and swung the bundle round his neck with a gourd of cool sweet water. He lifted his helpless old mother onto his back and climbed blindly up the steep, narrow mountain paths to the summit of Obatsuyama. There he made her a soft cushion of fallen pine needles, wrapped her padded coat round her stooping shoulders and said farewell with an aching heart and tearful eyes - but her love then made him carry her back home instead.

Comprehension B. Choose the correct option

  • Q: 1. Shinano, the town where they lived, was governed by a despotic leader. In this sentence the word “despot” means that ________________.
    Options: the governor was a kind person / the governor was an intelligent man / the governor was a cruel man / the governor was a wise fellow
    Ans: the governor was a cruel man
  • Q: 2. He lifted his helpless old mother to his back and set out on his painful journey up the mountain. The journey was painful because ________________.
    Options: the farmer had the burden of his mother / the mountain was steep / the mountain was steep and he was to abandon his mother / he could face the soldiers of the king on his way
    Ans: the mountain was steep and he was to abandon his mother
  • Q: 3. The son decided to take her mother back to his hut because ________________.
    Options: the mountain was not a proper place for living / she did not want to stay there / the governor abolished the law / he was greatly moved by the pains she took to guide him back his home
    Ans: he was greatly moved by the pains she took to guide him back his home
  • Q: 4. The saying “with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom” means that ________________.
    Options: whoever wears a silver crown is wise / wisdom comes with the passage of time / the snow always falls on the wise / the king is always wise
    Ans: wisdom comes with the passage of time
  • Q: 5. His demand was that his subjects should present him with a rope of ashes. Using the contextual clue, the word subjects in this sentence means ________________.
    Options: man / citizens / they / issues
    Ans: citizens

mcqs.q: Shinano, the town where they lived, was governed by a despotic leader. In this sentence the word “despot” means that ________________.
options: the governor was a kind person
the governor was a cruel man
the governor was an intelligent man
the governor was a wise fellow
mcqs.why: A despot is a cruel ruler with unlimited power, and the governor's order to kill the aged shows his cruelty.

mcqs.q: He lifted his helpless old mother to his back and set out on his painful journey up the mountain. The journey was painful because ________________.
options: the farmer had the burden of his mother
the mountain was steep and he was to abandon his mother
he could face the soldiers of the king on his way
mcqs.why: The journey was painful both physically, because the mountain was steep, and emotionally, because he had to abandon his mother.

mcqs.q: The son decided to take her mother back to his hut because ________________.
options: the mountain was not a proper place for living
she did not want to stay there
he was greatly moved by the pains she took to guide him back his home
mcqs.why: The mother had dropped piles of twigs to guide him home, and her unselfish love greatly moved him to bring her back.

mcqs.q: The saying “with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom” means that ________________.
options: wisdom comes with the passage of time
whoever wears a silver crown is wise
the snow always falls on the wise
mcqs.why: The crown of snow is the white hair of old age, so the saying means wisdom comes with age and the passage of time.

mcqs.q: His demand was that his subjects should present him with a rope of ashes. Using the contextual clue, the word subjects in this sentence means ________________.
mcqs.why: In this context 'subjects' means the people ruled by the governor, that is, the citizens of Shinano.

mcqs.q: Why did the farmer first decide to carry his mother to the summit of Obatsuyama?
options: His mother asked him to leave her there
He wanted to find a new home for her
The mountain was a holy place for the aged
The governor ordered that all aged people be put to death
mcqs.why: The despotic governor issued a cruel proclamation ordering all aged people to be put to death at once, and no one could refuse.

mcqs.q: Where did the son hide his mother after bringing her back home?
options: In a walled closet beneath the kitchen floor
On the summit of the mountain
In a hunter's hut in the forest
In a neighbour's house in Shinano
mcqs.why: He hid her in the walled closet for food beneath the kitchen floor, covered and hidden from view, and supplied her needs.

mcqs.q: What is the climax of 'The Aged Mother'?
options: The governor demands a rope of ashes
The mother tells her son to follow the piles of twigs and he refuses to leave her
The farmer cooks unwhitened rice at twilight
The governor meditates in silence at the end
mcqs.why: The climax comes on the summit when the mother gives her last injunction about the twigs and the son cries that he will not leave her.

mcqs.q: Why did the governor issue the cruel proclamation against the aged?
options: He needed soldiers for a war
The aged people had disobeyed him
He wanted to empty the province of Shinano
He feared anything suggesting failing health and strength
mcqs.why: Though a warrior, the leader had a cowardly shrinking from anything suggestive of failing health and strength, so he ordered the aged to be killed.

mcqs.q: How did the farmer disclose his secret to the governor?
options: He refused to answer any question
He honestly related the whole story of hiding his mother and her solution
He blamed a neighbour for the idea
He presented the rope without any explanation
mcqs.why: The honest farmer told the whole story with deep bows, and his honesty moved the governor to abolish the cruel law.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary: Use dictionary to find meaning, identify part of speech through abbreviation used, and find guide and entry words for the following words

  • Q: strength
    Ans: Meaning: the quality of being strong; physical power or force. Part of speech: noun (abbreviation n.). Entry word: strength.
  • Q: reverence
    Ans: Meaning (as in the glossary): a feeling of great respect or admiration for somebody/something. Part of speech: noun (abbreviation n.). Entry word: reverence.
  • Q: comfort
    Ans: Meaning: a state of being physically relaxed and free from pain; a thing that makes life easier. Part of speech: noun and verb (abbreviations n., v.). Entry word: comfort.
  • Q: frequent
    Ans: Meaning (as in the glossary): happening or doing something often. Part of speech: adjective (abbreviation adj.). Entry word: frequent.
  • Q: humble
    Ans: Meaning: modest; not proud; low in rank. The farmer and his mother led a happy, peaceful and humble life. Part of speech: adjective (abbreviation adj.). Entry word: humble.
  • Q: barbarous
    Ans: Meaning (as in the glossary): extremely cruel and shocking. Part of speech: adjective (abbreviation adj.). Entry word: barbarous.
  • Q: hunter
    Ans: Meaning: a person or animal that hunts wild animals for food or sport; the story mentions paths made by hunters and woodcutters. Part of speech: noun (abbreviation n.). Entry word: hunter.
  • Q: twig
    Ans: Meaning (as in the glossary): a small very thin branch that grows out of a larger branch on a bush or tree. Part of speech: noun (abbreviation n.). Entry word: twig.

Grammar: Modal Verbs A. Choose the correct answer about the function of the modal verbs in following sentences

  • Q: 1. May I use your mobile phone?
    Options: to make a prediction / to express possibility / to make a semi-formal request / to express permission
    Ans: to make a semi-formal request
  • Q: 2. You mustn't walk on grass.
    Options: to make a command / for prohibition / to make a conjecture / for suggestions
    Ans: for prohibition
  • Q: 3. He should come to the meetings on time.
    Options: to convey the idea of an obligation / to make a suggestion or advice / for prohibition / to form polite questions
    Ans: to make a suggestion or advice
  • Q: 4. Can you help me with this exercise?
    Options: to show inability or impossibility / to express or inquire about willingness / to show possibility / to express permission
    Ans: to express or inquire about willingness
  • Q: 5. You needn't take your umbrella. It isn't raining.
    Options: expressing prohibition / expressing obligation / expressing lack of necessity / expressing ability
    Ans: expressing lack of necessity
  • Q: 6. Could you say it again more slowly.
    Options: to make a request / to give a suggestion / to show ability in the past / to identify a possibility
    Ans: to make a request
  • Q: 7. The weather will be hot enough to go to the beach this weekend.
    Options: to express intention / to make a prediction / for habitual behavior / to show willingness or interest
    Ans: to make a prediction
  • Q: 8. The dog would bark every time the doorbell rang.
    Options: to request permission / for preferences / for requests / to show habitual activity
    Ans: to show habitual activity
  • Q: 9. Shall I help you with your luggage?
    Options: for suggestions / for offering someone help / for asking what to do / to indicate a promise
    Ans: for offering someone help
  • Q: 10. Can you help me with this exercise?
    Options: for asking what to do / requesting someone for help / for suggestions / to indicate a promise in the future
    Ans: requesting someone for help

Grammar: Modal Verbs B. Choose the most appropriate answer to express the idea specified in parentheses

  • Q: 1. You don't look well. You ________ see a doctor. (Advice)
    Options: are to / could / need to / should
    Ans: should
  • Q: 2. ________ take a message please? (Request)
    Options: May you / Could you / Shall you / Need to
    Ans: Could you
  • Q: 3. Whose book is this? I am not sure. It ________________ be Anam's. (Possibility)
    Options: might / must / should / would
    Ans: might
  • Q: 4. She ________ have stayed home yesterday because her little son was sick. (Necessity)
    Options: could / would / must / should
    Ans: must
  • Q: 5. You ________ leave work at 3:30 today. (Permission)
    Options: can / could / might / will
    Ans: can

Grammar: Regular and Irregular Verbs - Put the verb in brackets in the correct simple past form

  • Q: Yesterday Tahir ____ (get) up at 7 o'clock.
    Ans: got
  • Q: He ____ (have) a shower.
    Ans: had
  • Q: He had a shower and ____ (put) on some clean clothes.
    Ans: put
  • Q: Then he ____ (have) breakfast.
    Ans: had
  • Q: At half past seven he ____ (go) into the bathroom.
    Ans: went
  • Q: He went into the bathroom, ____ (brush) his teeth.
    Ans: brushed
  • Q: He brushed his teeth and ____ (comb) his hair.
    Ans: combed
  • Q: After that he ____ (put) on his shoes.
    Ans: put
  • Q: After that he put on his shoes and ____ (leave) his home to go to school.
    Ans: left
  • Q: He ____ (take) the bus.
    Ans: took
  • Q: He took the bus which ____ (have) a stop in front of his home.
    Ans: had
  • Q: He ____ (get) on this bus at a quarter to eight.
    Ans: got
  • Q: He ____ (get) off the bus in front of the school.
    Ans: got
  • Q: He got off the bus in front of the school and ____ (enter) his classroom just in time.
    Ans: entered
  • Q: He ____ (listen) to various teachers from 8 a.m. to 1:35 p.m.
    Ans: listened
  • Q: Then he ____ (hurry) home.
    Ans: hurried
  • Q: He hurried home because he ____ (be) very hungry.
    Ans: was
  • Q: He ____ (eat) lunch.
    Ans: ate
  • Q: He ate lunch and ____ (do) his homework.
    Ans: did
  • Q: Later on he ____ (watch) TV.
    Ans: watched
  • Q: In the evening he ____ (have) dinner with his parents.
    Ans: had
  • Q: After that he ____ (meet) some friends in the city.
    Ans: met
  • Q: When he ____ (come) home, he washed his face.
    Ans: came
  • Q: When he came home, he ____ (wash) his face.
    Ans: washed
  • Q: He washed his face and ____ (brush) his teeth.
    Ans: brushed
  • Q: He brushed his teeth before he ____ (put) on his pyjamas.
    Ans: put
  • Q: Finally, he ____ (recite) a few Ayah of the Holy Quran in bed late at night.
    Ans: recited
  • Q: He recited a few Ayah of the Holy Quran in bed late at night until he ____ (fall) asleep.
    Ans: fell

mcqs.q: May I use your mobile phone?
mcqs.why: Here 'May I...?' is used politely to ask to use the phone, which is a semi-formal request using the modal 'may'.

mcqs.q: You mustn't walk on grass.
mcqs.why: The modal 'mustn't' tells someone that walking on the grass is not allowed, so it expresses prohibition.

mcqs.q: He should come to the meetings on time.
options: to convey the idea of an obligation
to make a suggestion or advice
mcqs.why: Here 'should' advises that coming on time is the right thing to do, so it gives a suggestion or advice.

mcqs.q: Can you help me with this exercise?
options: to express or inquire about willingness
mcqs.why: In this Grammar A item, 'Can you...?' asks whether the other person is willing and able to help with the exercise.

mcqs.q: You needn't take your umbrella. It isn't raining.
mcqs.why: The modal 'needn't' means it is not necessary to take the umbrella because it is not raining.

mcqs.q: Could you say it again more slowly.
options: to show ability in the past
mcqs.why: Here 'Could you...?' politely asks the listener to repeat something more slowly, so it makes a request.

mcqs.q: The weather will be hot enough to go to the beach this weekend.
mcqs.why: The modal 'will' is used here to say what the weather is expected to be, which is a prediction about the future.

mcqs.q: The dog would bark every time the doorbell rang.
mcqs.why: Here 'would' describes what the dog regularly did every time the bell rang, showing a habitual past activity.

mcqs.q: Shall I help you with your luggage?
mcqs.why: The speaker uses 'Shall I...?' to offer help with the luggage to the other person.

mcqs.q: Can you help me with this exercise?
options: to indicate a promise in the future
mcqs.why: In this second book item, the same sentence is keyed as requesting someone for help, asking the listener to help with the exercise.

mcqs.q: You don't look well. You ________ see a doctor. (Advice)
mcqs.why: For giving advice, 'should' is the appropriate modal: you should see a doctor when you do not look well.

mcqs.q: ________ take a message please? (Request)
mcqs.why: A polite request to take a message is made with 'Could you... please?', so 'Could you' fits the blank.

mcqs.q: Whose book is this? I am not sure. It ________________ be Anam's. (Possibility)
mcqs.why: Because the speaker is not sure, 'might' expresses the possibility that the book belongs to Anam.

mcqs.q: She ________ have stayed home yesterday because her little son was sick. (Necessity)
mcqs.why: The book keys 'must' here for necessity: her sick son made it necessary for her to stay home yesterday.

mcqs.q: You ________ leave work at 3:30 today. (Permission)
mcqs.why: For giving permission to leave work early, 'can' is used: you can leave work at 3:30 today.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing A. Write a summary of any other story that you have read about mother

  • Q: A. Write a summary of any other story that you have read about mother.
    Ans: Model summary: In a well-known story, a young boy lived with his widowed mother in a small village. The mother worked in other people's houses so that her son could study. When the boy grew up and got a good job in the city, he at first felt ashamed of his old, plain mother, but when she fell ill he realised that every success of his life was built on her sacrifices. He served her with love till her last day. Like 'The Aged Mother', the story teaches that a mother's love is unselfish and that children must respect and care for their parents in old age.

Writing B. Translate the following passage from English to Urdu

  • Q: B. Translate the following passage from English to Urdu. The trembling mother's voice full of unselfish love delivered her last injunction. “Let not thine eyes be blind, my son.” She said. “The mountain road is full of dangers. Look carefully and follow the path which holds the piles of twigs. They will guide you to the familiar path farther down”. The son surprised and looked back to the path and then to the hands of the poor old lady. They were shriveled, scratched and soiled. His heart broke within and bowed to the ground crying aloud: “oh, honorable mother, your kindness breaks my heart! I will not leave you. Together we will follow the path of twigs, and together we will die!”
    Ans: Note: this is a translation exercise; this solved book is English-only, so no translation is reproduced here.
  • Q: Analyze the last paragraph in the text to identify the theme / general subject, key idea / central thought (a statement about general subject), and supporting details.
    Ans: General subject: the governor's change of heart at the end of the story. Central thought: Shinano needs the wisdom of the aged more than the strength of youth, so the cruel law against old people is abolished. Supporting details: the governor meditates in silence, lifts his head, says gravely that he should not have forgotten the saying 'with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom!', and that very hour the cruel law is abolished and the custom drifts into the past until only legend remains.
  • Q: Discuss respect of elders / parents with reference to today's youth. Write a paragraph of at least 100 words.
    Ans: Respect of elders is the main lesson of 'The Aged Mother', but today's youth often forget it. Many young people consider old parents a burden, speak to them impatiently and leave them alone, just as the governor of Shinano valued only the strength of youth. The story shows that this attitude is wrong: the aged mother, whom the law called useless, saved her son on the mountain with her piles of twigs and saved the whole province with her wisdom about the rope of ashes. Elders carry the experience of a lifetime, and 'with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom'. Today's youth should therefore listen to their parents, serve them in old age and never abandon them, because a society that honours its elders remains wise, kind and united.
  • Q: Write down the summary of the lesson 'The Aged Mother'.
    Ans: A poor farmer in Shinano lived with his aged widowed mother. The despotic governor ordered all aged people to be put to death, so the son sadly carried his mother up Mount Obatsuyama to abandon her. On the way the mother quietly dropped piles of twigs so that her son could find his way back safely. Her unselfish love broke his heart; he brought her home and hid her in a closet under the kitchen floor. Later the governor demanded a rope of ashes, and the hidden mother taught her son to burn a twisted straw rope on flat stones on a windless night. When the governor learned the truth, he realised that wisdom comes with old age, abolished the cruel law, and the custom became only a legend.

mcqs.q: In the model summary of another story about a mother, how did the mother support her son's studies?
options: She worked in other people's houses
She sold her house in the city
She sent him to live abroad
mcqs.why: The model summary says the widowed mother worked in other people's houses so that her son could study.

mcqs.q: In that model summary, what did the son feel about his old, plain mother after getting a city job?
options: He felt proud of her at once
At first he felt ashamed of her
He felt grateful from the start
He sent her money every day
mcqs.why: The summary says that at first the son felt ashamed of his old, plain mother after he got a good job in the city.

mcqs.q: In that model summary, when did the son realise his success was built on his mother's sacrifices?
options: When he got his first salary
When he moved to the city
mcqs.why: Only when his mother fell ill did he realise that every success of his life was built on her sacrifices.

mcqs.q: What lesson do both that story and 'The Aged Mother' teach, according to the summary task?
options: Children should leave parents when they grow old
Success in a city matters more than parents
A mother's sacrifices should be forgotten quickly
A mother's love is unselfish and children must respect and care for parents in old age
mcqs.why: Both stories teach that a mother's love is unselfish and that children must respect and care for their parents in old age.

mcqs.q: According to the summary of 'The Aged Mother', what did the mother drop on the mountain road?
options: Piles of twigs to guide her son back
mcqs.why: In the summary, the mother quietly dropped piles of twigs so her son could find his way back safely.

mcqs.q: According to that summary, how did the hidden mother solve the rope-of-ashes demand?
options: She told him to buy a rope from the market
She told him to refuse the governor
She taught him to burn a twisted straw rope on flat stones on a windless night
She taught him to make a rope of wet straw
mcqs.why: The summary says the hidden mother taught her son to burn a twisted straw rope on flat stones on a windless night.

mcqs.q: What happened after the governor learned the truth, according to the summary?
options: He ordered all mothers to be hidden
He demanded another rope of ashes
He realised wisdom comes with old age and abolished the cruel law
mcqs.why: When the governor learned the truth, he realised wisdom comes with old age, abolished the cruel law, and the custom became a legend.

mcqs.q: What is the central thought identified in the analysis of the last paragraph?
options: Shinano needs the wisdom of the aged more than the strength of youth, so the cruel law is abolished
Shinano needs only the strength of youth
The governor should keep the cruel law unchanged
The farmer should be rewarded with gold
mcqs.why: The analysis gives the central thought that Shinano needs the wisdom of the aged more than the strength of youth, so the law is abolished.

mcqs.q: Which supporting detail appears in the analysis of the last paragraph?
options: The farmer climbs the mountain again at twilight
The mother cooks rice for the governor
The governor lifts his head and says he should not have forgotten 'with the crown of snow, there cometh wisdom!'
The governor sends soldiers to the hut
mcqs.why: The supporting details include the governor meditating, lifting his head and quoting the saying about the crown of snow and wisdom.

mcqs.q: According to the paragraph on respect of elders, why should today's youth honour their parents?
options: Elders carry the experience of a lifetime and bring wisdom
Elders have no experience to share
Youth are always wiser than elders
Old parents should be left alone quietly
mcqs.why: The paragraph says elders carry the experience of a lifetime, and with the crown of snow there cometh wisdom, so youth should honour them.

Listening and speaking
