mcqs.why: Hughie's kindness to the supposed beggar is repaid with ten thousand pounds, so the theme is that kindness begets kindness.

mcqs.q: 5. In Oscar Wilde's "The Model Millionaire", Alan considered the model's face his fortune because __________.
mcqs.why: Alan Trevor valued the model because his miserable, wretched expression was exactly what the painting of a beggar needed.

mcqs.q: 6. In Oscar Wilde's "The Model Millionaire", Baron Hausberg was interested in knowing about Hughie because __________.
mcqs.why: The Baron was moved by Hughie's sympathy and generosity in giving a sovereign to a man he thought was a poor beggar.

mcqs.q: What had Hughie Erskine once been before his business failed?
mcqs.why: The solved answer says Hughie had once been a successful tea merchant, but a slump in the tea trade badly affected his business.

mcqs.q: How much did Alan Trevor get for the single picture of the beggar-man?
mcqs.why: The text says Alan got two thousand guineas for the single picture of the beggar-man, which shows how highly his work was valued.

mcqs.q: What did Hughie give away to the wretched-looking beggar in Trevor's studio?
options: A cheque for ten thousand pounds
mcqs.why: Though Hughie himself had only a sovereign and some coppers, he gave the sovereign away because he thought the beggar wanted it more.

mcqs.q: What did Baron Hausberg send Hughie on the morning after the studio visit?
options: A cheque for £10,000 as a wedding present
mcqs.why: The next morning the Baron sent Hughie a cheque for ten thousand pounds as 'a wedding present from an old beggar,' making his marriage possible.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary — Find out the meaning of the following words and identify their parts of speech through abbreviations used in dictionary.

  • Q: philanthropic
    Ans: Meaning: generous and caring about other people (from the text: Trevor says Hughie's act 'reflects the highest credit on your philanthropic spirit'). Part of speech: adjective (abbreviation: adj.).
  • Q: chuckling
    Ans: Meaning: laughing quietly to oneself with amusement (the Baron 'kept chuckling to himself' after Hughie left). Part of speech: verb, present participle of 'chuckle' (abbreviation: v.).
  • Q: patched
    Ans: Meaning: repaired roughly with patches sewn on (his 'thick boots were patched and cobbled'). Part of speech: adjective / past participle of 'patch' (abbreviation: adj./v.).
  • Q: strolled
    Ans: Meaning: walked in a leisurely way (Hughie 'strolled into the cafe at about eleven o'clock'). Part of speech: verb, past tense of 'stroll' (abbreviation: v.).
  • Q: cobbled
    Ans: Meaning: repaired, especially shoes, roughly (his boots were 'patched and cobbled'). Part of speech: verb, past participle of 'cobble' (abbreviation: v.).

Grammar A. Change the following Assertive Sentences into Indirect Speech.

  • Q: 1. Boys said, "It has been raining since morning. We cannot play today."
    Ans: Boys said that it had been raining since morning and that they could not play that day.
  • Q: 2. She said to him, "I am leaving now and shall return after two hours."
    Ans: She told him that she was leaving then and would return after two hours.
  • Q: 3. The girl said to me, "My father went to the market and brought toys for me."
    Ans: The girl told me that her father had gone to the market and had brought toys for her.
  • Q: 4. Her husband said to her, "I shall not go to the office today as I am not feeling well."
    Ans: Her husband told her that he would not go to the office that day as he was not feeling well.
  • Q: 5. My father said to me, "I fear that you have caught cold again."
    Ans: My father told me that he feared that I had caught cold again.

B. Change the following Interrogative Sentences into Indirect Speech.

  • Q: 1. The doctor said to his patient, "Are you taking the medicine prescribed to you regularly?"
    Ans: The doctor asked his patient if he was taking the medicine prescribed to him regularly.
  • Q: 2. Her friend said to her, "Can you spare your book for me for a week?"
    Ans: Her friend asked her if she could spare her book for her for a week.
  • Q: 3. She said to him, "Can I do anything for you?"
    Ans: She asked him if she could do anything for him.
  • Q: 4. His mother said to him, "Will you come home in the evening in time?"
    Ans: His mother asked him if he would come home in the evening in time.
  • Q: 5. His friend said to him, "Did I not warn you against this before hand?"
    Ans: His friend asked him if he had not warned him against that beforehand.

C. Change the following Exclamatory Sentences into Indirect Speech.

  • Q: 1. The woman said, "What a beautiful child this is!"
    Ans: The woman exclaimed with joy that that was a very beautiful child.
  • Q: 2. His aunt said, "What a pleasant surprise to see you here!"
    Ans: His aunt exclaimed with joy that it was a very pleasant surprise to see him there.
  • Q: 3. Hameed said, "How unlucky I am that I cannot find out any solution!"
    Ans: Hameed exclaimed with sorrow that he was very unlucky that he could not find out any solution.
  • Q: 4. The captain said, "Bravo! Well done, boys!"
    Ans: The captain applauded the boys, saying that they had done well.
  • Q: 5. The leader said, "Alas! We have lost the game."
    Ans: The leader exclaimed with sorrow that they had lost the game.

D. Change the following imperative sentences into Indirect Speech.

  • Q: 1. The land lord said to his servant, "Go away and leave the room at once."
    Ans: The landlord ordered his servant to go away and leave the room at once.
  • Q: 2. She said to her maid servant, "Bring me a glass of water."
    Ans: She ordered her maid servant to bring her a glass of water.
  • Q: 3. The teacher said to the boys, "Do not waste your time."
    Ans: The teacher advised the boys not to waste their time.
  • Q: 4. Mother said to her son, "Work hard lest you should fail."
    Ans: Mother advised her son to work hard lest he should fail.
  • Q: 5. The doctor said to the patient, "Do not smoke."
    Ans: The doctor advised the patient not to smoke.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: Boys said, "It has been raining since morning. We cannot play today."
options: Boys said that it has been raining since morning and they cannot play today.
Boys said that it had been raining since morning and that they could not play that day.
Boys say that it had been raining since morning and they could not play that day.
Boys said that it had been raining since morning and that we could not play today.
mcqs.why: In indirect speech the present perfect becomes past perfect, cannot becomes could not, and today changes to that day.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: She said to him, "I am leaving now and shall return after two hours."
options: She told him that she is leaving now and shall return after two hours.
She told him that she was leaving then and would return after two hours.
She told him that I was leaving then and would return after two hours.
She asked him that she was leaving then and would return after two hours.
mcqs.why: Said to becomes told, am leaving becomes was leaving, now becomes then, and shall return becomes would return in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The girl said to me, "My father went to the market and brought toys for me."
options: The girl told me that her father went to the market and brought toys for her.
The girl told me that my father had gone to the market and had brought toys for me.
The girl told me that her father had gone to the market and had brought toys for her.
The girl said me that her father had gone to the market and brought toys for her.
mcqs.why: The simple past verbs went and brought shift to the past perfect, and my and me change to her to match the girl.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: My father said to me, "I fear that you have caught cold again."
options: My father told me that he feared that I had caught cold again.
My father told me that I feared that you have caught cold again.
My father asked me that he feared that I had caught cold again.
My father told me that he fears that I have caught cold again.
mcqs.why: Fear becomes feared and have caught becomes had caught when the reporting verb is in the past tense.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The doctor said to his patient, "Are you taking the medicine prescribed to you regularly?"
options: The doctor asked his patient that he was taking the medicine prescribed to him regularly.
The doctor asked his patient if he is taking the medicine prescribed to you regularly.
The doctor told his patient if he was taking the medicine prescribed to him regularly.
The doctor asked his patient if he was taking the medicine prescribed to him regularly.
mcqs.why: A yes-no question in indirect speech is joined with if, and the question order changes to statement order with backshifted tense.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: Her friend said to her, "Can you spare your book for me for a week?"
options: Her friend asked her if she could spare her book for her for a week.
Her friend asked her if you can spare your book for me for a week.
Her friend told her if she could spare her book for her for a week.
Her friend asked her that she could spare her book for her for a week.
mcqs.why: Can becomes could in indirect speech, the question is linked with if, and the pronouns change to she, her and her.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: His mother said to him, "Will you come home in the evening in time?"
options: His mother asked him if he will come home in the evening in time.
His mother asked him if he would come home in the evening in time.
His mother told him if he would come home in the evening in time.
His mother asked him that he would come home in the evening in time.
mcqs.why: Will becomes would in reported questions, and the yes-no question is connected to the reporting verb with if.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The woman said, "What a beautiful child this is!"
options: The woman exclaimed with joy that this is a very beautiful child.
The woman said that what a beautiful child that was.
The woman exclaimed with joy that that was a very beautiful child.
The woman asked that that was a very beautiful child.
mcqs.why: An exclamation of joy is reported with exclaimed with joy, this becomes that, and is becomes was in the past reporting.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: Hameed said, "How unlucky I am that I cannot find out any solution!"
options: Hameed exclaimed with sorrow that he was very unlucky that he could not find out any solution.
Hameed exclaimed with joy that he is very unlucky that he cannot find out any solution.
Hameed said that how unlucky he was that he could not find out any solution.
Hameed exclaimed with sorrow that I was very unlucky that I could not find out any solution.
mcqs.why: How unlucky expresses sorrow, so it is reported with exclaimed with sorrow, am becomes was and cannot becomes could not.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The captain said, "Bravo! Well done, boys!"
options: The captain said bravo that the boys have done well.
The captain applauded the boys, saying that they had done well.
The captain exclaimed with sorrow that they had done well.
The captain ordered the boys that they had done well.
mcqs.why: Bravo is an expression of praise, so in indirect speech the captain applauded the boys and said they had done well.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The leader said, "Alas! We have lost the game."
options: The leader exclaimed with joy that they had lost the game.
The leader said alas that we have lost the game.
The leader told that they have lost the game.
The leader exclaimed with sorrow that they had lost the game.
mcqs.why: Alas expresses sorrow, have lost becomes had lost, and we changes to they when the leader's words are reported.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The land lord said to his servant, "Go away and leave the room at once."
options: The landlord ordered his servant to go away and leave the room at once.
The landlord asked his servant that he goes away and leaves the room at once.
The landlord ordered his servant that go away and leave the room at once.
The landlord advised his servant to go away and leave the room at once tomorrow.
mcqs.why: A stern imperative to a servant is reported with ordered followed by the infinitive to go away and leave the room.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The teacher said to the boys, "Do not waste your time."
options: The teacher ordered the boys to not waste your time.
The teacher advised the boys not to waste their time.
The teacher said the boys do not waste their time.
The teacher advised the boys that they do not waste your time.
mcqs.why: A negative imperative giving guidance is reported with advised and not to waste, and your changes to their.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: Mother said to her son, "Work hard lest you should fail."
options: Mother advised her son that work hard lest you should fail.
Mother ordered her son to work hard lest he should fail yesterday.
Mother advised her son to work hard lest he should fail.
Mother told her son that he works hard lest he should fail.
mcqs.why: Mother's imperative is advice, reported with advised plus to work hard, and you changes to he in the lest clause.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech for: The doctor said to the patient, "Do not smoke."
options: The doctor advised the patient not to smoke.
The doctor ordered the patient that he does not smoke.
The doctor said the patient do not smoke.
The doctor advised the patient to not smoking.
mcqs.why: A doctor's negative imperative is advice, so it is reported as advised the patient not to smoke, using not plus the infinitive.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing — Student Book Review (fictional / story book)

  • Q: Go to library and select a story book and write its review in the pattern given above. (Student Book Review — fictional / story book: 1. Author and Title, 2. Short summary, 3. Genre of the book, 4. Additional Information, 5. Recommendation)
    Ans: Book Review — 'The Model Millionaire' by Oscar Wilde. 1. Author and Title: Oscar Wilde, the famous Irish writer known for his wit, wrote this short story; it is one of his best-known short fictional pieces. 2. Short summary: Hughie Erskine, a handsome but poor and unsuccessful young man, cannot marry Laura because her father demands that he first possess £10,000. Visiting his painter friend Alan Trevor, Hughie pities the wretched beggar modelling there and gives him his only sovereign — without knowing who the 'beggar' really is. 3. Genre: It is a short story / work of fiction with a surprise ending. 4. Additional information: (a) Favourite quotation: 'Millionaire models are rare enough; but, by Jove, model millionaires are rarer still!' — it sums up the whole story in one witty line. (b) Favourite character: Hughie, whose generosity is believable because he gives when he himself has almost nothing. (c) Author's purpose: to entertain and to teach that kindness is repaid. 5. Recommendation: I strongly recommend this story to all students; it is short, humorous and easy to read, and it leaves the lasting lesson that a generous heart is worth more than wealth.

mcqs.q: In the solved book review, who is the author of 'The Model Millionaire'?
mcqs.why: The review's Author and Title section names Oscar Wilde, the famous Irish writer known for his wit, as the author.

mcqs.q: What is the genre of 'The Model Millionaire' as given in the solved review?
options: A short story / work of fiction with a surprise ending
mcqs.why: The review's Genre section describes the book as a short story and work of fiction with a surprise ending.

mcqs.q: Which section comes FIRST in the Student Book Review pattern used in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The review pattern begins with Author and Title, followed by short summary, genre, additional information and recommendation.

mcqs.q: Which section comes LAST in the Student Book Review pattern used in the lesson?
mcqs.why: Recommendation is the fifth and final section of the review pattern, where the reviewer advises readers about the book.

mcqs.q: What is the favourite quotation quoted in the solved review?
options: Kindness begets kindness in every age
Millionaire models are rare enough; but, by Jove, model millionaires are rarer still!
He wants it more than I do
Come to me when your son has got ten thousand pounds
mcqs.why: The review quotes 'Millionaire models are rare enough; but, by Jove, model millionaires are rarer still!' because it sums up the whole story.

mcqs.q: According to the solved review, what is the author's purpose in the story?
options: To describe how paintings are sold
To entertain and to teach that kindness is repaid
To explain the tea trade of England
mcqs.why: The Additional Information section says the author's purpose is to entertain and to teach that kindness is repaid.

mcqs.q: Why is Hughie the reviewer's favourite character, according to the solved review?
options: Because he is a famous and skilful painter
Because he becomes rich very quickly
Because his generosity is believable since he gives when he himself has almost nothing
Because he refuses to marry Laura
mcqs.why: The reviewer likes Hughie because his generosity is believable: he gives away his sovereign when he himself has almost nothing.

mcqs.q: In the short summary in the solved review, why can Hughie not marry Laura at first?
options: Because Laura's father demands that he first possess £10,000
Because he does not love Laura
Because he is leaving the country
Because Alan Trevor forbids the marriage
mcqs.why: The summary explains that Laura's father, the colonel, demands that Hughie first possess ten thousand pounds before the marriage.

mcqs.q: What recommendation does the solved review give at the end?
options: Only advanced readers should try this difficult story
It strongly recommends the story to all students as short, humorous and easy to read
Students should read only the summary of the story
The story is too old to be recommended
mcqs.why: The Recommendation section strongly recommends the story to all students because it is short, humorous, easy to read and teaches generosity.

mcqs.q: What lasting lesson does the solved review say the story leaves with the reader?
options: A generous heart is worth more than wealth
A beggar should never be trusted
Money must be saved and never given away
mcqs.why: The review concludes that the story leaves the lasting lesson that a generous heart is worth more than wealth itself.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking — Expressing refusal politely

  • Q: Break students into two groups (A and B). Student from group A should ask the question, and student from group B are to politely say "no". (Expressing refusal politely)
    Ans: Model polite refusals, using the book's pattern — regret, reason, alternative: (a) To a request: 'I'd love to help you, but right now I'm really busy with my examination preparation; I might be able to do it next week.' (b) To an offer: 'I appreciate the offer, but my schedule is full at the moment; thank you for thinking of me.' (c) To an invitation: 'That sounds great, but I'm sorry I can't come that night — I have to attend a family function; please invite me next time.'

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the title of the poem and predict what the poem is about?
    Ans: The title suggests the poem will be about chance or opportunity in life — most likely about whether opportunity comes only once, and about what we should do when a chance to succeed, improve or reform ourselves comes to us. In fact the poem presents Opportunity herself speaking, saying she returns every day and urges us not to waste our lives mourning the past.

A. Answer the following questions.

  • Q: 1. Who is the speaker in the poem?
    Ans: The speaker in the poem is Opportunity herself, personified as a woman who speaks in the first person ('I'). She says, 'THEY do me wrong who say I come no more / When once I knock and fail to find you in,' and throughout the poem she defends herself and advises the reader directly.
  • Q: 2. It is a commonly held belief that opportunity knocks once at the door; but this belief is rejected outright by opportunity herself. Why?
    Ans: People commonly believe that opportunity knocks only once and never returns, but Opportunity rejects this because it is simply not true of her. She says she stands outside our door every day and bids us wake and rise to fight and win; every night she burns the records of the day and at sunrise every soul is born again. A fresh chance therefore comes with every new morning, so the 'knocks once' belief wrongs her.
  • Q: 3. What is the advice of "Opportunity" to those who have failed or lost opportunity in the past?
    Ans: Opportunity advises those who have failed not to wail or weep for precious chances passed away or for golden ages on the wane. They should turn from the blotted archives of the past, laugh at vanished joys, and face the future whose pages are white as snow. Even the deepest fallen person should say 'I can!': 'I lend my arm to all who say "I can!"' — and rise and be again a man.
  • Q: 4. What was the effect of this poem, "Opportunity" on you? Describe your response in your own words.
    Ans: The poem filled me with hope and energy. I used to think that one failure in an examination or one missed chance had closed the door for me, but the poem taught me that every sunrise is a new birth and that the past cannot bind a moment yet to come. Its lines, especially 'I lend my arm to all who say "I can!", ' encourage me to stop regretting and to start working again with confidence.
  • Q: 5. What is the key theme of the poem, "Opportunity"? Explain the various themes discussed in the poem.
    Ans: The key theme is hope and renewal: opportunity does not come once only; it returns every day, so no failure is final. The other themes developed in the poem are: forgetting the dead past instead of mourning it ('My judgments seal the dead past with its dead'); forgiveness and a fresh start for the sinner ('Sins may be forgiven'); courage and self-belief ('I lend my arm to all who say "I can!"'); and the dignity of rising again, since no outcast ever sank so deep 'but yet might rise and be again a man.'
  • Q: 6. Point out some of the poetic devices used by the poet in the poem 'Opportunity' and identify the line/lines.
    Ans: Personification is used throughout: Opportunity speaks, knocks, stands at the door and burns records, e.g. 'Each night I burn the records of the day.' Simile: 'And find the future's pages white as snow' and 'Laugh like a boy at splendors that have sped.' Repetition: 'Each night... / Each morning...' and 'Art thou a mourner? / Art thou a sinner?' Alliteration: 'righteous Retribution's blow' and 'blind and deaf and dumb.' Metaphor: 'Each morning gives thee wings to flee from hell, / Each night a star to guide thy feet to heaven,' where a new day is pictured as wings and a star.

B. Choose the correct option.

  • Q: 1. To describe opportunity, the poet has employed the technique of __________.
    Options: alliteration / simile / personification / metaphor
    Ans: personification
  • Q: 2. By using the contextual clues the words closest in meaning to the phrase 'reel from' is __________
    Options: upset about / rush from / abstain from / think over
    Ans: upset about
  • Q: 3. "Dost reel from righteous Retribution's blow?" In this line the poet has used the technique of __________.
    Options: alliteration / metaphor / personification / simile
    Ans: alliteration
  • Q: 4. "And find the future's pages white as snow". In this line the word 'snow' is used as __________
    Options: simile. / metaphor / repetition / personification
    Ans: simile.
  • Q: 5. The mood of the poem, "Opportunity" is__________
    Options: hopeful / hopeless / sorrowful / cheerful
    Ans: hopeful

mcqs.q: 1. To describe opportunity, the poet has employed the technique of __________.
mcqs.why: Opportunity is presented as a living woman who speaks, knocks and stands at the door, which is the technique of personification.

mcqs.q: 2. By using the contextual clues the words closest in meaning to the phrase 'reel from' is __________
mcqs.why: In the context of suffering Retribution's blow, to reel from something means to be upset and shaken by it.

mcqs.q: 3. "Dost reel from righteous Retribution's blow?" In this line the poet has used the technique of __________.
mcqs.why: The repeated initial r sound in righteous and Retribution's is alliteration, the repetition of the same consonant sound.

mcqs.q: 4. "And find the future's pages white as snow". In this line the word 'snow' is used as __________
mcqs.why: The future's pages are compared to snow using the word as, and a comparison made with as or like is a simile.

mcqs.q: 5. The mood of the poem, "Opportunity" is__________
mcqs.why: The poem promises a fresh chance every morning and urges the fallen to rise again, so its overall mood is hopeful.

mcqs.q: Who is the speaker in the poem 'Opportunity'?
options: The poet speaking about a stranger
Opportunity herself, personified as a woman
mcqs.why: Opportunity herself is the speaker, personified as a woman who speaks in the first person throughout the poem.

mcqs.q: According to Opportunity, how often does she stand outside our door?
mcqs.why: Opportunity says she stands outside our door every day and bids us wake and rise to fight and win, rejecting the knocks-once belief.

mcqs.q: What does Opportunity do each night, according to the poem?
options: She closes the door for ever
She writes new rules for the sinner
She burns the records of the day
She counts the chances we have lost
mcqs.why: The poem says each night Opportunity burns the records of the day, so at sunrise every soul is born again with a fresh start.

mcqs.q: What does Opportunity advise those who have failed in the past to say?
mcqs.why: Opportunity lends her arm to all who say 'I can!', advising the failed to stop weeping over the past and rise with self-belief.

mcqs.q: What is the key theme of the poem 'Opportunity'?
options: Hope and renewal, because opportunity returns every day and no failure is final
The past must be mourned for ever
Success comes only to the rich
A lost chance never matters at all
mcqs.why: The key theme is hope and renewal: opportunity does not come once only, it returns every day, so no failure is final.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary A. Look at the words in the table below, besides its surface meaning these words have been purposely used to give depth to the meaning of the poem. Consult a dictionary for its literal sense and try to find out its conceivable connotations.

  • Q: knock
    Ans: Denotative meaning: to strike a door with the knuckles to attract attention. Connotation: the arrival of a chance or call to action — Opportunity 'knocking' means a chance presenting itself and asking to be admitted.
  • Q: wake
    Ans: Denotative meaning: to stop sleeping and become conscious. Connotation: to become alert and active, to rise from laziness and despair and get ready 'to fight and win.'
  • Q: fight
    Ans: Denotative meaning: to struggle or battle against an opponent. Connotation: to struggle against difficulties, failure and one's own weaknesses in the fight of life.
  • Q: win
    Ans: Denotative meaning: to be victorious or gain a prize. Connotation: to succeed in life and overcome failure, sin and despair.
  • Q: born
    Ans: Denotative meaning: brought into life by birth. Connotation: renewed and given a completely fresh start — 'At sunrise every soul is born again,' i.e. the past is wiped clean.
  • Q: hell
    Ans: Denotative meaning: the place of punishment for the wicked after death. Connotation: a state of misery, sin and hopelessness from which each morning lets us escape.
  • Q: heaven
    Ans: Denotative meaning: the abode of God and the blessed after death. Connotation: peace, goodness and ultimate success, towards which each night gives 'a star to guide thy feet.'
  • Q: mire
    Ans: Denotative meaning: wet, sticky mud; a bog in which one can sink. Connotation: deep trouble, disgrace or sin — 'Though deep in mire' means however deep a person has fallen in life.
  • Q: rise
    Ans: Denotative meaning: to get up from a lying or sitting position. Connotation: to recover from failure and regain one's dignity — 'But yet might rise and be again a man!'

Vocabulary B. Poetic words

  • Q: B. Scan the poem, "Opportunity" for poetic words and make a list of them. Substitute these words with simple everyday words.
    Ans: Poetic (archaic) words and their simple everyday words: thee = you; thou = you; thy = your; dost = do; art = are; thee/thou forms such as 'Rouse thee' = wake yourself; hath-type forms are not used, but 'sped' = gone/passed quickly; 'wane' (on the wane) = decline; 'aghast' = shocked. Replacing them, e.g. 'Dost thou behold thy lost youth' becomes in simple words 'Do you see your lost youth?'

Grammar A. Use appropriate punctuation marks (full stop, colon, semi colon, hyphen, quotation marks and question mark) in the following sentences.

  • Q: 1. We had a great time in Peshawar the kids really enjoyed it
    Ans: We had a great time in Peshawar; the kids really enjoyed it.
  • Q: 2. Some people work best in the mornings others do better in the evenings
    Ans: Some people work best in the mornings; others do better in the evenings.
  • Q: 3. What are you doing next weekend
    Ans: What are you doing next weekend?
  • Q: 4. Mother had to go to hospital she had heart problems
    Ans: Mother had to go to hospital: she had heart problems.
  • Q: 5. It is a fine idea let us hope that it is going to work
    Ans: It is a fine idea; let us hope that it is going to work.
  • Q: 6. Sorry to disturb you could I speak to you for a moment
    Ans: Sorry to disturb you — could I speak to you for a moment?
  • Q: 7. We will be arriving on Monday morning at least I think so
    Ans: We will be arriving on Monday morning — at least I think so.
  • Q: 8. In the words of Murphy's Law Anything that can go wrong will go wrong
    Ans: In the words of Murphy's Law: "Anything that can go wrong will go wrong."

B. Place the appropriate mark (selecting from the dash, ellipses or brackets) where needed in the following sentences. Cross out any misplaced marks. If the sentence is correct as written, indicate with a "C."

  • Q: 1. "I'm excited about the party, yet."
    Ans: Corrected: "I'm excited about the party yet." (The comma before 'yet' is misplaced and is crossed out.)
  • Q: 2. "I had never met him before last night when he came to my house," Aslam explained.
    Ans: C — the sentence is correct as written; no dash, ellipses or brackets are needed.
  • Q: 3. I remember a time when everyone used to quote famous appeal, "Ask not what your country can but what you can do for your country."
    Ans: C — the sentence is correct as written; the quotation is correctly introduced and punctuated.
  • Q: 4. Tariq hesitated at first, but then he said, "well, you are welcome to stay in the guest room."
    Ans: Corrected: Tariq hesitated at first, but then he said, "Well… you are welcome to stay in the guest room." (Ellipses show his hesitation before speaking.)
  • Q: 5. All the children six sisters two half-sisters and four full sisters and two brothers were at their parents' home for the celebration.
    Ans: Corrected: All the children — six sisters (two half-sisters and four full sisters) and two brothers — were at their parents' home for the celebration. (Dashes set off the explanation and brackets enclose the further detail.)

Grammar C. Correct the paragraph

  • Q: C. Correct the paragraph by adding appropriate punctuation and capitalization. (atif is one of the most laid-back people i know he is tall and slim with black hair and he always wears a t-shirt and black jeans his jeans have holes in them and his baseball boots are scruffy too he usually sits at the back of the class and he often seems to be asleep however when the exam results are given out he always gets an "A" i don't think hes as lazy as he appears to be)
    Ans: Atif is one of the most laid-back people I know. He is tall and slim with black hair, and he always wears a t-shirt and black jeans. His jeans have holes in them, and his baseball boots are scruffy too. He usually sits at the back of the class, and he often seems to be asleep. However, when the exam results are given out, he always gets an "A". I don't think he's as lazy as he appears to be.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'We had a great time in Peshawar the kids really enjoyed it'
options: We had a great time in Peshawar: the kids really enjoyed it?
We had a great time in Peshawar; the kids really enjoyed it.
We had a great time in Peshawar the kids really enjoyed it.
We had a great time in Peshawar, the kids, really enjoyed it.
mcqs.why: A semicolon joins the two closely related independent clauses about the trip to Peshawar and the kids enjoying it.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'Some people work best in the mornings others do better in the evenings'
options: Some people work best in the mornings; others do better in the evenings.
Some people work best in the mornings others do better in the evenings?
Some people work best in the mornings: others, do better in the evenings.
Some people work best in the mornings others; do better in the evenings.
mcqs.why: The two contrasting independent clauses are joined correctly with a semicolon before others do better in the evenings.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'What are you doing next weekend'
options: What are you doing next weekend;
What are you doing next weekend:
What are you doing next weekend?
What are you doing next weekend.
mcqs.why: The sentence asks a direct question, so it must end with a question mark rather than a full stop, colon or semicolon.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'Mother had to go to hospital she had heart problems'
options: Mother had to go to hospital; she had heart problems?
Mother had to go to hospital she had heart problems.
Mother had to go to hospital, she had heart problems,
Mother had to go to hospital: she had heart problems.
mcqs.why: A colon is used here because the second clause explains the reason for the first: she had heart problems.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'It is a fine idea let us hope that it is going to work'
options: It is a fine idea; let us hope that it is going to work.
It is a fine idea let us hope that it is going to work?
It is a fine idea: let us hope, that it is going to work.
It is a fine idea let us; hope that it is going to work.
mcqs.why: A semicolon correctly separates the two independent clauses in this sentence from the punctuation exercise.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'Sorry to disturb you could I speak to you for a moment'
options: Sorry to disturb you: could I speak to you for a moment.
Sorry to disturb you — could I speak to you for a moment?
Sorry to disturb you could I speak to you for a moment.
Sorry to disturb you; could I speak to you for a moment.
mcqs.why: The solved answer uses a dash after the apology and a question mark because could I speak to you is a question.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'We will be arriving on Monday morning at least I think so'
options: We will be arriving on Monday morning: at least I think so?
We will be arriving on Monday morning at least I think so.
We will be arriving on Monday morning — at least I think so.
We will be arriving on Monday morning; at least, I think so,
mcqs.why: A dash sets off the afterthought at least I think so from the main statement about arriving on Monday morning.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: 'In the words of Murphy's Law Anything that can go wrong will go wrong'
options: In the words of Murphy's Law: "Anything that can go wrong will go wrong."
In the words of Murphy's Law Anything that can go wrong will go wrong?
In the words of Murphy's Law; Anything that can go wrong will go wrong
In the words of Murphy's Law, Anything that can go wrong, will go wrong.
mcqs.why: A colon introduces the quoted law and quotation marks enclose the exact words of Murphy's Law, with the full stop inside.

mcqs.q: In exercise B, how is the sentence '"I'm excited about the party, yet."' corrected?
options: A dash is added before yet
The comma before 'yet' is crossed out as misplaced
mcqs.why: The solved correction crosses out the comma before yet because that comma is misplaced in the sentence about the party.

mcqs.q: In exercise B, how is Tariq's sentence corrected: 'Tariq hesitated at first, but then he said, "well, you are welcome to stay in the guest room."'
options: Tariq hesitated at first, but then he said, "Well… you are welcome to stay in the guest room."
Tariq hesitated at first but then he said well you are welcome to stay in the guest room
Tariq hesitated at first, but then he said (well) you are welcome to stay in the guest room.
Tariq hesitated at first — but then he said, "well — you are welcome."
mcqs.why: Ellipses after Well show Tariq's hesitation before speaking, and Well is capitalised as the start of his spoken sentence.

mcqs.q: In exercise B, how is the sentence about all the children at their parents' home correctly punctuated?
options: All the children six sisters two half-sisters and four full sisters and two brothers were at their parents' home for the celebration.
All the children, six sisters, two half-sisters and four full sisters and two brothers, were at their parents' home.
All the children — six sisters (two half-sisters and four full sisters) and two brothers — were at their parents' home for the celebration.
All the children… six sisters [two half-sisters and four full sisters] and two brothers… were at their parents' home.
mcqs.why: Dashes set off the whole explanation and brackets enclose the further detail about the six sisters in the solved correction.

mcqs.q: In the corrected paragraph about Atif, which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: atif is one of the most laid-back people i know
Atif is one of the most laid-back people I know.
Atif is one of the most laid-back people i know.
atif is one of the most laid-back people I know
mcqs.why: The corrected paragraph capitalises Atif at the start and the pronoun I, and ends the sentence with a full stop.

mcqs.q: In the corrected paragraph, how is Atif described in the second sentence?
options: He is tall and slim with black hair, and he always wears a t-shirt and black jeans.
he is tall and slim with black hair and he always wears a t-shirt and black jeans
He is tall and slim with black hair and he always wears a t-shirt and black jeans?
He is tall and slim, with black hair; and he always wears a t-shirt, and black jeans:
mcqs.why: The corrected paragraph begins the sentence with a capital He and uses a comma before and he always wears a t-shirt.

mcqs.q: In the corrected paragraph about Atif, what result does he always get when the exam results are given out?
options: He is always absent on result day.
mcqs.why: The corrected paragraph says that when the exam results are given out, Atif always gets an A, despite seeming lazy.

mcqs.q: Which is the correctly punctuated final sentence of the corrected paragraph about Atif?
options: i don't think hes as lazy as he appears to be
I don't think he's as lazy as he appears to be.
I dont think hes as lazy as he appears to be?
I don't think he's as lazy, as he appears to be:
mcqs.why: The final sentence needs a capital I, apostrophes in don't and he's, and a full stop at the end of the paragraph.

lessons.title: Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing

  • Q: A. Write an expository paragraph on the message of the poem, "Opportunity". Explain in your writing how effective or not the message of the poem is.
    Ans: The message of 'Opportunity' is that no chance is ever the last chance. Speaking in her own voice, Opportunity denies that she knocks only once: she stands at our door every day, burns the records of the old day each night, and gives every soul a new birth at sunrise. The poem therefore tells the failed, the mourner and even the sinner to stop weeping over the past and to say 'I can!' The message is highly effective because the personification makes the advice feel personal, and the hopeful mood turns regret into courage; a reader who feels finished is told, in memorable lines, that he may 'rise and be again a man.'
  • Q: B. Paraphrase the first and last stanza of the poem 'Opportunity'.
    Ans: First stanza (paraphrase): People do me wrong when they say that I, Opportunity, never come again if once I knock and do not find you at home. In truth I stand outside your door every day and call you to wake up and rise to struggle and succeed. Last stanza (paraphrase): Even if you are sunk deep in trouble, do not wring your hands and weep. I help everyone who says 'I can!'; no disgraced outcast has ever fallen so low that he cannot rise again and become a respectable man once more.
  • Q: C. 'Opportunity is missed by most people because it is dressed in overalls and looks like work'. Develop a mind map on this quote and write a detailed persuasive essay with help of this mind map.
    Ans: Mind map (in words): Centre — 'Opportunity is missed because it looks like work.' Branches: (1) People expect opportunity to look grand and easy; (2) Real opportunity comes disguised as hard work, discipline and low beginnings; (3) Those who fear effort let it pass; (4) Those who work — like Hughie in effort and the student in study — find it; (5) Result: success belongs to workers, not waiters. Essay: Most people miss opportunity because, as the saying goes, it is dressed in overalls and looks like work. We dream of a sudden, shining chance — a lottery, a patron, a lucky break — while the real chance stands before us in the plain clothes of daily labour: the extra hour of study, the humble first job, the small business run honestly. Walter Malone's Opportunity makes the same point: she does not arrive once in splendour; she stands at the door every day and bids us 'rise to fight and win,' which is work. The student who waits for an easy paper misses her; the student who works daily meets her every morning. Opportunity also burns the records of the day each night, so yesterday's laziness need not ruin us — but only today's effort can use today's visit. Therefore we should stop looking for opportunity in grand dress and start honouring it in working dress: begin the task, however small, and opportunity will be found inside it.

mcqs.q: What is the main message of the poem 'Opportunity', as explained in the expository paragraph?
options: No chance is ever the last chance
A chance once lost is lost for ever
Only the sinner is given a new chance
Work should be avoided when possible
mcqs.why: The expository paragraph states the message plainly: no chance is ever the last chance, because Opportunity returns every day.

mcqs.q: Why is the message of the poem described as highly effective in the solved writing?
options: Because the poem is very long and difficult
Because personification makes the advice feel personal and the hopeful mood turns regret into courage
Because the poet uses only archaic words
Because it tells readers to forget reading
mcqs.why: The solved paragraph says the message is effective because personification makes the advice feel personal and hope turns regret into courage.

mcqs.q: Which paraphrase correctly gives the meaning of the FIRST stanza of the poem?
options: People do me wrong when they say I never come again; in truth I stand outside your door every day and call you to wake, rise, struggle and succeed.
Opportunity comes only once and never returns to anyone.
A mourner should weep for ever over lost youth.
Sins can never be forgiven by anyone.
mcqs.why: The solved paraphrase of the first stanza says Opportunity stands at the door every day and bids us wake and rise to fight and win.

mcqs.q: Which paraphrase correctly gives the meaning of the LAST stanza of the poem?
options: The deepest fallen person should give up all hope
Only a respectable man is helped by Opportunity
Even if you are sunk deep in trouble, do not weep; Opportunity helps everyone who says 'I can!', and the lowest outcast may rise again.
A star guides our feet only in the morning
mcqs.why: The last stanza's paraphrase says no outcast has fallen so low that he cannot rise and become a respectable man once more.

mcqs.q: What task does Writing part C ask the students to develop from the given quote?
options: A summary of the poem in one line
A mind map on the quote, and then a detailed persuasive essay with its help
mcqs.why: Part C asks students to develop a mind map on the quote about opportunity dressed in overalls and write a persuasive essay from it.

mcqs.q: What stands at the CENTRE of the mind map in the solved Writing part C?
options: The youth of Pakistan and their jobs
'Opportunity is missed because it looks like work.'
mcqs.why: The solved mind map places the idea that opportunity is missed because it looks like work at its centre, with branches around it.

mcqs.q: According to the mind map, what do people wrongly expect opportunity to look like?
mcqs.why: One branch of the mind map says people expect opportunity to look grand and easy, so they fail to recognise it in work.

mcqs.q: According to the mind map and essay, in what disguise does real opportunity usually come?
options: As a lottery and a lucky break
As a patron who gives money freely
As hard work, discipline and low beginnings
As a shining chance that needs no effort
mcqs.why: The mind map says real opportunity comes disguised as hard work, discipline and low beginnings, which is why many people miss it.

mcqs.q: According to the solved persuasive essay, who finds opportunity?
options: Those who fear effort and let it pass
Those who wait for an easy paper
Those who work, like the student who studies daily
Those who dream of a sudden shining chance only
mcqs.why: The essay argues that the student who works daily meets Opportunity every morning, while those who fear effort let her pass.

mcqs.q: What conclusion does the solved persuasive essay reach?
options: We should begin the task, however small, and opportunity will be found inside it
We should wait until opportunity wears grand dress
Success belongs to waiters, not workers
Yesterday's laziness makes all effort useless
mcqs.why: The essay concludes that we should honour opportunity in working dress: begin the task, however small, and find opportunity inside it.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Listening and speaking

  • Q: Divide the class into groups of five students each and share your ideas with the class on the opportunities of employment available to youth of Pakistan.
    Ans: Model group sharing: The main opportunities of employment available to the youth of Pakistan include government jobs through public service commissions, the armed forces and police, teaching in public and private schools, health-sector jobs, banks and private companies, the IT and freelancing sector where young people earn from home, skilled trades after technical training (electrician, technician, mechanic), agriculture and livestock work in rural areas, and self-employment through small businesses and online selling. Our group concluded that qualifications, computer skills and a willingness to work hard — the very lesson of the poem 'Opportunity' — decide who succeeds in getting these opportunities.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
A. Do as directed.

  • Q: 1. Amjad is a successful writer. (Change into negative)
    Ans: Amjad is not a successful writer.
  • Q: 2. It is raining cats and dogs. (Change into interrogative)
    Ans: Is it raining cats and dogs?
  • Q: 3. She does not eat meat or fish. (Change into affirmative)
    Ans: She eats neither meat nor fish.
  • Q: 4. It was careless of him to leave the door unlocked. (Change into exclamatory)
    Ans: How careless of him to leave the door unlocked!
  • Q: 5. My mother makes delicious cookies. (Change into negative)
    Ans: My mother does not fail to make delicious cookies.
  • Q: 6. She writes with her left hand. (Change into interrogative)
    Ans: Does she write with her left hand?
  • Q: 7. I do not have two sisters. (Change into affirmative)
    Ans: I have two sisters.
  • Q: 8. She was clever to solve the problem that way. (Change into exclamatory)
    Ans: How clever she was to solve the problem that way!

B. Choose the correct option for the following sentences.

  • Q: 1. A subject and a verb that cannot stand alone is called a __________.
    Options: simple sentence / independent clause / dependent clause / complex sentence
    Ans: dependent clause
  • Q: 2. Since we had only gone a mile from camp, we could turn back before dark.
    Options: a simple sentence / a compound sentence / a complex sentence / a dependent clause
    Ans: a complex sentence
  • Q: 3. I know you don't like him, but that doesn't matter.
    Options: a simple sentence / a compound sentence / a complex sentence / a main clause
    Ans: a compound sentence
  • Q: 4. While the dinner was being served, Sana sneaked in through the side door.
    Options: a simple sentence / an independent clause / a compound sentence / a complex sentence
    Ans: a complex sentence
  • Q: 5. Those clouds promise snow; we might get another snow day off from school.
    Options: a simple sentence / a compound sentence / a complex sentence / a phrase
    Ans: a compound sentence

C. Choose the correct option to complete the conditional sentences.

  • Q: 1. What would you __________ if you won the lottery?
    Options: do / did / was doing / was do
    Ans: do
  • Q: 2. She wouldn't be nervous if she __________ her homework.
    Options: would do / did / does / do
    Ans: did
  • Q: 3. If my grandfather __________ alive, he __________ 110 years old.
    Options: were / was / would be / were / was / will be / were / would be
    Ans: were / would be
  • Q: 4. If you printed on both sides, you __________ paper.
    Options: were saved / saved / would save / would be save
    Ans: would save
  • Q: 5. We __________ football if the weather were good.
    Options: would be able to play / would were able to play / were able to play / will be able to play
    Ans: would be able to play
  • Q: 6. If you __________ a bike you wouldn't cycle to school.
    Options: don't have / didn't have / not had / weren't have
    Ans: didn't have
  • Q: 7. The film __________ more interesting if it __________ a happy ending.
    Options: would be / has / were / would have / was / would have / would be / had
    Ans: would be / had
  • Q: 8. If my father __________ me a ticket, I __________ to the cinema.
    Options: didn't buy / wouldn't go / weren't buy / won't go / wouldn't buy / didn't go / wasn't buy / won't go
    Ans: didn't buy / wouldn't go

mcqs.q: Change into negative: 'Amjad is a successful writer.'
options: Amjad is not a successful writer.
Amjad does not a successful writer.
How successful Amjad is as a writer!
mcqs.why: The negative form given in the review exercise is Amjad is not a successful writer, formed by adding not after is.

mcqs.q: Change into exclamatory: 'It was careless of him to leave the door unlocked.'
options: Was it careless of him to leave the door unlocked?
He did not leave the door unlocked carefully.
How careless of him to leave the door unlocked!
It was not careless of him to leave the door unlocked.
mcqs.why: The exclamatory form in the exercise begins with How and ends with an exclamation mark: How careless of him to leave the door unlocked!

mcqs.q: 1. A subject and a verb that cannot stand alone is called a __________.
mcqs.why: A group with a subject and verb that cannot stand alone is a dependent clause, as given in the book's answer key.

mcqs.q: 2. Since we had only gone a mile from camp, we could turn back before dark.
mcqs.why: The sentence has an independent clause and a dependent clause beginning with Since, so it is a complex sentence.

mcqs.q: 3. I know you don't like him, but that doesn't matter.
mcqs.why: Two independent clauses are joined by the coordinating conjunction but, which makes the sentence compound.

mcqs.q: 4. While the dinner was being served, Sana sneaked in through the side door.
mcqs.why: The dependent clause beginning with While is attached to an independent clause, so the whole sentence is complex.

mcqs.q: 5. Those clouds promise snow; we might get another snow day off from school.
mcqs.why: Two independent clauses joined by a semicolon form a compound sentence, as keyed in the book's exercise.

mcqs.q: 1. What would you __________ if you won the lottery?
mcqs.why: In a second conditional question, would is followed by the base verb do: What would you do if you won the lottery?

mcqs.q: 2. She wouldn't be nervous if she __________ her homework.
mcqs.why: The if-clause of a second conditional uses the past simple, so did completes She wouldn't be nervous if she did her homework.

mcqs.q: 3. If my grandfather __________ alive, he __________ 110 years old.
mcqs.why: A second conditional about an unreal present uses were in the if-clause and would be in the main clause.

mcqs.q: 4. If you printed on both sides, you __________ paper.
mcqs.why: With printed in the if-clause, the result clause of the second conditional needs would save to complete the sentence.

mcqs.q: 5. We __________ football if the weather were good.
mcqs.why: The unreal condition were good requires would be able to play in the main clause of this second conditional sentence.

mcqs.q: 6. If you __________ a bike you wouldn't cycle to school.
mcqs.why: The main clause wouldn't cycle shows a second conditional, so the if-clause needs the past simple didn't have.

mcqs.q: 7. The film __________ more interesting if it __________ a happy ending.
mcqs.why: Would be in the main clause pairs with had in the if-clause to form a correct second conditional sentence.

mcqs.q: 8. If my father __________ me a ticket, I __________ to the cinema.
mcqs.why: Didn't buy in the if-clause and wouldn't go in the main clause make the correct second conditional pair in the key.

lessons.title: Language Focus (Continued)
lessons.notes_html:
D. Choose the correct passive voice for the following sentences.

  • Q: 1. They probably won't attend lecture tomorrow.
    Options: The lecture probably not attended by them tomorrow. / The lecture probably won't be attended by them tomorrow. / The lecture not probably attended by them tomorrow. / The lecture probably won't been attended by them tomorrow.
    Ans: The lecture probably won't be attended by them tomorrow.
  • Q: 2. He was driving a car, when accident occurred.
    Options: A car driven by him, when the accident occur. / A car was driven by him, when the accident occur. / A car was been driven by him, when the accident occurred. / A car was being driven by him, when the accident occurred.
    Ans: A car was being driven by him, when the accident occurred.
  • Q: 3. Who designed a car?
    Options: By whom a car designed? / By whom a car had designed? / By whom was a car designed? / By whom a car was being designed?
    Ans: By whom was a car designed?
  • Q: 4. They took her to the hospital yesterday.
    Options: She was taken to the hospital yesterday. / She taken to the hospital yesterday. / She had taken to the hospital yesterday. / She was took to the hospital yesterday.
    Ans: She was taken to the hospital yesterday.
  • Q: 5. People visit Murree in hot summer season.
    Options: Murree visited by people in hot summer season. / Murree is visited by people in hot summer season. / Murree has visited by people in hot summer season. / Murree is being visited by people in hot summer season.
    Ans: Murree is visited by people in hot summer season.

E. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.

  • Q: 1. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
    Options: Spain is a beautiful country; the beache's are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean. / Spain is a beautiful country: the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean. / Spain is a beautiful country, the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean. / Spain is a beautiful country the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean.
    Ans: Spain is a beautiful country: the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean.
  • Q: 2. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
    Options: The children's books were all left in the following places: Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard. / The children's books were all left in the following places; Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard. / The childrens books were all left in the following places: Mrs Faisals room, Mr Fakhors office and the caretakers cupboard / The children's books were all left in the following places, Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard.
    Ans: The children's books were all left in the following places: Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard.
  • Q: 3. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
    Options: She always enjoyed sweets; chocolate, marshmallows and toffee apples. / She always enjoyed: sweets, chocolate, marshmallows and toffee apples. / She always enjoyed sweets chocolate marshmallows and toffee apples. / She always enjoyed sweet's, chocolate, marshmallow's and toffee apple's.
    Ans: She always enjoyed: sweets, chocolate, marshmallows and toffee apples.
  • Q: 4. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
    Options: Sarah's uncle's car was found without its wheels in that old derelict warehouse. / Sarah's uncle's car was found without its wheels in that old, derelict warehouse. / Sarahs uncles car was found without its wheels in that old, derelict warehouse. / Sarah's uncle's car was found without it's wheels in that old, derelict warehouse.
    Ans: Sarah's uncle's car was found without its wheels in that old, derelict warehouse.
  • Q: 5. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
    Options: I can't see Tahir's car, there must have been an accident. / I cant see Tahir's car; there must have been an accident. / I can't see Tahir's car there must have been an accident. / I can't see Tahir's car: there must have been an accident.
    Ans: I can't see Tahir's car: there must have been an accident.

F. Change the following sentences into indirect.

  • Q: 1. Jaffar said, "I love this town." Jaffar said __________.
    Ans: Jaffar said that he loved that town.
  • Q: 2. "Do you like football?", he asked me. He asked me __________.
    Ans: He asked me if I liked football.
  • Q: 3. "I can't drive a lorry", he said. He said __________.
    Ans: He said that he couldn't drive a lorry.
  • Q: 4. "Be nice to your brother", he said. He asked me __________.
    Ans: He asked me to be nice to my brother.
  • Q: 5. "Don't be nasty", he said. He urged me __________.
    Ans: He urged me not to be nasty.

mcqs.q: 1. They probably won't attend lecture tomorrow.
options: The lecture probably not attended by them tomorrow.
The lecture probably won't be attended by them tomorrow.
The lecture not probably attended by them tomorrow.
The lecture probably won't been attended by them tomorrow.
mcqs.why: The passive of won't attend is won't be attended, keeping probably in place, as given in the book's correct option.

mcqs.q: 2. He was driving a car, when accident occurred.
options: A car driven by him, when the accident occur.
A car was driven by him, when the accident occur.
A car was been driven by him, when the accident occurred.
A car was being driven by him, when the accident occurred.
mcqs.why: Was driving is past continuous, so its passive is was being driven, with occurred kept in the past tense.

mcqs.q: 3. Who designed a car?
options: By whom was a car designed?
By whom a car had designed?
By whom a car was being designed?
mcqs.why: The passive question form is By whom was a car designed?, using was plus the past participle designed.

mcqs.q: 4. They took her to the hospital yesterday.
options: She was taken to the hospital yesterday.
She taken to the hospital yesterday.
She had taken to the hospital yesterday.
She was took to the hospital yesterday.
mcqs.why: Took is past simple, so the passive is was taken, with she as the new subject of the sentence.

mcqs.q: 5. People visit Murree in hot summer season.
options: Murree visited by people in hot summer season.
Murree has visited by people in hot summer season.
Murree is visited by people in hot summer season.
Murree is being visited by people in hot summer season.
mcqs.why: Visit is present simple, so the passive uses is visited: Murree is visited by people in hot summer season.

mcqs.q: 1. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Spain is a beautiful country; the beache's are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean.
Spain is a beautiful country, the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean.
Spain is a beautiful country: the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean.
Spain is a beautiful country the beaches are warm, sandy and spotlessly clean.
mcqs.why: The colon correctly introduces the explanation about the beaches, and beaches needs no apostrophe as a simple plural.

mcqs.q: 2. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: The children's books were all left in the following places; Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard.
The children's books were all left in the following places: Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard.
The childrens books were all left in the following places: Mrs Faisals room, Mr Fakhors office and the caretakers cupboard
The children's books were all left in the following places, Mrs Faisal's room, Mr Fakhar's office and the caretaker's cupboard.
mcqs.why: A colon introduces the list of places, and the possessive apostrophes in children's, Faisal's, Fakhar's and caretaker's are correct.

mcqs.q: 3. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: She always enjoyed sweets; chocolate, marshmallows and toffee apples.
She always enjoyed sweets chocolate marshmallows and toffee apples.
She always enjoyed: sweets, chocolate, marshmallows and toffee apples.
She always enjoyed sweet's, chocolate, marshmallow's and toffee apple's.
mcqs.why: This is the book's keyed correct option, with a colon after enjoyed and commas separating the items in the list.

mcqs.q: 4. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Sarah's uncle's car was found without its wheels in that old derelict warehouse.
Sarahs uncles car was found without its wheels in that old, derelict warehouse.
Sarah's uncle's car was found without it's wheels in that old, derelict warehouse.
Sarah's uncle's car was found without its wheels in that old, derelict warehouse.
mcqs.why: Its is the correct possessive without an apostrophe, and a comma separates the two adjectives old and derelict.

mcqs.q: 5. Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I can't see Tahir's car, there must have been an accident.
I can't see Tahir's car: there must have been an accident.
I cant see Tahir's car; there must have been an accident.
I can't see Tahir's car there must have been an accident.
mcqs.why: The book keys the colon version as correct: the second clause explains the first, and can't keeps its apostrophe.
